ActivityEmbedding.description: One embedding declared on a class of the graph.

class.description: The class IRI the embedding covers.

oneOf.description: The newest commit the serving version covers.

The newest failure of the embed job when it is newer than the
embedding's last update and the embedding is not ready and current.

lag_commits.description: Commits the serving version is behind `published_seq`.

oneOf.description:
While `backfilling`: the instances the pass visited, and the class's
instance count when one bounded read gives it.

ActivityError.description:
A tenant-safe failure: a stable code and a short message. Unknown
failures carry `job_failed`; the item id identifies the job for an
operator.

retryable.description: True when a retry can succeed without a change by the user.

oneOf.description:
The failure of a failed item, or the last failure of an item that
waits for or runs a retry (`retryable: true`).

finished_at_micros.description: Set for succeeded, failed and cancelled items.

id.description: The job id.

stage.description:
Machine stage, for example `compacting_truth`, `building`,
`publishing`, `rdf_partitions_pending`, `admission_deferred`, or the
import stage.

subject.description:
What the job works on beyond the graph: the export id, or the graph a
fork writes.

oneOf.description: The commit the job works toward, when it has one.

ActivityProgress.description: How far a job has come. `total` is absent when the job does not know it.

ActivityTest.description:
The workflow test a `reason` or `decide` call belongs to: the call log
names the route `tests/<workflow>` and the scope `test`, it counts as the
workflow's in the model activity and the budget, and calibration, the
model checks and model trials leave it out. `captureActivities` of the
TypeScript SDK sets it.

workflow.description: The workflow under test: 1 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`.

ActivityWorkflow.description:
The run of a workflow turn that an activity call belongs to
(`workflow` of `POST /v1/workflows/activities/*`). The SDKs set it from
the step context. The caller names its workflow and turn; the server
checks the shape, and counts the call under the named workflow that
owns the identity when the graph has one. It does not check that the
caller holds the turn: the work token names the graph only.

identity.description:
The engine identity whose turn makes the call (1 to 128 characters
of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`).

instance.description:
What the call works on: an instance IRI or a document's name, at
most 512 characters.

run_id.description:
The run's id (`run.id` of the claimed task's turn): it names the same
identity and turn.

step.description:
The key of the step that makes the call (`ctx.step`'s key, 1 to 128
characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`): the call log names it (`step`)
with `scope: live`. Added 2026-10-21; an older server refuses the
field.

ActivityWriteLimit.description:
The unpublished commits on the graph head against the write path's limits
on them. Past any `soft_*` limit each write waits a little (the wait grows
toward the hard limit); at any `max_*` (hard) limit a write is refused with
a retryable `429 ingest_busy` until the index catches up.

pending_bytes.description:
What the unpublished commits store for strong reads: their runs'
bytes, or the decoded text of a commit without runs.

pending_records.description: Statements the unpublished commits assert or retract.

soft_pending_commits.description: Where writes start to slow down. 0 when the server has no soft limit.

AddEntityTypeOp.description:
Declare a new entity type. Idempotent: a no-op if the name already exists.
Pair with `widen_relation` (in the same request, ordered before it) to add
a brand-new type to an existing relation's domain or range.

name.description: Display name of the new entity type.

AddPropertyOp.description:
Declare a new typed scalar property field (e.g. `status`, `dueDate`,
`budget`) so a commit's `entity_properties` can write it on a live graph.
Additive: every existing record stays valid and no migration is needed.
Unlike `define_ontology` (which recreates the graph ontology), this bumps
the ontology version and registers just the field. Idempotent — a no-op
if a field with this name already exists (the existing type is kept).

allowed_values.description:
Optional **enforced** allowed-value set (a SHACL `sh:in`): a commit
whose value for this field is outside the set is rejected at write
time, so a controlled vocabulary is a one-line declaration instead of
a separate shapes graph. Only for enumerable types
(`keyword`/`text`/`i64`/`bool`); rejected on `f64`/`date_time`/`bytes`.
Use `set_property_constraint` to tighten an existing field.

name.description:
Display name of the new property field (case-insensitive; a commit's
`entity_properties[].field` resolves to it).

required.description: Advisory required flag recorded on the field (not enforced on commit).

unit.description:
Optional unit of an `i64` or `f64` field: the symbol of a known
unit (`mm`, `cm`, `dm`, `m`, `km`, `mm2`, `cm2`, `dm2`, `m2`, `ml`,
`cl`, `dl`, `l`, `cm3`, `dm3`, `m3`, `mg`, `g`, `kg`, `t`, `w`,
`kw`, `wh`, `kwh`, `s`, `min`, `h`). Metadata: commits are not
converted. Writers that read text convert to it. Use
`set_property_unit` to change it on an existing field.

value_type.description:
`bool` | `i64` | `f64` | `date_time` | `keyword` | `text` (default) |
`bytes`. The commit path rejects values whose type doesn't match.

AddRelationOp.description:
Declare a new relation type (e.g. `HAS_PHASE`, `ASSIGNED_TO`) with its own
domain and range, by name. The named domain/range entity types must
already exist (add them earlier in the same request with `add_entity_type`
if new). Idempotent: a no-op if a relation with this name already exists —
use `widen_relation` to grow an existing relation's domain/range. Optional
fields default exactly as the ontology spec importer does.

domain.description: Entity-type names allowed as the source (domain).

name.description: Display name of the new relation.

range.description: Entity-type names allowed as the target (range).

symmetric.description: Whether the relation is symmetric (default false).

transitive.description: Whether the relation is transitive (default false).

AddSuperTypesOp.description:
Add direct parent classes to an existing entity type. All named classes
must already exist, or be declared earlier in the same request with
`add_entity_type`. Existing links are skipped, so the op is idempotent.
Removing a parent is not additive and requires an explicit migration.

entity_type.description: Entity type whose direct parents should grow.

super_types.description: Direct parent entity-type names to add.

AdditiveOntologyEvolveOp.description: Governed proposal operation restricted to additive ontology changes.

AdditiveOntologyEvolveRequest.description: Additive-only ontology proposal helper for structured-output systems.

AnalyticBinding.description: One solution: each query variable bound to a resolved entity.

AnalyticCombinator.description:
A group-graph-pattern combinator folded over an analytic query's base BGP —
the SPARQL operators beyond a plain conjunctive join. Each carries its own
basic graph pattern (the right side); combinators apply left-to-right in the
order given. Externally tagged (`{"union": [ … ]}`, `{"optional": [ … ]}`, …).

oneOf.description: `{ base } UNION { patterns }` — multiset union of the two solution sets.

union.description: `{ base } UNION { patterns }` — multiset union of the two solution sets.

oneOf.description:
`base OPTIONAL { patterns }` — left join; unmatched base rows are kept with
the optional variables unbound.

optional.description:
`base OPTIONAL { patterns }` — left join; unmatched base rows are kept with
the optional variables unbound.

oneOf.description:
`base MINUS { patterns }` — drop base rows compatible with a right solution
they share a variable with.

minus.description:
`base MINUS { patterns }` — drop base rows compatible with a right solution
they share a variable with.

oneOf.description:
`base FILTER EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with a compatible right
solution (a semijoin).

exists.description:
`base FILTER EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with a compatible right
solution (a semijoin).

oneOf.description:
`base FILTER NOT EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with no compatible
right solution.

not_exists.description:
`base FILTER NOT EXISTS { patterns }` — keep base rows with no compatible
right solution.

AnalyticQueryRequest.description:
A basic-graph-pattern query: a conjunction of triple patterns evaluated over
the graph's current edges (joined on shared variables), served from the
conformant published RDF dataset.

combinators.description:
Group-graph-pattern combinators (UNION / OPTIONAL / MINUS / EXISTS /
NOT EXISTS) folded over the base `patterns`, left-to-right. Empty (the
default) leaves the query a plain conjunctive BGP.

oneOf.description:
Read consistency (A3 serving; A5 default). `eventual` (the **default**)
serves ENTIRELY from the last published segment RDF family (the
maintenance-owned, asserted-only default) at its watermark — no in-memory
gap fold, so the query stays available while background indexing lags — and
surfaces the served watermark on `snapshot.served_at_seq`. Eventual serving
requires a published dataset; a graph with none yet returns a retryable 429.
`strong` (explicit opt-in) succeeds only when the immutable published
generation itself covers head. Otherwise it returns retryable
`strong_read_pending`; no query folds mutable WAL state.

limit.description: Cap the number of returned bindings.

max_fetched_bytes.description:
Companion byte ceiling on block bytes fetched by the query. Clamped to the
server's `MAX_ANALYTIC_FETCHED_BYTES`; also trips `truncated_by_read_budget`.

max_object_reads.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on object reads (GETs) the query's scans may issue —
the per-request object-storage cost cap. Clamped to the server's
`MAX_ANALYTIC_OBJECT_READS`; when hit, the scan stops and the response's
`truncated_by_read_budget` flag is set.

max_solutions.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on the intermediate join solution set. Clamped to the
server's `MAX_ANALYTIC_SOLUTIONS`; when the join hits it the result is
partial and the response's `truncated` flag is set. Distinct from `limit`,
which is a caller-requested cap on the final, complete result.

oneOf.description:
A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `eventual`, a floor not yet covered by the
published dataset returns a retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429 (poll
until it lands); under `strong` the floor is satisfied by construction and a
floor above head is a client error. `None` == no floor.

truncated.description:
True when a safety cap (the intermediate-solution ceiling) cut the join —
the solution set is partial. Not set by `limit`, which is caller-requested.

truncated_by_read_budget.description:
True when the per-request object-read budget (`max_object_reads` /
`max_fetched_bytes`) was hit, so scans stopped early — the result may be
incomplete.

AnalyticTerm.description:
A triple-pattern term: a named query variable (`{"var": "x"}`) or a fixed
entity (`{"entity": {...}}`).

AnalyticTriplePattern.description:
One triple pattern of an analytic (BGP) query. The predicate is a relation
name, resolved server-side. In an inference rule body the predicate may also
be the reserved [`RDF_TYPE_PREDICATE`] for a type-membership constraint.

AskStructuredQuery.description:
The constrained structured plan: the entity type the answer set is
restricted to (the QALD-class-task shape), plus — when the question admits
them — a relation and an anchor entity. Every slot is real vocabulary by
construction (decoded under the shortlist trie or forced by a type
signature, and server-verified ⊆ the shortlist either way).

target_type.description:
Decoded target entity type (a declared class, subtype-inclusive at
execution).

CalibrationServingDefaults.description:
Calibration serving default derived from a promoted `calibration` run:
the Platt scaler the retrieval-premise producer applies when a request
supplies no inline `calibration`. The scaler is fit on the BM25 entity
channel (the same channel query-driven premise requests use) from
execution-verified outcomes.

model_id.description: The retrieval channel the scaler was fitted on.

run.description: The promoted registry run this scaler came from.

snapshot_commit_seq.description:
The snapshot the scaler was fitted at (its split pin — provenance;
the producer re-pins the manifest to the served snapshot).

oneOf.description: Exactly one complete committed source transaction in this first codec.

CaptureScope.description: Immutable authorization and identity binding for a capture epoch.

CapturedSignal.description:
One captured signal as the range reader returns it: the stored envelope
plus the commit seq of the object it was flushed at (the temporal-split
coordinate trainers filter on).

last_commit_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the head commit.

expected_graph_epoch.description: Must match the existing live graph. Adoption never creates graph truth.

owner_id.description: Omit to use the implicit environment root.

CatalogIndexRepairResponse.description:
A page checks derived directories against authoritative catalog records.
Continue through empty pages until next_cursor is null.

CatalogNamespace.description: Stable ownership metadata. Paths are optional addresses, not storage keys.

parent_id.description: Omit to use the implicit environment root.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation; an empty page may still have a continuation.

CatalogPendingOperation.description:
Summary of a durable pending request. Private request fingerprints and
idempotency keys are not part of the public inventory.

complete_through_micros.description: Always null for raw historical projection.

profile.description: raw-resource-receipts-v1; never add this to registered-profile totals.

status.description: Always partial or unavailable; discovery cannot prove all traffic.

time_basis.description: execution_completion_time; pages select one UTC day.

source_evidence.description: Opaque content evidence; never an object key or native ETag.

complete_through_micros.description:
Selected interval's end when its frozen denominator is fully proven.
This is not a global or contiguous historical watermark.

page_totals.description: Totals for this page, not the entire interval. Follow every next_cursor.

profile.description: registered-request-resource-v1; excludes raw historical and other lanes.

status.description: unavailable, open, closing, partial or complete for this interval only.

time_basis.description: admission_time; late outcomes retain the original hour.

totals_scope.description: returned_owner_index_page: native inventory is not a total-completeness proof.

cpu_nanos.description: Exact unsigned integer decimal string; never a floating-point estimate.

oneOf.description: Absent on servers predating capture retention status.

CdcCaptureRetentionStatus.description: Committed capture-retention facts; eligibility is not a scheduled deletion.

eligible_after_ms.description: Earliest eligibility of the observed applied watermark, if one exists.

pending_cleanup_bytes.description: Still charged until the durable physical-cleanup plan is acknowledged.

retained_after_sequence.description: Capture batches at or below this floor no longer authorize replay.

schema.description: Exact immutable schema bytes; digest must already be in the mapping.

expected_revision.description:
Revision observed by the caller. Only a later control for this customer
invalidates it; routing, acknowledgements and other customers do not.

CdcMetadataPutRequest.description:
Operational metadata is scoped to an exact graph incarnation. The current
epoch comes from discovery/status; an old request cannot target a new graph.

schema.description: Exact immutable schema bytes; digest must already be in the mapping.

mapping.description:
Authoritative mapping, including the exact approved schema digests the
hosted supervisor passes to the pinned reader.

CdcSourceDiscoveryStatus.description: Source-scoped discovery does not require a destination graph or graph epoch.

oneOf.description:
Write-time validation outcome (roadmap item 9 M0). Present only when the
commit raised at least one warning; absent on a fully-conformant commit.
M0 reports structural domain/range mismatches in `warn` mode (never
blocks); `reject` mode and SHACL shapes arrive with the constraints work.

drain_pressure.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry: the WAL drain pressure at ack time as a
`0.0`–`1.0` tail-fill ratio. Present only once the tail is over half full.
Clients SHOULD reduce write concurrency as this rises; advisory only.

oneOf.description:
What `replace_owned` removed. Present only on a fresh commit that
carried `replace_owned`.

Active graph-schema SHACL validation outcome. Present only when the graph
has an activated schema shape set and the commit violated or warned on it.

throttle_ms.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry: the pacing latency this write ack
absorbed — head-lane serialization plus admission wait — in whole
milliseconds. Present only past a noise floor (a fast commit omits it) and
mirrored to the `X-LBB-Throttle-Ms` response header. Clients SHOULD reduce
write concurrency as this rises; it is never load-bearing for correctness.

written_properties.description:
Property fields actually written by this commit, per entity (canonical
field names, resolved against the ontology). Lets a writer confirm a
property landed without a follow-up read. Present only on a fresh commit
that carried `entity_properties`; empty on idempotent replays and no-ops.

ConformanceReport.description:
Closed-world validation report for a commit. Mirrors the shape of a SHACL
`sh:ValidationReport`: `conforms` plus one `results` entry per violation.

focus_node.description: The focus node the constraint was evaluated on (the entity name/id).

value.description: The offending value (the endpoint's entity-type name).

CurrentGraphStatus.description:
RDF and class observations from one graph incarnation. Their commit observations
may differ during concurrent writes; they are not an atomic transaction snapshot.

complete.description: All requested diagnostics were inspected, independently of readiness/lag.

CurrentStatusResponse.description:
Selected only by `version=status/1` during the pre-release compatibility phase.
`ok` confirms that this status request completed, not database/model health.

control_revision.description:
Routing revision of the last customer control, independent of data
progress. A poll's revision fences conflicting controls, not appends.

detached.description: A proved graph deletion permanently detaches this destination.

oneOf.description: Immutable paged outbox; a pause is bounded by the explicit byte quota.

provisioned.description: The graph binding, delivery log and all pinned schemas are durable.

include_shared.description:
Explicit approval to copy tables classified as shared to this source's
bounded customer set. False rejects shared tables; no default broadcast.

prefix.description: An approved namespace, never a raw database value used as a path.

DateBucketGranularity.description:
The calendar unit a [`SparqlGroupKey::DateBucket`] truncates a datetime to.
Truncation is in UTC; the label is the bucket's start as a sortable string.

DecideActivityQuestion.description: One choice question of a decide request.

criteria.description:
Option id → what the option means: 2 to 64 options, ids
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`.

instructions.description: What to decide about the state. Not empty.

DecideActivityRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/activities/decide`: the decision model answers each
question about `state` with one of its options.

effect_id.description:
The effect id of the workflow step that makes the call (`ctx.step`'s
`effectId`): with one, the first answer is kept, and a repeat of the
same request returns it with `cached: true`. `[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]`, 1 to
200 characters.

label.description: A short name for the call log, at most 64 characters.

questions.description:
Question id → question: 1 to 64 questions, ids
`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`.

state.description: What the questions are about: any JSON, at most 200,000 characters.

oneOf.description:
A workflow test makes the call ([`ActivityTest`]). Added 2026-10-20;
an older server refuses the field.

The workflow turn that makes the call: the call log names its run
(`origin.run`). The TypeScript SDK sets it from the step context.

DecideActivityResponse.description: The answers of a decide call.

answers.description: Question id → answer. A question the model did not answer is missing.

cached.description:
The answers were kept from an earlier request with the same
`effect_id`.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What this request cost, in millionths of a US dollar: 0 for a cached
answer.

tokens_in.description: Input tokens this request used: 0 for a cached answer.

tokens_out.description: Output tokens this request used: 0 for a cached answer.

DecorationStatus.description:
One row of the engine's decoration-status catalog: whether a declarable
ontology decoration is actually acted on by the engine (`enforced`), recorded
and meaningful but not the mechanism (`advisory`), or present-but-unwired
(`reserved`). The catalog is engine-global — identical for every graph — so
the API, MCP, and console agree on what the engine *acts on* versus what it
merely *remembers*. See `decoration_catalog`.

effect.description: One line: what the engine does with it (or that it does nothing yet).

name.description: The decoration field name (e.g. `inverse_name`, `transitive`, `value_type`).

DemoCasePayloads.description: Case evidence is returned only after the final graph-incarnation proof.

actual_result.description: At most max_result_bytes, preserved even for a wrong/unsupported term.

DemoCurrentRunResponse.description:
The fixed demo/1 RDF roster is identity-store, auth-outage and sso-customer
on semantic_graph. Known unported datasets are unavailable, not empty passes.
Every completed case uses exactly the response's one epoch/commit pin.

complete.description:
All three cases completed with interpretable answers, independently of
whether those answers matched. Timeout/partial/unavailable is false.

completed_case_count.description: Unknown when case payloads are withheld after an interrupted run.

expected_case_count.description: Unknown (null) for a known dataset without a current case definition.

DemoRunLimits.description: Diagnostic limits, not validity bounds on RDF data, ontologies or manifests.

deadline_millis.description:
Cooperative IO/elapsed budget. Late synchronous completion cannot pass;
this does not claim that an operating-system thread is forcibly stopped.

DemoSparqlResult.description:
The engine's result document, preserved verbatim like SparqlTextResponse.
An unavailable malformed-result case can carry the reported document as
evidence; no lexical RDF value is converted through an application number.

outputs.description:
What it made: stored pages, the commit sequence of its facts. At most
16 KiB of JSON.

run_id.description: The run that made it (your own id: a turn, a message id).

Derivation.description: One derivation as the server keeps it.

DerivationCheckResponse.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/derivations/check`: whether the key has a
derivation.

content_uploaded_at.description:
The upload of the content's live file: its `uploaded_at`, RFC 3339.
Send it back with the record. Then a run of a file deleted since the
check records nothing. Absent when the file is not live: deleted,
reclaimed, not written yet, or no file at all.

DerivationKey.description:
What a derivation is of: one content, one workflow version, one set of
settings.

settings_digest.description:
A digest of the settings it ran with (for example the hex SHA-256 of
their canonical JSON; `none` without settings): 1 to 128 of `A-Z`,
`a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

sha256.description: The content's SHA-256, 64 hexadecimal characters (stored lowercase).

version.description: Its version, in the same characters.

workflow_type.description:
The workflow type that made it: 1 to 128 of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`,
`_`, `.` and `-`.

content_uploaded_at.description:
The upload the work was done for: the `content_uploaded_at` of the
check. The record writes only while it is the file's live upload.
When the file was deleted since, it records nothing and answers
`409 derivation_upload_changed`. Without it, the record belongs to
the upload at the time of the record.

outputs.description: What it made, at most 16 KiB of JSON.

run_id.description: The run that made it, at most 256 characters.

DerivationRecordResponse.description:
The answer of a record: the derivation the server keeps, and whether
this request wrote it (`false`: the key had one, which is returned).

DeveloperWorkflowDetails.description: `details` of a developer workflow (a triggered workflow of `workflow`).

every_field.description: The watch has no fields: a change of any fact of an instance marks it.

inbox_full_since.description: The inbox of the workflow was full at the last send, since this time.

instance_id.description: The workflow instance that receives the messages: `starter.<name>`.

next_message.description: The number of the next message id.

ontology_version.description: The ontology version the workflow last checked the watched class at.

pending_removed.description: Instances that left the class, waiting to be sent.

Digest.description: Validated content address. Deserialization cannot introduce an object path.

DiscoveryFailure.description:
Fixed operator-facing failures. Source/driver exception strings cannot enter
the stored result. An adapter maps any unknown failure to `reader_failed`.

oneOf.description:
Once approved, replacement/cancellation through discovery is forbidden.
Connection retirement is the control path after this durable boundary.

DiscoveryTableMapping.description:
Schema hashes come from the verified catalog, never from a browser's JSON
serializer. Relation keys are the catalog's stable `pg_<table OID>` ids.

effect_id.description:
The effect id of the workflow step that makes the call (`ctx.step`'s
`effectId`): with one, the first answer is kept, and a repeat of the
same request returns it with `cached: true`. `[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]`, 1 to
200 characters.

label.description: A short name for the call log, at most 64 characters.

texts.description: 1 to 256 texts, each not empty and at most 8,000 characters.

oneOf.description:
The workflow turn that makes the call: the call log names its run
(`origin.run`). The TypeScript SDK sets it from the step context.

EmbedActivityResponse.description: The vectors of an embed call.

cached.description:
The vectors were kept from an earlier request with the same
`effect_id`.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What this request cost, in millionths of a US dollar: 0 for a cached
answer.

tokens_in.description:
Input tokens this request used (an estimate: characters / 4): 0 for
a cached answer.

vectors.description: One vector per text, in the order of the texts.

Embedding.description:
The persisted embedding (`…/embeddings/epoch=<e>/<name>/embedding.json`):
the latest declaration and which version serves, builds, and was served
before.

previous.description: The version that served before the last switch (one rollback).

EmbeddingBackfill.description:
A pass over every instance of the class: the first backfill of a
version, or a rescan when the commit deltas are not available.

cursor.description: The last instance IRI done; the next page starts after it.

rescan.description: A rescan of a ready version (the delta chain was not available).

target_seq.description: The published commit the pass reads.

EmbeddingCandidate.description:
One fact the instances of a class could give their text, measured on a
sample of the class.

chosen.description: The field is in the previewed recipe.

coverage.description: Share of the sampled instances with at least one value (0 to 1).

examples.description: Up to three values from the sample, as they appear in the text.

max.description: Values per instance the field keeps (the recipe's `max`).

name.description: The line name the field gets in the text.

path.description:
The path as a recipe stores it: one predicate IRI, or a link and the
predicate read on the linked entity.

EmbeddingCandidateKind.description: What kind of value a candidate field gives the text.

dim.description: The vector dimension; the model's when absent.

exclude.description: Names or IRIs to drop from the automatic choice.

from.description:
The fields in text order. Absent: the server picks them from a sample
of the class (the label, frequent text literals, the labels of linked
entities) and stores the result.

model.description: The model id; the catalog's embedding model when absent.

name.description: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`; defaults to the class's local name.

title.description:
The field that names each hit, as a path (`display_name`,
`schema:name`, `<https://…>`, `company/label`). Absent on a new
embedding: the ontology's name property (see
[`EmbeddingTitleSource`]); absent on an existing one: its name stays.

EmbeddingField.description:
A resolved field: the predicate IRIs of the path (one or two), the name
in the text, and the value cap.

name.description:
The word before the colon in the text; defaults to the local name of
the first predicate.

EmbeddingFieldSpec.description:
A field as a caller writes it: a path, or a path with a display name and
a value cap.

oneOf.description: `label`, `description`, `calls/label`, `rdfs:label`, `<https://…>`.

model_id.description:
The embedding model of the graph: every serving embedding of the
graph uses it, so one query vector serves a search over all classes.
Absent before the first declaration (the catalog's model applies then).

next_model_id.description:
The model a move goes to: every embedding builds a version with it,
and the graph switches when all are ready (the search keeps
`model_id` until then).

EmbeddingManifest.description:
One version (`…/<name>/v<n>/manifest.json`, CAS): its recipe, its runs,
and how far it covers the graph.

oneOf.description: The published commit the version has embedded through.

runs.description: Oldest first. A newer run shadows an older run for the same id.

EmbeddingModelRequest.description:
Move every embedding of the graph to another model
(`PUT /v1/embeddings/model`). Each embedding builds a new version beside
the serving one; the graph switches to the new model at once when every
embedding has it ready, so a search never mixes two models.

dim.description: The vector dimension; the model's when absent.

iris.description: Show these instances instead of the first ones.

sample.description: Sample entities to show (default 5, at most 50).

EmbeddingPreviewRequest.description:
Preview a declaration (`POST /v1/embeddings/preview`): stores nothing and
calls no model.

candidates.description:
Every field the class could give its text: the recipe's fields first,
then the others by coverage. The automatic choice takes the label,
text facts on at least 10% of the sample, and links to named
entities; values and rarer facts are left for the caller to add.

estimate.description: The spend of embedding every instance, from the samples' mean length.

instances.description: Instances of the class at the published generation.

sampled.description: Instances the candidates were measured on (up to 1,000).

title_suggestion.description:
A fact whose values read as names, when the hits are named by
`rdfs:label` (found or declared) and the labels do not name them (on
less than half of the instances, keys or codes like `yc-job:94386`,
or one value repeated), or the instances have no name. The choice
reads the values, never the property names: a text fact on at least
90% of the sample, about one value per instance, at least 80%
distinct, at most 10% keys or codes, one sentence each, and a median
of at most 120 characters. The most distinct wins, then the shortest.
A suggestion only; the recipe keeps its `title` until a declaration
names another.

EmbeddingRecallStats.description:
Recall of the version's index against an exhaustive search over the same
runs and filter, from sampled searches.

recall_at_k.description: The mean recall@k over the samples.

EmbeddingRecipe.description:
What an embedding embeds and with which model. A change of fields or
model is a new version.

class.description: The class IRI whose instances (`?s a <class>`) are embedded.

title.description:
The path whose value names each hit: one predicate IRI, or a link and
the predicate read on the linked entity. Empty: the instance's
`rdfs:label`. An instance with no value here shows its `rdfs:label`,
else the local name of its IRI.

EmbeddingRunRef.description:
One immutable run of a version: an `lbb-ann` ranged v4 index with a raw
f32 region, and an `ids` table.

bytes.description:
Bytes of the run's objects (meta, blocks, ids); 0 for runs written
before the field existed.

id.description: `<micros:020>-<nonce>`: unique per write.

tombstones.description: Ids the run removes from older runs.

text.description:
The exact text the model would embed; empty when the entity has no
value in any field (it gets no vector).

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

reranked_candidates.description:
Number of candidates re-scored with exact raw-f32 distances. Zero when
`rerank` was not requested or the run has no raw region.

oneOf.description:
Which persisted ANN run served this query relative to the resolved
`as_of` ceiling. Present only when `explain` is set. See
[`SearchTemporalCoverage`].

A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `Eventual`, a floor not yet covered returns a
retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429. `None` == no floor. See
`SearchEngineOptions::min_indexed_seq`.

query_vector.description:
Client-computed query vector. When present it is used directly and the
provider only identifies the embedding space; `query` remains for
display/explain purposes.

rerank.description:
Opt into exact raw-f32 reranking of the persisted vector candidates.
Only effective when the run carries a raw-f32 region (built with
`include_raw`); otherwise it is a no-op. Default off keeps the compact
4-bit-approximate path.

rerank_top_k.description:
How many top approximate candidates to re-score exactly before
truncating to `top_k`. Defaults to a small multiple of `top_k` when
unset; ignored unless `rerank` is set.

oneOf.description: The newest commit of the graph now.

lag_commits.description:
Commits the serving version is behind the newest commit
(`head_seq` − its `embedded_through_seq`). 0: a search finds every
commit. The commits wait for the publication
(`head_seq` − `published_seq`), then for the embed job.

oneOf.description: The commit of the published RDF generation now.

EmbeddingStep.description: What one step of the embed job did.

more.description: The version has more work (a backfill page, a fold).

scanned.description: Instances whose text the step rebuilt.

EmbeddingStepTimings.description: Where the time of one job step went, in milliseconds.

embed_ms.description: Reading reused vectors and calling the model.

scan_ms.description:
Finding the instances: the class page, or the commit deltas and the
instances they make dirty.

text_ms.description: Building the texts from the graph.

write_ms.description: Building and writing the run, and the manifest CAS.

EmbeddingTitleSource.description: Where the name of a hit comes from.

EmbeddingUsage.description: Embedding spend. The token count is an estimate: characters / 4.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes the version's runs store (the storage it is billed for).

attributes.description:
The entity's RDF-projected properties as typed JSON: numbers, booleans,
RFC3339 datetime strings, strings and sets. Nulls, bytes, vectors,
non-finite numbers and empty sets have no RDF projection and are omitted.

oneOf.description: Whether the relationship `properties` in `rdf_relations` are complete.
Whether the relationship evidence in `rdf_relations` is complete.

Current RDF relationships. Unlike native edge events, these facts carry
no confidence, valid-time interval, event id or evidence attribution.

Present only when a per-request cap actually cut one of the collections
above, so an ordinary entity's response is byte-identical to the
uncapped one. A supernode read returns the caps' worth of rows plus this
block, rather than its whole degree.

unavailable_sections.description:
Legacy sections unavailable in this read model. An empty listed section
means unavailable, not that the entity has no history or relationships.

EntityDetailTruncation.description:
Which of an entity read's degree-proportional collections were cut, and by
how much. Only the cut collections appear.

edge_property_lookups.description:
True when the per-response cap on edge property reads stopped the
property read: some relationships show no `properties` although they
have some.

oneOf.description:
Set when `outgoing`/`incoming`/`current_state` are a partial view of the
entity's current edges.

evidence_lookups.description:
True when the per-response cap on evidence statement lookups stopped
the evidence read: some relationships may show fewer evidence entries
than they have, without `evidence_truncated`.

truncated_by_read_budget.description:
True when the request's object-read budget stopped the read before its
row caps did, so the counts below are floors for a different reason:
the read gave up rather than the collection being full.

entity_id.description:
Optional resolved entity id (32-char hex). When set, the embedding attaches
to exactly this entity, bypassing `(type, key, name)` resolution. This is
the identity a managed backfill has for each entity it enumerates from a
snapshot — it holds the id but not the original external `key`, which the
id is a one-way hash of, so name-based resolution would create a phantom
name-keyed twin instead of attaching to the keyed entity. `entity_id`
takes precedence over `key`/`name`; `type` is still resolved for the
entity record.

key.description:
Optional stable external key, matching [`NamedEntityInput::key`]. Set it to
attach this embedding to a keyed entity; omit it for `(type, name)`
identity.

oneOf.description: Defaults to Cosine.

attributes.description:
Typed scalar attributes (native JSON), present only when the request asks
for a projection via `?fields=a,b` (or `?fields=*` for all). Lets "list
entities and their titles" be one call instead of a list + N point
lookups. Same `attributes` shape the single-entity read returns.

EntityFieldsWritten.description: The property fields written to one entity by a commit (canonical names).

removed_fields.description:
Previously-stored fields this write **dropped** — present (and non-empty)
only under `property_merge: "replace"`, where the commit's field list
becomes the entity's whole attribute set. Under the default `merge` it is
always empty (a merge never removes a field), so a populated
`removed_fields` is the explicit signal that a destructive replace pruned
attributes the commit did not re-send.

fields.description:
Typed entity properties to return on each matched row. Empty keeps the
lean row; `"*"` or `"all"` projects every property.

filter.description: Property/metadata predicate evaluated against one loaded graph snapshot.

limit.description:
Maximum rows returned. The response's `matched_count` still reports the
full number of matches before this limit is applied.

matched_count.description: Total entities satisfying the predicate before `limit` is applied.

oneOf.description:
Highest commit covered by the **vector/ANN index**, or `None` when no ANN
index has been built. See [`Self::bm25_indexed_commit_seq`].

Highest commit covered by the **BM25 full-text index**, or `None` when no
full-text index has been built. Together with `ann_indexed_commit_seq`
this answers "is this graph indexed for search?" on the dedicated entity
metadata diagnostics read — unlike `snapshot.compacted_seq`, which is the
graph snapshot base. Ordinary entity detail leaves derived-index lineage
absent so a point read never blocks on index discovery. Lag behind
`snapshot.commit_seq` is the unindexed tail.

EntityPropertiesInput.description:
Literal property values to attach to one entity (matched by type + name).

`properties` accepts **two interchangeable shapes**:
- verbose — a list of `{ "field": "...", "value": { "<type>": v } }` objects,
  where `<type>` is one of `bool|i64|f64|date_time|keyword|text`; and
- flat — a `{ "field": value }` object, e.g. `{ "h_index": 52, "title": "VP" }`,
  where the value type is inferred from JSON (bool/integer/float/string) and
  then coerced to the field's declared type at commit (so a flat string lands
  in a `keyword` field, a flat `"2026-06-26"` in a `date_time` field, and a
  flat integer in an `f64` field).

The flat shape removes the nested-`value` ceremony that made `entity_properties`
hard to get right; reach for the verbose shape only when you need to force a
specific wire type.

entity_id.description:
Optional resolved entity id (32-char hex). When set, these properties
attach to exactly this entity, bypassing `(type, key, name)` resolution —
the same escape hatch [`EntityEmbeddingInput::entity_id`] provides. A
managed backfill enumerating a snapshot holds each entity's id but not the
original external `key` (the id is a one-way hash of it), so resolving by
name would attach to — or mint — a phantom name-keyed twin instead of the
real keyed entity. `entity_id` takes precedence over `key`/`name`; `type`
is still resolved for the entity record.

key.description:
Optional stable external key, matching [`NamedEntityInput::key`]. Set it to
attach these properties to a keyed entity; omit it for `(type, name)`
identity.

properties.description:
The field values to write, as a list of `{ "field", "value" }` objects or
as a flat `{ "field": value }` map (see [`PropertiesInput`]).

remove_fields.description:
Field names to **drop** from this entity, applied after `properties` in the
same commit — a surgical per-field delete that avoids a replace-mode
re-send of the whole survivor set (the silent-wipe footgun). Works in
either `property_merge` mode: the named fields are removed from the
entity's stored set even when the rest of the commit merges. A field
listed in both `properties` and `remove_fields` is rejected (you cannot
both set and drop it); an unknown field name is rejected. Dropped fields
are echoed back under `written_properties[].removed_fields`.

EntityReadResponse.description:
The existing entity resource selects its additive wire response only when
the caller explicitly requests `records/1`.

EvalAskInput.description:
The inputs of an Ask request (`POST /v1/query/ask`) that shape its
answer, kept on an `ask` trace and its golden so a run asks the same way.
Every field is optional. An object stored before 2026-10-06 may hold
`previous`, the earlier steps of the removed one-shot rewrite: they read
as notes at the end of `context` (the loop reads what the app knows
there), so a follow-up question keeps its meaning when a run asks it
again.

anchor.description: The entity IRIs the user picked (`anchor`).

context.description: The app's notes for the model (`context`).

oneOf.description: The route the caller fixed (`route`).

timeline.description:
The app's own dated points (`timeline`), so a history question finds
the same commits on every run.

today.description:
The date the question was asked (`YYYY-MM-DD`), so a relative
question reads the same window on every run.

EvalDataset.description:
An Evals dataset: a name, a kind, the settings it is graded with, and
its items. It belongs to a graph and is erased with it.

about.description: What the dataset is, in sentences, as an answer key has it.

id.description: `ds_` and an opaque suffix.

items.description: The items, in the order they were added. A list leaves them out.

EvalDatasetCreateRequest.description:
`POST /v1/evals/datasets`: create a dataset with its first items, or
from a source: `source: {kind: "test", id}` makes the answers of that
workflow test the items, and its settings the `install`. A test has one
dataset (the test's `dataset`): a save of a test whose dataset exists
brings that dataset up to date and answers it.

oneOf.description:
Where the items come from, instead of `items`, `about` and
`install`. Only a test (`kind: "test"`) is a source here.

EvalDatasetDeleted.description:
`DELETE /v1/evals/datasets?id=`: the dataset was deleted. A delete
repeated answers the same.

EvalDatasetExpected.description:
`expected.json` of an export: the answer key. Its `records` are the
items without their text and instance, which `records.json` holds.

EvalDatasetExport.description:
A dataset in the files of a template's samples: the inputs
(`records.json`) and the answer key (`expected.json`).

EvalDatasetInstall.description:
The settings a `values` dataset is graded with, as a template answer key
has them: the value type of each property (`text`, `keyword`, `i64`,
`f64`, `bool`), the units, and the context.

case.description: What the example shows, in one sentence.

iri.description: The instance the input was read from, when it came from a graph.

leave_out.description: Values a correct run does not write.

name.description: The input's name: a record name or label, unique in the dataset.

text.description:
The input text, at most 40,000 characters. A write needs it; the
`expected.records` of an export leave it out, because `records`
holds it, as a template's `records.json` does.

EvalDatasetItemsRequest.description:
`POST /v1/evals/datasets/items`: add items to the dataset `id`. An item
with the name of an item the dataset has replaces it in its place.

EvalDatasetKind.description: What the items of a dataset hold.

EvalDatasetList.description:
`GET /v1/evals/datasets`: the graph's datasets, newest first, without
their items.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

EvalDatasetRecord.description:
One input of an export (`records.json` of a template): its name, its
text and the instance it was read from.

EvalDatasetSource.description:
The origin of an item: its kind and the id of the test, review item or
template it came from.

EvalExpectedValue.description:
One value of an item: a value a correct run writes, or, in `leave_out`,
one it must not write.

accept.description: Other spellings a text value may take, lower case.

quote.description: Words of the text that state the value.

reason.description: Why a value is left out.

stated.description:
The number and unit as the text states them, when the property holds
another unit: `450 mm` for a `width_cm` of 45.

value.description:
The value: numbers compare as numbers, text in lower case and trimmed
against `accept`. In `leave_out`, null means no value at all for the
property.

EvalExperiment.description:
An Evals experiment. `get` returns it with its items; a list leaves them
out.

a.description: The configuration in use at the start.

oneOf.description: A person applied B.

cost_micro_usd.description: What both arms spent so far.

error.description: Why it failed, at most 500 characters.

estimate_micro_usd.description: What the start estimated both arms to cost.

oneOf.description: For `done`: why it ended.

id.description: `exp_` and an opaque suffix.

items.description: One row per item, in dataset order. A list leaves them out.

max_cost_micro_usd.description: The cost limit of both arms together, in millionths of a US dollar.

by.description: Who: the caller identity of the write (`account:<id>`, `key:<id>`).

EvalExperimentArm.description: One arm: a full configuration of the workflow, run as a workflow test.

cost_micro_usd.description: What the arm's model calls cost so far, in millionths of a US dollar.

fingerprint.description:
The arm test's fingerprint: a live run with the same one ran the same
configuration.

models.description: The model of each use (`extract`, `decide`), fixed at the start.

revision.description:
The settings revision (`wrev_…`): the hash of the settings the arm
ran, which every workflow has.

test.description: The arm's workflow test (`wtest_…`), which holds its values.

EvalExperimentArmItem.description: One arm's grade of one item.

score.description:
F1 of the item's precision and recall, 0 to 1; 0 when the arm did
not answer.

EvalExperimentArmReport.description: One arm's figures over the compared items.

failed.description: Items the arm did not answer.

precision.description: Over every compared item, as the template grader computes it.

review_share.description: Values sent to review over values written and sent to review.

EvalExperimentArmRequest.description:
What B changes in A: `{model: {use, model}}` or `{revision}`, exactly
one (`experiment_arms_mixed` for both).

oneOf.description: The use whose model B changes; absent for a revision.

EvalExperimentChangeKind.description: The part of the configuration B changes.

EvalExperimentCreateRequest.description:
`POST /v1/evals/experiments` (and `…/estimate`): run B against the
workflow's configuration in use on a dataset's items.

dataset.description: A dataset of the graph whose kind the workflow reads (`ds_…`).

max_cost_usd.description:
The cost limit of both arms, in US dollars: more than 0, at most 100,
default 5.

max_items.description: Items to run, the dataset's first ones: 1 to 200, default 200.

workflow.description: A named workflow of the graph.

EvalExperimentDataset.description: The dataset an experiment runs on.

deleted.description:
The dataset was deleted after the experiment ran; the report stays as
it was last scored.

EvalExperimentEstimate.description:
`POST /v1/evals/experiments/estimate`: what a start with the same body
would estimate. It writes nothing.

budget_left_micro_usd.description:
What is left of the environment's monthly workflow budget; absent
when the environment has no limit.

items.description: The items the experiment would run.

EvalExperimentItem.description: One item of an experiment: its names and each arm's grade.

oneOf.description: A's grade; absent until A answered the item.

input.description:
The arms' input IRI (`urn:lbb:item:…`): the arms' tests hold the
item's values under it.

iri.description: The item's instance, when it has one.

item.description: The item's name in the dataset.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

EvalExperimentModelChange.description: B's model change: another model for one use.

EvalExperimentReport.description:
The comparison of B against A over the items both arms answered or
failed.

ci_low.description: The 95% interval of the mean difference (a paired bootstrap).

cost_ratio.description: B's cost per item over A's.

labels_etag.description: The etag of the dataset's items it was scored with.

outcome.description:
`too_few` under 10 items, else `better`, `worse` or `same` by the
interval.

qualifies.description:
The trials' bar: at least 20 items, `ci_low` at least −0.05, B's
failure share at most A's plus 0.05, and B cheaper per item or
`better`.

stale.description:
The dataset's items changed since it was scored (set by a read; a
turn scores it again).

unlabeled.description: Values of unlabeled properties on which the arms differ.

EvalExperimentStatus.description:
Where an experiment stands. `queued` → `running` → `done`, `failed` or
`cancelled`; the last three are final.

EvalExperimentUnlabeled.description:
A value of a property an item does not label, on which the arms differ:
a person grades it (a `grade` review item).

a.description: A's value, when A wrote one.

b.description: B's value, when B wrote one.

EvalExperimentWorkflow.description:
The workflow both arms run, with its creation time: a workflow made
again under the name is another workflow.

created.description: When the workflow was created, RFC 3339.

EvalItem.description: One result of a query: a hit of a search, or a row of a SPARQL query.

id.description:
Stable id of the result: the term id of a hit; on the `ask` surface
`e:` + the blake3 of the entity IRI the row names, or `v:` + the
blake3 of its values; on the `sparql` surface the blake3 of the
canonical row; `ask:true` / `ask:false` for an ASK answer.

iri.description: The entity the result names, when it names one.

label.description: A short display form: the hit's label, or the row's values.

rank.description: Position in the returned list, from 0.

value.description: The result as returned: a SPARQL binding row, or a hit.

id.description: The result id (`id` on a hit or a trace item).

valid.description: True: the result answers the request (thumbs up).

EvalItems.description: The results a query returned, in a form that compares across commits.

items.description: The first [`EVAL_INLINE_ITEM_LIMIT`] results, in returned order.

items_blake3.description: blake3 over the sorted result ids: the set, not the order.

rejected.description: Results the judge labeled not relevant.

review.description: Results the judge left for a person.

model.description: The model behind the provider, when it has one.

by.description: Free-form labeler identity (an agent name, a user id, a judge model).

probability.description: The judge's probability that the result answers the request.

valid.description: True: the result answers the request (thumbs up).

EvalLabelRequest.description:
Thumbs up or down on results of a trace: one result as `item` + `valid`,
or several in `items`. On an `ask` trace, `valid` without `item` or
`items` labels the answer as a whole: `true` makes the trace's query the
golden query of the question; `false` with `sparql` makes that query the
golden query (the server checks and runs it once); `false` alone marks
the answer wrong. `route` with `valid: true`, or with `valid: false` and
`sparql`, names the question's route; `valid: true` alone takes the
trace's route.

oneOf.description:
With an answer label that names the golden query (`valid: true`, or
`valid: false` with `sparql`): the route the question expects. A run
checks the router's pick against it.
`explicit` (default) or `implicit`. `judge` is reserved for the server.

sparql.description: With `valid: false` and no `item`: the right query for the question.

oneOf.description: The golden that now holds the labels.

EvalMode.description:
Where evals run. `Off` records traces and goldens but never runs them on
its own; `Advisory` runs them on demand and on the periodic tick. A
blocking gate is not part of this increment.

EvalQueryCheck.description:
The query check of an `ask` golden: the rows of the query Ask wrote
against the rows of the golden query, both read at the same commit. It
passes when `missing` and `extra` are 0.

extra.description: Rows only the written query returns.

missing.description: Rows only the golden query returns.

EvalQueryType.description: The type of a question's query.

EvalResults.description: One run of the suite at one commit of the graph. One object per commit.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What the models of the run's Ask replays cost together, in
millionths of a US dollar; absent when the run asked nothing.

goldens_version.description: The suite version the run read.

precision.description: Mean precision over the goldens with judged results returned.

recall.description: Mean recall over the goldens with known-relevant results.

regression.description: True when `score` is below the settings threshold.

review_traces.description: Traces this run opened for results nobody judged yet.

route_checked.description:
Goldens with a route check: the golden has a route and the router
answered.

route_right.description: Route checks where the router picked the golden's route.

score.description: Share of goldens that pass; `1.0` for an empty suite.

EvalRouteCheck.description:
The route check of an `ask` golden: the router's pick for the question
against the route the golden expects. It scores the router and does not
change the verdict: the answer loop may take another route, and an
answer stands on its rows.

probability.description: The router's probability of its pick.

EvalRunAnswer.description: The app's answer to one `ask` golden.

oneOf.description:
The commit the query reads, for a question about an earlier point;
default the commit the run checks.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What the app's models cost for this answer, in millionths of a US
dollar.

error.description: Why the app has no answer: the verdict is an `error`.

oneOf.description: The answer in words and its citations, for the verdict.

How the app routed the question: the `route` of
`POST /v1/query/ask` in `mode: "route"`. A run checks the router's
pick against the golden's route.

sparql.description:
The `SELECT` or `ASK` query whose rows hold the answer. The server
runs it. Absent: the app wrote no query (it found the question
unanswerable), or it failed (`error`).

EvalRunAnswersRequest.description:
The app's own answers to `ask` goldens (`POST /v1/evals/run/answers`):
the app asked each question with its own loop. The run checks these
goldens only, as it checks Ask's answers, and keeps the results in the
app's own series.

answers.description: One answer per golden, at most 2,000.

runner.description:
The app: lower-case letters, digits and `-`, at most 40 characters
(default `app`). `GET /v1/evals/results?runner=` reads its runs.

max_goldens.description: Goldens the runner executes per run, at most [`EVAL_HARD_MAX_GOLDENS`].

threshold.description: Score below which a run is reported as a regression.

EvalShown.description: The hits an app showed of a search.

review_traces.description: Traces with results the judge left for a person.

unlabeled_items.description: Results nobody labeled yet, across those traces.

unlabeled_traces.description: Traces with a result nobody labeled yet, among the most recent traces.

EvalSurface.description: Which surface a trace or a golden belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The answer label of an `ask` trace: its query is right for the
question (`valid: true`), or it is wrong.

The inputs of the Ask request, for an `ask` trace of
`POST /v1/query/rewrite`.

golden_id.description: The golden that holds this trace's labels.

judged_at.description: RFC 3339; set when the judge looked at the trace.

oneOf.description: The type of the query, for an `ask` trace.

What Ask answered in words, with the IRIs it cited: on the trace of
`POST /v1/query/ask`, and on a run's review trace of an `ask`
golden. An answer label judges it with the query.

request.description: The user's words, as the caller passed them in `request`.

oneOf.description:
The rerank of a search trace, as the search reported it: whether
the model ran, the hits it read and the hits it moved. Each item of
a reranked search holds its `relevance`.

review.description:
Results the judge looked at but left for a person, with its
probability (between the two thresholds).

oneOf.description:
How the question was routed, on an `ask` trace: the route of
`POST /v1/query/ask`, or the `route` the caller sent with
`POST /v1/query/sparql-text`. An answer label `valid: true` makes its
`kind` the golden's route.

served_at_seq.description: The commit of the graph the results were read at.

oneOf.description:
The hits the app showed of a search trace: its cut (`shown` of
`POST /v1/search`) and how many hits passed it. Each item holds
`shown`.

sparql.description: The SPARQL query, or the query text on the vector surface.

v.description: Trace format version. Currently `2`: labels per result.

cost_micro_usd.description:
What the models of the replay cost, in millionths of a US dollar
(`via: ask`), or what the app said its models cost (`via: app`).

oneOf.description: The type the golden expects (`ask` goldens).

precision.description:
`relevant_returned / (relevant_returned + wrong_returned)`, over the
judged results that came back.

oneOf.description:
The query check (`ask` goldens of type `sparql` or `hybrid` with a
golden query). The result counts above are the result check against
the judged results.
The type of the query that ran this time (`ask` goldens).

relevant_missing.description: Known-relevant results that did not come back.

oneOf.description:
What Ask (`via: ask`) or the app (`via: app`) answered this time in
words, with the IRIs it cited. The run checks the rows; it reports
the words.

review_trace_id.description: The trace opened for the unknown results (the review queue).

oneOf.description: The route of the question this time (`via: ask` or `app`).

The router's pick against the golden's route, when the golden has a
route and the router answered. It does not change `verdict`.

shown.description:
The hits the app would show this time, for a `search` golden with a
cut: the result counts above count only these.

sparql.description:
The query Ask wrote this time (`via: ask`), or the app's query
(`via: app`).

oneOf.description: How the run tested the golden; absent when it was skipped.

EvalVia.description: How a run tested a golden.

EvidenceCompleteness.description: Whether the evidence (or the edge properties) a read returns is complete.

observation_id.description:
Stable observation id used by full-fidelity export/import. Ordinary
callers omit it and receive the existing deterministic request id.

oneOf.description:
Optional page-region anchor for this evidence. Requires `text`
(the region anchors to the evidence observation the text creates).

EvidenceRegion.description:
A page region of a piece of evidence: a 0-based page and a box in
coordinates normalized to the page (`[0, 1]`, origin top-left, y down),
on the grid the commit quantized them to.

ExtractorDatasetResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/extractor-dataset` — the extractor fine-tune's training
feed: stored `EPISODE` transcripts joined (via evidence observations) to
the facts the observe pipeline committed from them, plus the ontology
vocabulary the serving prompt carries (so the trainer rebuilds the exact
extraction prompt).

relations.description: The extraction prompt's relation vocabulary at this snapshot.

split_seq.description: Facts with commit seq ≤ this were consumed.

types.description: The extraction prompt's entity-type vocabulary at this snapshot.

ExtractorExample.description:
One extractor training example: an episode transcript and the facts that
were actually committed from it.

ExtractorFact.description:
One extractor training fact, mirroring the resident extractor's strict
output JSON (`{statement, source_type, source, relation, target_type,
target, confidence}`) — every committed fact was vocabulary-snapped
before it was committed, so labels are execution-verified.

FileCitation.description:
One fact whose evidence names a file: the edge's statement node, the
edge, and the evidence source (the file's `Document` IRI with the
fragment of the place).

FileCounts.description:
`GET /v1/files/counts`: the graph's files by parse status, counted over
the `Document` entities of the published generation.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
The commit the published generation holds: the counts are as of it.
Absent before the graph's first publication (all counts 0).

by_parse_status.description:
The files by `parse_status` (`parsed`, `unsupported`, `failed`), and
`waiting` for a file with none yet.

purged_edges.description:
With `purge=true`: the edges whose evidence names the file that the
delete retracted (at most [`FILE_PURGE_EDGES_MAX`]).

FileLine.description:
One parsed line: its id (`p<page number>-l<line number>`, both from 1),
its text (the words joined by one space, NFC), its box and its words.

FileList.description: `GET /v1/files`: one page of the graph's files, newest upload first.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
With `parse_status` or `name`: the commit of the published
generation whose `Document` facts the filter read. A file uploaded,
renamed or parsed after it matches once a generation holds the
change. Absent for the plain list, and before the graph's first
publication (a filtered list is then empty).

next.description:
The cursor of the next page: pass it as `after`. Absent when the list
ended. A page can hold fewer than `limit` files while `next` is set.

FilePage.description:
One parsed page. `page` is the 0-based index (the `page` of a region
anchor); `width` and `height` are in PDF points.

ocr_required.description:
The page has fewer than 16 characters of text (white space not
counted) and images that cover at least 40% of it: a scan, or a page
of pictures. The parse read almost no text from it, and OCR is not
built. Absent (false) for every other page, so the pages of a file
with a text layer keep their bytes.

FilePages.description:
`GET /v1/files/pages`: pages `from` (inclusive) to `to` (exclusive) of a
parsed file, 0-based.

FilePagesPutRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/files/pages?sha256=&parser=`: what a parser made of one upload
of a file, sent by a worker that parses outside the server (LBB's hosted
`documents.parse`). `parsed` stores every page once under the parser id;
`failed` and `unsupported` store no page and record why.

error.description: Why the parse failed, at most 500 characters. Only without pages.

pages.description:
Every page of the file, in order, `page` 0 to `n - 1`, at most 2,000.
Only with `parsed`.

uploaded_at.description:
The upload the parser read: the file record's `uploaded_at`
(`GET /v1/files/record`). When the file was deleted and uploaded
again since, the server stores nothing and answers `409
file_upload_changed`; a deleted file answers `404 file_not_found`.

stored.description:
False when the same pages were stored before under this parser id:
nothing was written.

FileParse.description: What the parse starter made of a file.

ocr_pages.description:
The pages that need OCR (`ocr_required` is true on them). Absent
when none does, and for a parse that wrote no page flags.

cited_by.description:
With `deleted=true`: the current facts whose evidence names this
file, at most [`FILE_CITATIONS_MAX`], read at the published
generation. A delete with `purge=true` retracts them; while one cites
a deleted file the reclaim keeps its bytes. Empty in every other
answer.

deleted_at.description:
RFC 3339 time of the delete. Only `GET /v1/files/record` with
`deleted=true` answers a deleted file; every other answer holds live
files and leaves this out.

language.description:
The natural language of the content, a BCP 47 tag such as `en` or
`de-CH`.

name.description: The name it was uploaded under (the last upload's).

schema.description:
The schema the content follows, as an upload stated it (a name or
a URL).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex: the file's identity.

uploaded_at.description: RFC 3339 time of the first upload.

commit_seq.description:
The commit that wrote the `Document` entity (absent when nothing
changed).

created.description:
False when the graph held these bytes under this name already: the
upload changed nothing.

FileWord.description:
One word of a parsed line. `box` is `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` normalized to the
page (0 to 1, origin top left), 4 decimals.

FitProposal.description: One change the reasoning model proposed, and what the checks made of it.

change.description: The evolve operations the suggestion would carry.

detail.description: Why a proposal was dropped, when the check says more.

entity.description: The instance whose text the proposal came from.

key.description:
The suggestion key: `fit:<source>/<kind>/<normalised names>`. The
same change from many instances is one suggestion.

name.description: The class, property or relation the change adds or widens.

quote.description:
The sentence of the text that supports the change, as the model
quoted it.

support.description: The decision model's probability that the quote supports the change.

FitProposalKind.description: What kind of change a proposal is.

last_error.description: Why the last step stopped, until a later step succeeds.

pending.description: Changed instances still to read, oldest first.

oneOf.description: The published commit the source has read through.

spend.description:
This month's spend (the month rolls over at the first step of the
next month).

FitSourceBackfill.description:
A pass over every instance of the class: the first pass of a source, or a
new pass when the commit deltas are not available.

cursor.description: The last instance IRI done; the next page starts after it.

target_seq.description: The published commit the pass reads.

FitSourceCounters.description: What a fit source has done since it was declared.

already_covered.description: Dropped: the ontology has the change already.

chunks.description: Chunks sent to the reasoning model.

failed_chunks.description:
Chunks the reasoning model gave no usable answer for (a refusal, an
answer cut at its token limit, or text that is not JSON), read as no
proposal so that one text cannot stop the source.

instances.description: Instances read (an instance read again after a change counts again).

invalid.description: Dropped: the change is not valid against the ontology.

kept.description: Proposals that support a suggestion (new or existing).

quote_not_found.description: Dropped: the quote is not in the text.

reopened.description: Dismissed suggestions reopened by new evidence.

skipped.description:
Changed instances not read: more changed in one window than the job
keeps (5,000).

updated.description: Updates of open suggestions with new evidence.

weak_support.description: Dropped: the decision model scored the support below 0.5.

FitSourceDeclareRequest.description: Declare or change a fit source (`PUT /v1/ontology/fit-sources`).

class.description: The class IRI whose instances the fit reads.

context.description:
One sentence about what the text is, for the model ("employee
interviews about their work processes"). At most 500 characters.
Absent on an existing source: its context stays.

exclude.description: Names or IRIs to drop from the automatic choice.

from.description:
The fields in text order, with the path syntax of embeddings
(`transcript`, `label`, `rdfs:label`, `about/label`, `<https://…>`).
Absent: the server picks the text facts of a sample of the class,
longest text first, and stores the result.

name.description: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`; defaults to the class's local name.

month_cost_micro_usd.description: The stack's fit spend this month, in millionths of a US dollar.

monthly_budget_usd.description:
The stack's monthly budget for fit from text in US dollars (every
source of every graph together); absent when there is no limit.

iris.description: Show these instances instead of the first ones.

propose.description: Run the models on the first 3 sample instances (a dry run).

sample.description: Sample instances to show (default 3, at most 20).

FitSourcePreviewRequest.description:
Preview a declaration (`POST /v1/ontology/fit-sources/preview`): the text
the fit would read. With `propose`, the models also run on at most 3
instances and the proposals come back; nothing is filed or stored.

candidates.description:
Every field the class could give the text: the recipe's fields first,
then the others by coverage.

cost_micro_usd.description:
With `propose`: the spend of the dry run, in millionths of a US
dollar.

instances.description: Instances of the class at the published generation.

proposals.description:
With `propose`: every proposal of the sample instances, the dropped
ones included.

sampled.description: Instances the candidates were measured on (up to 1,000).

truncated.description:
With `propose`: the dry run reached its time limit (60 s), and the
proposals of the instances that did not finish are left out.

FitSourceRecipe.description:
What a fit source reads. A change of fields or context applies to the
instances read after it; the job does not read the earlier ones again.

class.description:
The class IRI whose instances (`?s a <class>`, subclasses included)
the fit reads.

queued.description: The fit job was asked to run now; the status shows its progress.

steps.description:
The steps the call ran itself. Empty from
`POST /v1/ontology/fit-sources/refresh`, which only asks the fit job
to run (`queued`).

chars.description: Characters of the whole text the fit reads.

chunks.description: Chunks the text makes (one reasoning-model call each).

text.description:
The text, up to 8,000 characters; empty when the instance has no
value in any field.

truncated.description: `text` is the start of a longer text.

FitSourceSpend.description:
The model spend of a fit source in one month (UTC), from the providers'
reported usage at list prices.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

FitSourceStatus.description: A fit source as `GET /v1/ontology/fit-sources` reports it.

lag_commits.description: Commits the source is behind the published generation.

oneOf.description: The commit of the published RDF generation now.

suggestions.description: The suggestions of this source (origin id `fit:<name>`) per status.

FitSourceStep.description: What one step of the fit job did.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

more.description: The source has more work (a backfill page, changed instances).

FitTextPages.description: Pages of a document, 1-based and inclusive.

FitTextRequest.description:
Run the fit once on a text (`POST /v1/ontology/fit-text`): pasted text,
or the parsed pages of an uploaded file. Exactly one of `text` and
`document`.

context.description: A sentence about the text, for the models.

document.description: The SHA-256 of an uploaded file whose pages `documents.parse` parsed.

dry_run.description: Run the models and the checks, and file nothing.

name.description:
The source name in the suggestion keys (`fit:<name>/…`),
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`. Default `text-<first 8 hex of the blake3
of the text, or of the file's SHA-256>`.

oneOf.description: Documents only: the pages to read (default: all, from page 1).

chars.description: Characters of text the models read.

chunks.description: Chunks the text was cut into (one reasoning-model call each).

failed_chunks.description:
Chunks the reasoning model gave no answer for (a refusal, an error,
or the 120 s limit).

oneOf.description: Documents only: the pages read, 1-based and inclusive.

proposals.description:
Every proposal, the dropped ones included, with what the checks made
of it.

truncated.description:
The call did not read all of the text: past 60,000 characters, or
past 50 pages.

updated.description:
Suggestions that got this text's evidence (open ones, and dismissed
ones it reopened); 0 with `dry_run`.

FitTextSpend.description: The spend of one fit-text call.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

FlatPropertyValue.description:
A bare JSON value in the flat `{ field: value }` property shape: a boolean,
an integer, a number, a string, or an array of integers or of strings. The
wire type is inferred from JSON; the commit path coerces it to the field's
declared `PropertyType`, so the inferred variant only needs to be in the
right ballpark.

columns.description: Source columns in the exact order of the referenced primary key.

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to the pinned published generation.

oneOf.description:
Which immutable run in the pinned published generation served this
query. Present only when `explain` is set. See
[`SearchTemporalCoverage`].

A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `Eventual`, a floor not yet covered returns a
retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429. `None` == no floor. See
`SearchEngineOptions::min_indexed_seq`.

offset.description:
Number of leading results to skip after ordering, for stateless paging:
`offset = page * top_k` walks pages deterministically. Defaults to 0.
Paging operates over a bounded candidate pool (~16 × `top_k`), not the
full match set, so paging is lossy past that pool: an `offset` beyond the
pool returns an empty page and documents outside the pool are omitted.
Keep `top_k` large enough that the pages you need fall inside the pool.

order.description:
Sort direction for `order_by`. Defaults to descending (highest score /
metadata value first).

order_by.description:
Ordering key for the result page. Defaults to relevance score. Ties
always break on the stable document id so paging is deterministic.
Ordering is applied over the bounded candidate pool (~16 × `top_k`), so
`order_by: metadata` reorders the top-scoring slice rather than the full
match set — matches outside the pool are not considered.

FusionServingDefaults.description:
Fusion serving default derived from a promoted `fusion` run: the weights
the search path applies when a request neither overrides the field nor
pins an explicit retrieval profile.

run.description: The promoted registry run these weights came from.

accepted_at.description: RFC 3339; set when the current results were accepted as the reference.

accepted_by.description: Who accepted the last change: `user` or the judge provider.

oneOf.description:
The answer label that made `sparql` the golden query of an `ask`
golden (who, when). Absent: `sparql` is the query of the newest
labeled trace, and the run checks the judged results.

The inputs a run asks an `ask` golden's question with, from the
newest labeled trace.

frozen_at_seq.description: The commit the judgments were last changed at.

id.description:
blake3 of the request words, the query text and entailment (plus
embedding and `top_k` for a search), so a regenerated or
re-added golden keeps its identity and its trend. An `ask` golden
keys on the question alone: its words, its sorted anchors and a
digest of its earlier steps.

judgments.description: The judged results by id: the ground truth.

oneOf.description:
The type of query an `ask` golden expects: the type of its golden
query, else of the newest labeled trace's query.

The route an `ask` golden's question expects, from an answer label:
the label's `route`, else the route of a trace labeled
`valid: true`. A run checks the router's pick against it.

The cut of a `search` golden, from the newest labeled trace: a run
checks only the hits the app shows (relevant ones must show, wrong
ones must not).

trace_ids.description: The most recent traces that labeled into this golden (bounded).

v.description: Golden format version. Currently `2`: judgments per result.

sparql.description:
The SPARQL query, or the query text for `surface: search`. Freezes a
`sparql` or a `search` golden; a question becomes an `ask` golden
through a label on its trace.

GoldenJudgment.description: What a golden knows about one result.

relevant.description:
True: the result answers the request and must keep being returned.
False: the result is wrong and must not come back.

GoldenSuite.description: The suite: one CAS-versioned document per graph.
