GraphActivityResponse.description:
The background work on one graph epoch, as `GET /v1/graph/activity`
reports it.

head_seq.description: The newest commit written to the graph.

idle.description:
True when no item is queued, waiting or running, `publication` is
`current`, and every embedding is `ready` with `lag_commits` 0 or
`failed` (a failed embedding waits for a fix, so no work runs).

items.description:
Queued, waiting and running items first, then finished items. Newest
first in each group. At most 25.

observed_at_micros.description:
Server clock when the route read the state (micros since the Unix
epoch).

published_seq.description:
The newest commit the published RDF generation covers (queries see
it). 0 before the first generation.

target_seq.description: The commit the publication works toward.

write_limit.description:
How close the unpublished commits are to the limit at which the
server refuses new writes (retryable `429 ingest_busy`) until the
index catches up.

GraphAnchor.description:
A structural co-bind constraint: restrict (or boost) the text/vector
candidates to entities within an anchor entity's relation-neighborhood. This
is the engine-native form of the query-conditional channel routing validated
in the Stage-G ablation (quality-ledger R17) — "documents about X AND in the
same group as Y" becomes one snapshot-consistent search rather than a blind
list fusion. The neighborhood is computed from the snapshot-reduced Base
family; final candidates are still re-verified against snapshot visibility.

anchor.description: The anchor entity to expand from.

hops.description: Neighborhood radius in hops (clamped to a small bound; default 2).

oneOf.description: `filter` (hard JOIN) or `boost` (soft). Defaults to `filter`.

relation.description:
Restrict the neighborhood walk to this relation type (by name). `None`
follows every relation.

GraphBindMode.description: How a graph anchor co-binds with the text/vector channels.

GraphCard.description:
WS3 — a per-graph, per-snapshot self-description an agent can inject as prompt
context: the types, relations, properties, and top attribute values that
actually exist, with counts and a freshness watermark. The database writes
its own guaranteed-true few-shot examples. Computed from the ontology,
resident overlay, and BM25 meta — no doc/postings reads — and bounded by
`limits` so it stays small enough to prompt with.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
The last commit written at or before the moment. Absent when the
server cannot place it: `note` says why.

committed_at.description:
When that commit was written, RFC 3339; absent when it records no
time.

first_commit_at.description:
The moment is before the graph's first commit: when that commit was
written (or the graph created), RFC 3339.

moment.description: The moment asked about, RFC 3339 UTC: the end of `date`, or `moment`.

note.description: Why there is no commit, or what to know about the one found.

GraphCommitDryRunResponse.description:
The result of a validate-only commit (`POST /v1/graph/commit?dry_run=true`):
the request is fully validated against the ontology and the active schema and
the would-be effect is reported, but nothing is persisted. A 4xx here is the
same validation error a real commit would raise (unknown type/relation,
unregistered property field, type mismatch), so it is a safe ETL preflight.

dry_run.description: Always true — marks this as a non-persisting preflight.

op_count.description: Number of WAL ops the commit would produce.

oneOf.description: What `replace_owned` would remove.

Active-schema SHACL audit of the prospective commit, when a shape bundle
is active. `conforms=false` means a `reject`-mode commit would be blocked.

skipped_edges.description: Edges that would be skipped as unchanged (idempotent no-ops).

triplets.description: Triplets that would be written, after idempotent skip-unchanged filtering.

written_properties.description:
Property fields that would be written, per entity (canonical names),
resolved against the ontology — the same echo a real commit returns.

GraphCommitRequestBody.description: An absent body version selects legacy. Explicit records/1 selects strict records; no fallback or graph activation.

drain_pressure.description:
R27d(1) advisory WAL drain pressure (0.0–1.0), mirrored from
`commit.drain_pressure`. Present only once the tail is over half full.

oneOf.description: What `replace_owned` removed, mirrored from `commit.owned`.

replayed.description:
Top-level replay signal for idempotency-key collisions/retries. Mirrors
`commit.idempotent_replay` so callers do not have to unwrap the commit
envelope before deciding whether anything new was written.

throttle_ms.description:
R27d(1) advisory pacing telemetry, mirrored from `commit.throttle_ms` to
the envelope top level (like `replayed`) and to the `X-LBB-Throttle-Ms`
response header. Present only past a noise floor; clients SHOULD reduce
write concurrency as it rises.

written_properties.description:
Top-level echo of property fields actually written by this request.
Empty on idempotent replays and no-ops.

deleted_feedback_objects.description:
Always 0: search feedback is reclaimed in the background with the
rest of the graph.

deleted_objects.description:
Objects the request itself removed (the workflow state and history
of the deleted graph). The rest is reclaimed in the background; see
`reclaims`.

reclaims.description:
The background passes that reclaim the deleted graph's storage, one
per branch. Empty when reclaim is turned off on the server.

oneOf.description:
Selected-profile workflow payload cleanup runs on maintenance workers.
Its source-key terminals remain as explicit anti-resurrection metadata.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
Pin the export to a past snapshot: only entities, assertions, and
observations committed at or before this `commit_seq` are emitted. A pin
past the current head is rejected loudly (never clamped), matching the
graph read paths. `None` exports the latest head. This is what makes a
long-running training run's export reproducible — resolve the head once,
then pin every subsequent read to the same `commit_seq` so an N+1 commit
mid-run can never change the training corpus.

snapshot_token.description:
Opaque, self-describing token for the exact snapshot this export reflects
(`tenant:graph:branch:epoch:commit_seq`). Records the exported snapshot's
provenance so a caller can pin subsequent reads to — and verify
reproducibility against — the same point in history.

GraphForkResponse.description:
Response to `POST /v1/graph/fork`: the fork runs as a durable background job
(a create-only copy of the source graph into a new graph id in the same
tenant), so this acknowledges the enqueue and points at the poll surface.

poll.description:
Poll the destination graph's metadata to observe the fork completing
(the destination becomes readable once its head is published).

GraphImportJobAccepted.description: Stable response returned when a durable import is accepted or replayed.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request resolved to an existing job with the same
idempotency key and exact content hash.

GraphImportJobFailure.description:
Terminal failure details for a durable import. The message is safe to expose
to the submitting client; internal object keys and worker identities stay in
structured server logs.

attempts.description: Delivery attempts consumed when the job became terminal.

diagnostic_id.description:
Stable opaque correlation id for server-side logs. It is intentionally
not an object key, worker id, or graph identity.

stage.description: Last durable low-cardinality stage reached by the worker.

GraphImportJobProgress.description: Bounded progress persisted by an import worker after every grouped commit.

GraphImportJobStage.description: Low-cardinality execution stage exposed while a durable import is active.

GraphImportJobState.description:
Lifecycle of a durable NDJSON import submitted through
`POST /v1/graph/import-jobs`.

A succeeded import has durably committed its records and enqueued the final
publication job. It does **not** mean the published read generation has
already caught up to [`GraphImportJobStatus::committed_commit_seq`].

GraphImportJobStatus.description: Queryable status for a durable import job.

oneOf.description:
Final publication enqueue receipt. Presence means publication was
accepted, not that published reads have caught up.

GraphImportLine.description:
One line of an NDJSON bulk-import stream (`POST /v1/graph/import`). Each line
is a single JSON object that is either a triplet (carries `relation`) or an
entity-properties record (carries `properties`); the two shapes are disjoint,
so the importer routes each line by shape. This is the streamable counterpart
of `TripletCommitFile`: a client streams a large dataset line-by-line instead
of buffering one giant commit, and the server batches lines into bounded
internal commits.

GraphImportLineError.description:
A per-line parse/commit failure surfaced by the bulk importer. `line` is the
1-based NDJSON line number. The importer records these and continues (skip the
bad line), unless `strict` is requested.

GraphImportPublishedGenerationOutcome.description:
Durable publication accepted after `POST /v1/graph/import`.
The import request never constructs index families or waits for publication;
clients can poll the returned job while continuing to observe the previously
published generation.

GraphImportResponse.description:
Aggregate outcome of a bulk NDJSON import. `committed_commit_seq` is the
sequence of the last internal batch commit (absent if nothing committed).
`errors` is bounded; `error_count` is the true total even when the list is
truncated. `published_generation` is present when at least one batch
committed; publication is automatic.

idempotency_key.description: The caller key, or the server-minted key when the caller omitted one.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when every internal mutation batch was the already-committed
receipt for this idempotency key.

mutation_receipt_id.description:
Stable identity for the whole multi-batch mutation. Replays return this
exact receipt and the original terminal commit sequence.

observations.description: Exact observation records imported from a full-fidelity export.

GraphListResponse.description: The live, head-backed graphs under a tenant (one stack in SaaS mode).

include_indexes.description:
Opt in to deprecated BM25/ANN family lineage inspection. RDF publication
status is always reported independently; this does not inspect current
class-declared embeddings. HTTP and CLI defaults are false.

index_caught_up.description:
One-shot "has the published RDF base caught up to head?" signal, so a
bulk-import caller does not hand-assemble the predicate.
`Some(true)` iff the validated RDF generation is served at the head commit;
`Some(false)` when publication is still pending or absent. This is
reported even when legacy index inspection is disabled. The optional
representation remains for wire compatibility with earlier servers.

This is a **publication lag** signal, not a statement about index
content, class embedding readiness, or model/configuration coverage.
`include_indexes=true` separately reports legacy BM25/ANN lineage when
present; its watermarks never determine this RDF signal.

published_lag_commits.description: Commit distance from the graph head to its validated published RDF base.

segment_count.description: Compacted snapshot segments referenced by the graph manifest.

GraphRdfImportError.description:
A bounded parse error from RDF bulk import. The RDF parser reports syntax
positions in its message, so this type keeps the wire shape honest instead of
pretending there is always a recoverable line number.

GraphRdfImportPredicate.description:
A predicate discovered while importing RDF through `POST /v1/graph/import/rdf`.
`uri` is the original RDF predicate IRI. `relation` is the fixed
`RDF_TRIPLE` relation used for committed edges, while `lbb_predicate_iri`
remains the source predicate IRI that the RDF/SPARQL projection emits.

GraphRdfImportResponse.description:
Aggregate outcome of an RDF import. Every RDF statement is committed
through a fixed `RDF_TRIPLE` edge; source predicate and literal term metadata
are stored on the edge so the RDF/SPARQL projection can emit source RDF terms
while avoiding one ontology relation/property per source predicate.

GraphReclaimSchedule.description: A background pass that reclaims the storage of a deleted graph branch.

mode.description: `apply` deletes; `plan` only counts what a pass would delete.

not_before.description: RFC 3339. The pass does not start before this time.

GraphReloadResponse.description:
Outcome of `POST /v1/graph/reload` — the declarative "make the graph match
this full dataset" verb. One atomic cutover replaces the whole current state:
records present in the payload are upserted, and entities present at the
pre-reload head but absent from the payload are removed from current state
(retraction semantics — history stays queryable via `?as_of_commit_seq=`).
The delta report is the "prove I don't have wrong data" aid.

The whole reconciliation lands as a single graph-head advance, so a reader
never observes a mixed old/new state: a snapshot pinned at `prior_commit_seq`
sees only the old state, and `new_commit_seq` sees only the new state, with
nothing in between.

dry_run.description:
True when this was a `?dry_run=true` preview: nothing durable changed and
the counts + `new_commit_seq`/`new_snapshot_token` are the *proposed*
effect of a real reload against the same pre-reload head.

edges_added.description: Payload edges not currently present, within the reconciled scopes.

edges_changed.description: Payload edges already present (re-asserted), within the reconciled scopes.

edges_removed.description: Current edges retracted because an endpoint left current state.

entities_added.description: Entities present in the payload but not at the pre-reload head.

entities_changed.description:
Entities present in both the payload and the pre-reload head (re-asserted;
this is a presence intersection, not a deep property diff).

entities_removed.description:
Entities present at the pre-reload head but absent from the payload — the
ones leaving current state.

error_count.description:
Parse errors for malformed payload lines (bounded; `error_count` is the
true total). Mirrors bulk import.

graph_created.description:
True when the target graph did not exist and this reload bootstrapped it
(the pre-reload baseline was empty).

idempotency_key.description:
The idempotency key that scopes this reload's single commit (the caller
key, or a server-minted one).

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request id was already applied (idempotent replay): the
diff counts are reported as zero because nothing new was written.

new_commit_seq.description:
Commit sequence after cutover (real), or the proposed next sequence (dry
run).

new_snapshot_token.description: Snapshot token after cutover (real), or the proposed token (dry run).

no_op.description:
True when the desired state already matched the current state and no
commit was written (real mode only).

prior_commit_seq.description:
Commit sequence of the pre-reload head — the diff baseline and the
rollback anchor.

prior_snapshot_token.description:
Snapshot token of the pre-reload head. Read it back with
`?as_of_commit_seq=<prior_commit_seq>` to see the old state — the rollback
hint.

removed_sample.description:
A bounded sample of the entities leaving current state, as `type/name`
display identities (external keys are one-way-hashed and unrecoverable) —
a sanity aid for confirming the reload drops what you expect.

GraphRetractRequest.description:
Retract specific edges and/or every edge touching given entities. Graph facts
are append-only; a retraction does not erase events but appends a retracting
event that supersedes the matched current edges, so they drop out of
current-state reads (and re-appear in an `as_of` read before the retraction).
This is the surgical alternative to the whole-graph reset for fixing a
wrongly-added fact — e.g. an auto-extracted entity that turned out to be noise.

edges.description:
Specific edges to retract, matched against current edges by
(source, relation, target).

entities.description:
Entities whose every current edge (as source or target) is retracted —
effectively tombstoning the entity from current-state reads. The entity
record itself is retained (append-only) and stays visible in `as_of` reads.

purge_entity_properties.description:
Also clear every stored scalar property (`text`, `acl`, …) of each entity
in `entities`, so the entity has **no current presence** and fully leaves
search AND SPARQL in this one call — the "delete this record" primitive.
Without it, `retract` tombstones edges only; a property-carrying entity
(e.g. a content chunk with an `acl`) stays searchable and ACL-filterable
because presence is `live-edge OR non-empty properties`. Append-only: the
records survive in `as_of` reads; only the current property set is cleared
(a later `commit` can repopulate it). No-op for `edges`-only requests.

edge_event_ids.description: The retracting edge-event ids appended by this request.

idempotent_replay.description:
True when this request id was already applied (idempotent replay); counts
are reported as zero because nothing new was written.

no_op.description: True when nothing matched, so no event was written.

purged_entities.description:
Entities (from `entities`) whose stored properties were cleared by
`purge_entity_properties`. Zero when the flag is unset.

retracted_edges.description: Distinct current edges retracted by this request.

retracted_entities.description: Entities (from `entities`) that had at least one current edge retracted.

pending.description:
At least one exact source-cleanup job has not succeeded. This does not
assert physical closure of every late immutable payload publication.

GroundabilityReport.description:
WS13 — a graph's self-reported groundability: per graph, which completion
mechanisms will carry. Turns the campaign's hand measurements into a
self-service report so a caller can pick narrowing / fine-tuning /
lexical-first without running the experiment.

IdentityMember.description: One record of a [`SuggestedIdentity`], by its import identity.

key.description: Its stable import key (for an integration, `<connection>:<stream>:<id>`).

name.description:
Its current display name. The `SAME_AS` edge names both endpoints, so
a different name would rename the record.

source.description: Display text for the source, for example `hubspot-main contacts`.

IndexLineage.description: Typed convergence view over the persisted serving families.

ann_empty.description:
True when the published ANN family is an empty root. Same meaning as
`bm25_empty`.

oneOf.description:
Watermark the published ANN family is served at. Same caveat as
`bm25_indexed_commit_seq`; read `ann_empty` alongside it.

bm25_empty.description:
True when the published BM25 family is an empty root — the deployment
runs without the search stack
(`LBB_PUBLISH_EMPTY_INDEX_FAMILIES`), or the corpus genuinely has no
indexable documents at this watermark. Either way the family is current
*and* contains nothing, so a health check must not read `caught_up`
alone as "search is serving results".

oneOf.description:
Watermark the published BM25 family is served at. This reports
*publication currency*, not index content: a family published as a
self-identifying empty root is current at this watermark while
containing no documents. Read `bm25_empty` alongside it.

caught_up.description:
Both families are published at the head commit. This is a *publication
lag* signal — it says the derived families have caught up with graph
truth, not that they hold data. An empty family is caught up.

manifest_view_token.description:
Content identity of the head generation plus the exact manifest
views observed while constructing this response.

current_tables.description:
Tables already carrying this accelerator format. This does not promise
expression coverage for every predicate or every query shape.

max_additional_bytes.description: Conservative optional-index output ceiling, excluding root metadata.

source_bytes.description:
Logical bytes of source PSO tables requiring a build; dictionary reads
and metadata are additional. This is not a billing quote.

IndexUpgradeRequest.description: Online upgrades of optional accelerators; RDF truth is never reingested.

dry_run.description: Plan only by default. Set false to enqueue durable maintenance work.

retry_id.description:
Optional operator retry identity, after inspecting a terminal attempt.
For the same starting published root, repeating this identity coalesces
onto the same job.

target.description: Versioned build recipe. Omit to use the current server recipe.

IndexVisibilityFamily.description: One of the index families referenced by an atomic published read root.

IssuedWorkerCredential.description: No Debug implementation: credentials must not appear in diagnostic output.

dim.description: The vector dimension, for an embedding model.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort sent with each call (`low`, `medium`, `high`,
`xhigh`, `max`), for a model that takes one. Absent: the server's
default for the role.

id.description:
The provider's model id (`openai/text-embedding-3-small`,
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, …).

max_price_per_million_usd.description:
Refuse the model when the provider prices it above this (USD per
million tokens); `None` leaves the platform default in force.

ManagedModelCatalog.description:
The catalog: one model per role. A role that is absent falls back to the
server's compiled default.

version.description: Monotonic; every write increments it. `0` for the compiled defaults.

ManagedModelChoice.description:
A model the operator can pick for a role: what the platform knows how
to serve today.

max_input_tokens.description:
The most tokens one input may have (embedding models). The embed job
shortens a longer text, longest values first.

price_per_million_usd.description: USD per million input tokens, for cost estimates.

ManagedModelRole.description: What a managed model is used for.

ManagedModelsPutRequest.description:
Replace the catalog. Every role named here is set; a role left out keeps
the compiled default.

expected_version.description: Refuse the write when the document's version is not this one.

choices.description:
The models the platform can serve per role, for a picker. A catalog
entry may still name a model outside this list.

writable.description:
Whether the caller may write the catalog on this route (single
mode). In SaaS mode the operator writes it through the ops route.

ManagedModelsSource.description: Where the served catalog came from.

ModelActivityDay.description: One feature and model on one day (UTC).

checks.description: Calls of this model a judge checked (`docs/architecture/model-checks.md`).

overruled.description: The judge's row: reviews that corrected the judge.

reviewed.description: The judge's row: checks of this judge people reviewed.

score_milli.description: The sum of the checked calls' ground-truth scores, in thousandths.

wrong.description: Checked calls whose ground truth is `wrong`.

ModelActivityFeature.description: The feature a model call served.

ModelActivityGraph.description:
One feature and model on one graph over the month. `graph` is `*` for
the graphs past the ledger's bound ("other graphs").

checks.description: Calls of this model a judge checked (`docs/architecture/model-checks.md`).

overruled.description: The judge's row: reviews that corrected the judge.

reviewed.description: The judge's row: checks of this judge people reviewed.

score_milli.description: The sum of the checked calls' ground-truth scores, in thousandths.

wrong.description: Checked calls whose ground truth is `wrong`.

ModelActivityManaged.description: The model a feature uses now, from the managed model catalog.

ModelActivityReportEntry.description: One count the SaaS API reports. The counters default to 0.

at_ms.description:
When the calls happened, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: it
selects the day and the month.

ModelActivityReportRequest.description:
`POST /api/admin/model-activity` (database admin token): counts of model
calls the SaaS API made for a stack, at most
[`MODEL_ACTIVITY_REPORT_MAX_ENTRIES`].

accepted.description: Entries taken into the ledger's next write.

ModelActivityResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/activity?month=<yyyy-mm>`: the stack's model activity in
one month, with the model each feature uses now. The answering node adds
the calls it has not written to the ledger yet.

by_workflow.description:
The `workflows` feature per workflow and job. A server from before
2026-10-11 sends none.

months.description: The months with activity, oldest first.

ModelActivityTotal.description: One feature and model over the month.

checks.description: Calls of this model a judge checked (`docs/architecture/model-checks.md`).

cost_micro_usd.description: Estimated cost in millionths of a US dollar.

graphs.description: Graphs with activity (the `*` row of "other graphs" not counted).

items.description: Texts embedded, questions asked, results judged, or runs.

last_at_ms.description: The last activity, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (0: none).

overruled.description: The judge's row: reviews that corrected the judge.

reviewed.description: The judge's row: checks of this judge people reviewed.

score_milli.description: The sum of the checked calls' ground-truth scores, in thousandths.

wrong.description: Checked calls whose ground truth is `wrong`.

ModelActivityWorkflow.description:
One workflow, job and model on one graph over the month: the calls of the
`workflows` feature, per workflow and job. `workflow` is the workflow's
name: a triggered workflow's own calls, and the activity calls a turn of
a named workflow makes (the request's `workflow` names the turn; since
2026-10-21). `@activities` holds the activity calls outside such a turn,
and `*` (with `graph` `*`) the workflows past the ledger's bound. Added
2026-10-11: a month recorded before has no rows.

job.description: The call log's job of the calls (`define`, `resolve`, `reason`, `embed`).

key.description: Object key of the artifact (under the tenant prefix, so purge covers it).

ModelCadenceResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/cadence` — the auto-index doubling policy applied to
models: retraining is due when the graph has doubled since the promoted
run was trained (or when nothing was ever trained).

right.description: The right option's key, given with `no`.

ModelCalibrationAnswerRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/calibration/answer?graph&id`: answer one question. A
later answer replaces the earlier one. `right` only with `no`.

right.description: The right option's key, one of the question's options.

ModelCalibrationAnswerValue.description: A person's answer to "Is the judge right?".

ModelCalibrationApplied.description: The threshold a person applied from a session.

ModelCalibrationApplyRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/calibration/apply?graph&id`: apply a threshold, by
default the session's proposal.

ModelCalibrationBandAccuracy.description: The model's accuracy in one confidence band, against the ground truth.

correct.description: Known units the model got right.

known.description: Sampled units whose ground truth is known.

population.description: Units of the window in the band.

ModelCalibrationBandCount.description:
One confidence band of the population: `[low, high)`, the last
`[0.9, 1]`. A band holds two strata: the units no check disputes, and
the disputed units (their check shows the judge picking another option).

disputed_units.description: Disputed units of the window in the band.

units.description: Units of the window in the band that no check disputes.

workflow.description: For a workflow job: the workflow's name.

ModelCalibrationGateReport.description:
A workflow's gate in a session's report: how often the decisions it
wrote without a person are right, and how often the ones it sent to a
person are.

above.description: At or above the gate: written without a person.

below.description: Below the gate: sent to a person (or dropped).

gate.description:
The gate the sides split at: the workflow's gate when the session
started.

ModelCalibrationGateSide.description: The decisions on one side of a workflow's gate.

correct.description: Known units the model got right.

estimated_accuracy.description: Weighted by stratum, as the thresholds are.

known.description: Sampled units whose ground truth is known.

population.description: Units of the window on this side.

ModelCalibrationJudgeCall.description: One judge call of a session and what it cost.

ModelCalibrationJudgePick.description: The judge's pick of a question, from its check.

probability.description: The judge's probability of its pick.

reason.description: The judge's reason, from its check.

ModelCalibrationJudging.description: How the judging of a session's sample went.

checked_before.description: Calls that had a check before the session.

not_judged.description: Calls left without a check when the judging stopped.

stopped.description: Why the judging stopped early: `budget` or `time`.

ModelCalibrationModelPick.description: The model's pick of a question.

confidence.description:
The number the job's threshold compares: for `route` the pick's
probability (else the answer's confidence), for `fit` the answer's
confidence (else the pick's probability), for a workflow job the
value its gate compares.

ModelCalibrationOption.description: One option of a choice question.

ModelCalibrationOptions.description: What a calibration session runs with, set at its start.

budget_micro_usd.description: The judge cost the session may spend.

ModelCalibrationPopulation.description:
The units a session read from the call log. A unit is one choice question
of one logged call; for a workflow job, one gate decision a workflow
noted on its call (`ModelCall::gates`).

above_gate.description:
For a workflow job: units at or above the workflow's gate, which
were written without a person.

calls.description: Calls with at least one unit.

disputed.description: Units whose check shows the judge picking another option.

limited.description: The read bounds stopped before the start of the window.

without_confidence.description:
Answers without a confidence, or for a workflow job without a gate
decision: left out.

ModelCalibrationQuestion.description: One yes or no question of a session: is the judge right about this unit?

above_gate.description:
For a workflow job: the decision is at or above the workflow's gate,
so it was written without a person.

band.description: The confidence band of the model's pick, 0 to 3.

disputed.description:
The judge's check picked another option than the model before the
session.

id.description: `q1`, `q2`, … in the order the questions are asked.

instructions.description: The question's instructions, at most 500 characters.

options.description: The options a correction picks from.

options_truncated.description: The call had more options than the question keeps.

question.description: The question's id in the call.

ModelCalibrationReport.description: A session's report, computed when it is read.

agreement.description: `agreed / answered`, the judge's agreement with people.

agreement_low.description: The 95% Wilson interval of the agreement.

oneOf.description: For a workflow job: the decisions above and below its gate.

stop_reached.description:
The interval of the agreement is at most 0.1 on each side, or the
answers reached `max_questions`.

thresholds.description:
The candidate thresholds 0.50, 0.55, …, 0.95, from the lowest up.
The walk judges them from 0.95 down; the proposal is the lowest
that passes before the walk stops.

cost_micro_usd.description: The judge cost the session spent.

reason.description:
Why a failed session failed: `no_checker`, `no_calls`,
`no_workflow`, `stale` or `error`.

oneOf.description:
The report, on `GET /v1/models/calibration/get` and after an answer
or an apply.
For a workflow job: the workflow whose gate the session measures.

ModelCalibrationStartRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/calibration?graph`: start a calibration session of one
choice job. `route` and `fit` measure the threshold of the Ask router and
the ontology fit. `resolve`, `infer` and `map` measure the gate of a
workflow and name it in `workflow`: a `documents.link` workflow for
`resolve`, a `values.extract` workflow for `infer`, and for `map` the
`review` workflow that gates the proposals of `documents.map`. Every
field but `job` (and `workflow` for a workflow job) has a default.

budget_usd.description: The judge cost the session may spend, 0 to 100 US dollars; default 10.

max_questions.description: Answers after which the session stops asking, 1 to 120; default 40.

sample_per_band.description: Units sampled per confidence band, 1 to 30; default 15.

since_days.description: Days of the call log the session reads, 1 to 90; default 30.

target_precision.description:
The accuracy a proposed threshold must reach, 0.5 to 0.999. Default:
0.99 for `route` and `fit`; for a workflow job the workflow's
`gate.target_precision` (0.95 when it names none), the target of its
inbox measurement.

workflow.description:
The workflow whose gate a session of `resolve`, `infer` or `map`
measures, by name.

ModelCalibrationThresholdEstimate.description:
The estimated accuracy of the model's picks at or above one threshold,
and what the walk says about it.

automatic_share.description: The share of the population at or above the threshold.

estimated_accuracy.description:
Weighted by stratum (the band, and whether a check disputed the
unit): each known unit counts its stratum's population divided by the
stratum's known sampled units.

interval_low.description:
The low end of the estimate's 95% Wilson interval, at the effective
sample size of the weights.

known.description: Known sampled units at or above the threshold.

tail_high.description:
The tail: the units from the threshold up to 0.1 above it (the
tail that reaches 1 includes 1). Its units, its known sampled units
and their estimated accuracy.

why.description: Why it does not pass, in one sentence.

ModelCalibrationThresholdOutcome.description:
What the walk says about one candidate threshold. The walk goes through
the candidates from 0.95 down, with the rule of the workflow gates
measured from inbox decisions.

ModelCalibrationValidation.description: Whether people validated a session's figures.

ModelCalibrationWorkflow.description: The workflow whose gate a session measures.

gate.description:
Its gate when the session started: decisions at or above it were
written without a person.

name.description: The workflow's name.

at_ms.description: When the call was made, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

attempt.description:
Which attempt of one reading made the call (added 2026-10-27): `2`
for the retry of the `repair` setting of `values.extract`, or of a
`reason` activity call that names it with its `attempt` option.
Absent for the first attempt and for a call that is not one of
several attempts.

oneOf.description:
Why the call used its model (added 2026-10-22): the model choice in
force, in the words of its row (`GET /v1/models/choices`). Calls of
`values.extract` and the activity calls carry it.

gates.description:
The gate decisions a workflow made from the call's answers, by
question id: what the decision states and the value its gate
compares. A calibration session of a workflow job reads them
(`docs/architecture/calibration.md`, "Sessions of a workflow
gate"). Choice calls of `documents.link`, `documents.map` and
`values.extract` carry them; added 2026-10-12.

id.description: `<at_ms:020>-<node>-<seq:010>-<n>`: the batch and the index in it.

input.description:
The provider-neutral request, at most 64 KiB of JSON. A long system
text is stored once and named by its hash (`{"grounding": "<hash>"}`).

output.description: The model's answer, at most 64 KiB of JSON.

sampled.description: The sampler picked the call for a check.

oneOf.description:
`test` for a call of a workflow test, `live` for a workflow's own
work (added 2026-10-20). Absent on calls that name no step, such as
an activity call outside a turn.

step.description:
The step of the workflow that made the call (added 2026-10-20):
`values` or `support` for `values.extract`, the step key the SDK
sends (`workflow.step`) for an activity call inside a turn.

truncated.description: A text or a list was cut to fit the bounds.

use.description:
The model use the call served (added 2026-10-20): `extract` for an
AI step's reasoning call and for a `reason` activity call, `decide`
for a decision call and a `decide` activity call. Calls of
`values.extract` and the activity calls carry it.

ModelCallCheckResponse.description:
`POST /v1/models/calls/check`: the call is queued for a check by the
graph's checks workflow.

ModelCallChoice.description:
Why a logged call used its model (`ModelCall::choice`): the row in force
when the call resolved its model, in the row's words.

fallback.description:
A choice applied and could not serve on the node (no key, or its
record did not read): the call used the next level that could, which
the other fields name.

id.description: The row in force (`mch_…`); absent for a test's model.

ModelCallDetailResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/calls/get`: one call with its groundings as text, and its
check.

ModelCallGate.description: A gate decision a workflow made from one answer of a logged choice call.

pick.description:
The option the decision states: the entry a `documents.link`
mention names (`none_of_these` for no link), the option a
`documents.map` answer chose, `supported` for a value of
`values.extract`.

value.description:
The value the workflow's gate compares, 0 to 1: at or above the gate
the decision is written without a person.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

request_id.description: The HTTP request that made the call.

route.description: The route that made the call (`/v1/search`, `integrations/fit`).

oneOf.description:
The run of a workflow that made the call (added 2026-10-14): a
turn of an engine identity, or a step of the Rust path. Other
origin fields go beside it, never inside.

trace_id.description: The eval trace of the request, when it has one.

workflow.description:
The named workflow the call counts under (added 2026-10-21): the
workflow LBB runs (`starters/<name>`), the workflow whose turn made
an activity call, or the workflow a test names. Absent for a call of
no workflow. The model activity, Evals and the workflow page read
it, not the run's identity.

ModelCallReport.description: One call the SaaS API reports.

confidence.description:
The top decision probability: a call below 0.6 is sampled four times
as often.

truncated.description: The sender cut a text or a list to fit its bounds.

ModelCallReportRequest.description:
`POST /api/admin/model-calls` (database admin token): the calls the SaaS
API made for a stack, at most [`MODEL_CALL_REPORT_MAX_CALLS`].

accepted.description:
Calls taken into the log's next write; 0 for a stack that is gone or
being deleted.

oneOf.description: Why the call used its model (`ModelCall::choice`).

error.description: Why the call failed, at most 160 characters.

instance.description: What the call works on: an instance IRI, or a document's name.

run_id.description:
The run summary's id of the workflow run that made the call
(`origin.run.run_id`).

oneOf.description: `live` or `test` (`ModelCall::scope`).

summary.description:
At most 160 characters: the search text, the question, the stream
name.

oneOf.description: What the call used.

ModelCallRowUsage.description: What one call used, in a list row.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

ms.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds.

ModelCallRun.description:
The run of a workflow that made a call (`origin.run`): the identity and
turn of an engine run, the run summary's id, and what the call works on.

identity.description: The engine identity (`starter.<name>` for a step of the Rust path).

instance.description: What the call works on: an instance IRI, or a document's name.

run_id.description:
The run summary's id (`GET /v1/workflows/named/runs/get`), when the
caller named it.

turn.description: The turn's number; absent for a step of the Rust path.

ModelCallScope.description:
Whether a logged call did a workflow's live work or ran in a workflow
test, which writes nothing (`ModelCall::scope`).

ModelCallShape.description: The shape of a job's input and output, and so of its check.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

model_answer.description:
The model's answer in a few words, when it has a short one: the
options a decision model picked (`lookup`). Absent on older checks.

ModelCheckBrief.description: The check of a call, in a list row.

ModelCheckBudget.description: The stack's check budget of one day (UTC).

ModelCheckJudge.description: What the judge said about a call.

reference.description: The judge's own answer: the grades, its pick, a corrected query.

ModelCheckListResponse.description: `GET /v1/models/checks`: the checks of a month, newest first.

ModelCheckReview.description: What a person said about a check.

reference.description: The person's answer (for a relevance check `{grades: {<id>: 0..3}}`).

oneOf.description: The right verdict, when the review corrects the judge.

ModelCheckReviewRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/checks/review?graph&id`: agree with the check, or
correct it. With `agree: true` no verdict, score or reference; with
`agree: false` the verdict is required.

ModelCheckTruth.description:
The ground truth of a call: the review when there is one, the judge's
verdict otherwise.

ModelChecksSummary.description: `GET /v1/models/checks/summary`: the graph's checks in one month.

calls.description: Model calls logged this month for the graph.

checker_available.description: The node can check calls (the checker model is configured).

months.description: The months with a summary, oldest first.

ModelChoice.description:
The choice of one use in one scope. A list gives the environment's rows
and the workflows' own; with `workflow` it gives the row in force for
each use of that workflow.

by.description:
Who set it (`account:<id>`, `key:<key id>`, `token`); `null` for a
default row.

choosable.description: A person can choose the use's model (`false` for `embed`).

created.description: When the row was first set, RFC 3339; `null` for a default row.

oneOf.description:
The use's default model: what a delete of the environment's row goes
back to.

experiment.description:
The experiment whose B a person applied with this choice (`exp_…`,
added 2026-10-26); absent when the model was set otherwise.

graph.description: The graph of a `workflow` row; `null` for the environment.

id.description:
`mch_` and 24 hex characters (a hash of the scope and the use).
Opaque: the same scope and use keep it.

oneOf.description: The model the use runs: absent when the server runs no model for it.

options.description:
The models the use can run on this server, with their efforts, list
prices and whether the server holds their key.

oneOf.description: The model before the last change.

since.description: When the model was set, RFC 3339; `null` for a default row.

workflow.description: The workflow of a `workflow` row; `null` for the environment.

ModelChoiceDeleted.description:
`DELETE /v1/models/choices`: the choice was removed, and the use runs the
next level. A delete of no choice, or repeated, answers the same.

id.description: The row's id (`mch_…`).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

ModelChoicePutRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/models/choices`: choose the model of a use, for the
environment, or for one workflow of the graph (`workflow`).

experiment.description:
An experiment whose B this write applies (`exp_…`, added
2026-10-26): its model change for `use` on `workflow`. The write
checks that the workflow still runs the experiment's A (409
`experiment_outdated`); when it runs B already, it changes nothing.
The row then names the experiment.

model.description: One of the row's `options`, with an effort it takes.

workflow.description: A named workflow of the graph; absent for the environment.

signal_from_seq.description: Signal-bus range the training examples were drawn from (commit seqs).

synthetic_fraction.description: Fraction of examples that were execution-verified synthetic pairs.

ledger_ref.description: Pointer into the quality/perf ledger row that gates promotion.

ModelJob.description: What LBB used a model for. Every call has one job.

ModelJobQuality.description: One job and model over a month of checks.

score.description: The mean ground-truth score; 0 when no checks.

ModelJudgeQuality.description: The judge over a month of checks.

agreement.description: `(reviewed - overruled) / reviewed`; absent before any review.

ModelRegistryResponse.description: `GET /v1/models/registry` — the runs of one kind, newest first.

current.description: The promoted run number, when a `CURRENT` pointer exists.

base_model.description:
The base model this run derives from (e.g. `bge-small-en-v1.5`,
`Qwen3-1.7B`); free-form but stable within a kind.

promoted.description: Advisory at write time; promotion truth is the CAS `CURRENT` pointer.

recipe_id.description:
The training/derivation recipe identifier (searchable; the flywheel
driver hill-climbs recipe space).

oneOf.description:
Reserved post-quantum signature envelope (SLH-DSA; ECC forbidden for
these artifacts). `null` until signing lands — the field exists from
day one so signed and unsigned manifests share one schema.

source_job_id.description:
Durable background job that produced this run. The server assigns this
from the queue's stable job ID so redelivery returns the same run.

ModelRunView.description:
One registry entry as reads report it: the manifest plus its run number
and the *effective* promotion state (from the `CURRENT` pointer, not the
manifest's advisory flag).

ModelServingDefaults.description:
The serving defaults derived from promoted model runs, pinned to the
graph head like the embedding config (`model_defaults_ref`). One object
serves every in-process kind; promotion truth stays the registry's
`CURRENT` pointer — this is its read-optimized projection. **[PIN]**
field names (persisted object).

oneOf.description:
Extractor adapter serving default (a LoRA adapter on the resident
model's volume); resident extraction passes it per generate call.

ModelSplitAudit.description:
`GET /v1/models/split-audit` — makes the WS9 temporal-split obligation
checkable: a trainer MUST train on data ≤ `trained_at_commit_seq` and
evaluate on data > it; the manifest records the lineage window so this
audit can verify it after the fact.

lineage_respects_split.description:
The lineage window closes at or before the split pin
(`signal_to_seq ≤ trained_at_commit_seq`).

split_within_history.description: The split pin lies within the graph's history (`≤ head`).

ModelSwitch.description:
A task whose model a person switched on one graph, after a trial of the
model met the bar.

model.description: The model the task uses on the graph.

oneOf.description: The model it used before the switch.

trial.description: The trial that met the bar, and its report at the switch.

ModelSwitchRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/switches?graph`: switch a task to the candidate of a
trial that meets the bar.

ModelThreshold.description: The applied threshold of one job.

validated.description: People validated the session when it was applied.

ModelThresholdsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/thresholds?graph`: the graph's applied thresholds of the
`route` and `fit` jobs. A workflow's gate is its own setting.

ModelTrainingConfig.description:
Per-graph automatic-training configuration, stored as one small CAS
object under the graph prefix (purged with the tenant). **[PIN]** field
names. Default: off — training never starts without an explicit opt-in.

auto_train.description: Master switch for cadence-triggered training. Off by default.

kinds.description:
Which [`TRAINABLE_KINDS`] the cadence loop may train. Empty with
`auto_train: true` means "all trainable kinds".

budget_micro_usd.description:
The candidate's, the current model's (on calls another model made)
and the checker's cost the trial may spend.

calls.description: The compared calls, newest call first. Empty in a list.

oneOf.description:
The model the task used on the graph when the trial started: the
switched model, else the catalog's. The candidate is compared with
it on every call.

current_cost_micro_usd.description: The current model's cost on the calls it answered again.

id.description: `<created_ms:020>-<8 hex>`.

skipped.description:
Checked calls the trial could not compare: no usable ground truth, an
input the candidate cannot answer.

until_ms.description: The trial collects new checks until this time.

ModelTrialAnswer.description: One model's answer to a compared call.

brief.description:
The answer in a few words: a decision's picks, the first items of an
order, the first words of an answer.

error.description: Why there is no answer: `refused`, `failed`, `no answer`.

score.description: 0 to 1; absent when the model did not answer.

oneOf.description: Absent when the model did not answer.

current.description:
The model the task uses: the call's own answer when that model made
the call, else its answer to the call again (`replayed`).

judge_cost_micro_usd.description:
The checker's cost for the candidate's answer, and for the current
model's when it answered again (`ask`).

pinned.description: `ask`: the candidate's queries read the commit the original read.

reason.description: The checker's reason about the candidate's answer (`ask`).

replayed.description:
Another model made the call (before a switch, say), so the model the
task uses answered it again for this comparison.

truth.description: The ground truth of the call's check when the trial compared it.

ModelTrialCallResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/trials/call?graph&id&call`: one compared call with the
call itself, its check and the candidate's answer.

answer.description:
The candidate's answer: `output` in the shape of the call's output,
`steps` for `ask`, and `current` (its own `output` and `steps`) when
the model the task uses answered the call again.

oneOf.description: The logged call (long system texts as text); absent when it is gone.

ModelTrialCandidate.description: A model a trial can test on a job.

available.description: This server holds the provider's key.

efforts.description: The efforts it takes, lowest first; empty for a model without one.

price_in_per_million_usd.description: USD per million input and output tokens, when known.

switchable.description:
A trial of it that meets the bar can switch the task to it: the task
can run on this provider (`ask`: Claude; `route`: Jev).

ModelTrialJobOption.description: One job a trial can run on.

checked.description: Checked calls of the last three months a trial can compare.

oneOf.description:
The model the job uses on this graph now: its switch, else the model
of its newest checked call, else the catalog's.
The catalog's model: what a revert goes back to.
The switch of the job on this graph, when a person made one.

ModelTrialListResponse.description: `GET /v1/models/trials?graph`: trials, newest first, without their calls.

ModelTrialModel.description: A model: the candidate of a trial, or the model a job uses now.

effort.description:
The reasoning effort sent with each call (`low` … `max`), for a model
that takes one.

available.description: Trials can run here: workflows are on and the catalog has a checker.

calls.description: Calls both models answered and the trial scored.

cost_ratio.description:
The candidate's cost per call over the current model's; absent when
the current model's cost is 0.

delta.description: Mean of candidate score − current score.

qualifies.description:
The candidate meets the quality threshold: at least 20 calls, `ci_low`
at or above −0.05, a failure share at most 0.05 above the current
model's, and cheaper per call or `better`.

ModelTrialSide.description: One model's figures over the compared calls.

cost_micro_usd_per_call.description: The mean model cost of one call, in millionths of a US dollar.

failed.description: Calls the model did not answer (an error, a refusal, no answer).

ms_p50.description: The median latency of one call.

right.description: The share of calls whose answer is right, 0 to 1.

ModelTrialSkippedJob.description: A job a start did not test, and why.

days.description: Days to collect new checks, 1 to 30; default 14.

jobs.description:
The jobs to test it on; absent: every job it can do that has checked
calls.

target.description: Calls to compare per trial, 1 to 100; default 40.

ModelTrialStartResponse.description:
The answer to a start: the trials (an open trial of the same job and
candidate is answered as it is), and the jobs left out.

ModelUse.description:
A use of a model: the model slot a call fills. The call log names it on
each call (`ModelCall::model_use`, wire name `use`).

NameSemantics.description:
Whether entity names look like natural language (embeddings will carry) or
opaque identifiers (a hash/lexical approach fits better).

sampled.description: Entity names sampled for the heuristic.

key.description:
Optional stable external key. When set, entity identity is `(type, key)`
and `name` is just a display label — so a later rename keeps the same
entity, and two records that share a name stay distinct by key (e.g. two
"Cambridge" universities in a relational import). Omit it to keep the
default `(type, name)` identity. To attach properties or embeddings to a
keyed entity, set the same `key` on those inputs.

active_revision.description:
The settings revision the workflow runs on (`wrev_…`):
`GET /v1/workflows/named/revisions` lists its history, and
`POST /v1/workflows/named/revisions/activate` moves it.

created.description: When it was created, RFC 3339 (the same as `created_at`).

details.description:
The workflow's own status, on a read of one workflow (`?name=`): for a
workflow your worker runs `DeveloperWorkflowDetails` (the message in
flight, the instances waiting); for LBB's own its steps' status (the
documents of `documents.link`, the properties of `values.extract`).
A list and a workflow with a content trigger leave it out.

oneOf.description: The fan-in identity, when the workflow has one.

name.description:
The workflow's id: unique on the graph, and the key of every
`/v1/workflows/named*` route.

on_exhausted.description:
What a turn of a shard that failed for good does: absent while
`block`.

route_by.description: The routing field as given; absent: the instance IRI.

runs_in.description:
`worker`: your worker runs the turns. `lbb`: LBB runs the work in
the starters job (the Rust path of this release).

shard_states.description: The shards of a workflow your worker runs; empty for LBB's own.

starter.description:
The starter workflow it was made from: `workflow` for a workflow of
your worker, a catalog id (`documents.parse`, `values.extract`, …)
for LBB's own.

status.description: The status shape of every workflow (as `/v1/workflows/triggered`).

window.description:
The send-ahead window; absent: the inbox limit (a workflow made
through `/v1/workflows/triggered`).

workflow.description:
The target: the workflow type and version that receive the work.
LBB's own are `lbb.*` types.

NamedWorkflowFanIn.description: The fan-in identity of a workflow and what the engine holds for it.

id.description: The id word (`fan_in` of the request).

NamedWorkflowList.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/named`: the graph's workflows, by name, in the list
envelope (`limit` 1 to 200, default 100; `cursor`). A request with
`Lbb-Version` before 2026-10-21 gets the earlier shape: every workflow
in `workflows`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

NamedWorkflowQueue.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/named/queue?name=&trigger=&cursor=&limit=`: what a
watch has not sent yet, with origins, the pass in progress, and per
shard its unfinished turns and its running turn's progress. The items
are a page in the list envelope; the other fields describe the queue. A
request with `Lbb-Version` before 2026-10-21 gets the earlier shape:
`items` and an integer `next_after` in place of `object`, `data`,
`has_more` and `next_cursor`.

data.description:
From the position `cursor` names, at most `limit` (1 to 100, default
50): instances first, then removed instances, in send order.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page. The
queue moves as it drains, so a page is a view at one time.

pending.description:
Items waiting to be sent (instances and removed instances), on this
page or not. A workflow LBB runs reads its items from this queue
itself.

processed_through_seq.description: The published commit the watch read through.

shards.description: The shards of a workflow your worker runs; empty for LBB's own.

NamedWorkflowRequest.description:
Create a workflow with triggers, or change one (`PUT
/v1/workflows/named`). The same request again is a no-op. The target is
a workflow type of your worker; LBB's own types (`lbb.*`) are made from a
starter workflow (`PUT /v1/workflows/triggered`) in this release.

batch.description:
Instances per message, 1 to 64 (default 16). A content trigger sends
one content per message (`batch` 1 or absent).

budget_usd_per_month.description:
The workflow's own monthly budget of model calls, in US dollars: the
activities its turns call (`reason`, `decide`, `embed`) answer `429
workflow_budget_exceeded` with `retry_at` once the month's spend
reaches it. The stack's budget of the workflow's kind applies too.
Absent: no budget of its own.

fan_in.description:
The workflow's fan-in identity (dogfooding design §3.3 G9): one more
engine identity of the workflow's type, `starter.<name>.<fan_in>`,
that the shards' turns send to (a catalogue, the things of a
linking). `[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}`. Send with deterministic message
ids (`generated-<sha256>-<version>`, `decided-<shard>-<turn>`): a
repeat is admitted once. It is paused, resumed and woken with the
shards, its runs and blobs file under the workflow, and its model
calls count against the workflow's budget. Absent: none.

oneOf.description:
What a turn of a shard that failed for good does: `block` (the
default) holds the shard's inbox until a person retries or skips it;
`skip` keeps the failed turn in the history and goes on. Each shard
takes a change at the watch's next send to it.
The outputs your code owns.

route_by.description:
A field of the watched class (one step of the path syntax) whose
value is the routing key: the changes of one key go to one shard, in
order. Absent: the instance IRI. A content trigger routes by the
content's SHA-256 and takes no `route_by`.

shards.description:
Engine identities that receive the messages, 1 to 16. Default 1.
A change needs every shard's inbox empty (`409 workflow_shards_busy`).

triggers.description:
Exactly one trigger in this release: a watch, a content trigger, a
schedule or a stream, and a review trigger beside it. A workflow keeps its
trigger's kind; to change it, delete the workflow and create it
again.

window.description:
Messages the watch keeps queued per shard, 1 to 128. Default 4; the
rest waits in the watch's queue.

workflow.description: The workflow type and version that receive the messages.

queued.description: The starters job was asked to run.

NamedWorkflowShard.description:
One shard of a workflow: its engine identity, the watch's cursor for it,
and what the engine holds (when the server could read it).

oneOf.description: The message the watch wrote down and sends next.

inbox_full_since.description: The inbox was full (128 messages) at the last send, since this time.

next_message.description:
The number of the next message id (`starter-<name>-<n>`,
`starter-<name>.<k>-<n>`).

oneOf.description: The progress of its running turn, when it follows the convention.

The engine's status of the identity; absent before its first
message or without the engine.

window_full_since.description:
The send-ahead window was full at the last run, since this time: the
rest waits until a turn finishes.

NarrowRelationOp.description:
Remove entity types from a relation's domain and/or range (a subtractive
change). Conflicts when current edges of the relation already use a
removed source/target type — those edges stay (append-only) but begin to
warn. Blocked until those edges are migrated or retracted.

NarrowingRecall.description:
Whether the graph's own entities are retrievable by their names — a proxy
for "will narrowing/retrieval carry". Computed by self-querying a sample and
checking top-10 membership; no LLM.

OntologyChangeSuggestion.description: A durable, reviewable ontology change suggestion.

accepted_links.description: How many `SAME_AS` edges the accept wrote.

accepted_ontology_version.description: The ontology version the accepted change produced.

change.description:
The evolve operations that accepting applies, in order. May be empty
when `identities` or `facts` is not.

change_sources.description:
For an edited change: for each op of `change`, the index of the op in
`proposed_change` it was edited from, or null for an op the person
added. Lets a producer map its proposal onto what was accepted.

decided_by.description: Who accepted, dismissed or superseded it, when, and why.

oneOf.description: Graph facts that accepting commits after `change` applies.
The commit of the facts, once accepted.

What the producer wrote after the accept, when it writes the facts
itself (the `review` workflow).

identities.description: Records to link as one identity after `change` applies.

oneOf.description:
The last dry run of `change` against the ontology, or the result of
accepting it. `impact.base_ontology_version` below the graph's current
ontology version means the dry run is out of date.

impact_error.description: Why the last dry run failed (for example an unknown class).

key.description:
The producer's idempotency key. Creating again with the same key
updates this suggestion instead of adding another one.

mapping.description:
Opaque to the server: how the origin applies the change to its own
configuration once accepted (for an integration, its mapping changes).

proposed_change.description:
The operations as the producer proposed them, kept when a person edited
`change` before accepting.

oneOf.description:
The facts as the producer proposed them, kept when a person left
some out before accepting (`facts` then holds the accepted ones).

proposed_identities.description:
The identities as the producer proposed them, kept when a person
removed some before accepting.

oneOf.description:
The review part of an item filed through `/v1/reviews`: its kind,
question and answer. Absent on a plain suggestion (kind `change`).

revision.description: Starts at 1 and grows each time the producer revises the change.

OntologyChangeSuggestionAcceptRequest.description:
Accept a suggestion: apply its change to the current ontology, then link
its identities.

change.description: An edited change that replaces the proposed one ("edit, then accept").

change_sources.description:
With `change`: for each of its ops, the index of the proposed op it was
edited from, or null for an added op. Same length as `change`; each
index at most once.

comment.description: Added to the discussion with the acceptance.

oneOf.description:
The facts to commit, when a person left some out: each triplet and
each `entity_properties` row must be one of the proposed facts,
exactly as proposed (any other fact is refused with 400: an accept
never adds a fact), and the rows that `required` names must stay.
The other fields come from the proposed facts. Absent commits every
proposed fact.

identities.description:
The identities to link, when a person removed some or some members:
each must be a subset of a proposed identity, with at least two
members. Absent links every proposed identity.

OntologyChangeSuggestionCommentRequest.description: Add a comment to a suggestion's discussion.

OntologyChangeSuggestionCreateRequest.description:
Create a suggestion, or update the one with the same `key`.

Update rules for an existing key: an `open` suggestion takes the new
content (a different `change` raises `revision`); an `accepted` one is
returned unchanged; a `dismissed` one stays dismissed unless `change`
differs, which reopens it; a `superseded` one reopens.

oneOf.description: Defaults to the ontology as a whole.

change.description:
Up to 128 evolve operations; at least one unless `identities` or
`facts` is set (then it may be empty).

oneOf.description: Graph facts to commit on accept, after `change` applies.

identities.description: Up to 200 identities to link on accept.

key.description:
Idempotency key, at most 255 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9-_.:/]`, for
example `hubspot-main/deals`. When absent the server derives one from
`anchor`, `change` and (when set) `identities` and `facts`, so the same
suggestion is filed once.

mapping.description: Opaque origin data, at most 16 KiB of JSON.

rationale.description: Why the change is needed. At most 4,000 characters.

title.description:
Short imperative text, for example "Add class Deal". At most 200
characters.

OntologyChangeSuggestionDecisionRequest.description: Dismiss (a person) or supersede (the producer) a suggestion.

truncated.description:
More suggestions matched than `limit` allowed, or this read did not
cover every suggestion (more than 10,000, or some left to the next).

OntologyChangeSuggestionStatus.description: Where a suggestion is in its review.

OntologyChangeSuggestionSummary.description:
One row of a suggestion list: everything but the evidence samples, the
mapping and the discussion text.

oneOf.description: The batch decision that decided it, when a batch did.

confidence.description:
The lowest confidence of its evidence samples (`confidence`,
`support` or `probability`), from 0 to 1.

fact_count.description:
How many triplets and entity property rows the suggestion's facts
hold.

identity_count.description: How many identities the suggestion links.

oneOf.description: What it asks a person to decide; the server always sets it.

For a link review of `documents.link`: where the link goes from and
to, and what the model answered.
The suggestion's pattern; the server always sets it.

publishable.description: Whether the last dry run can be published; absent before any dry run.

rationale.description:
The start of the rationale, at most 300 characters (cut at a word,
with `…`); the suggestion holds all of it.

oneOf.description:
The review part of an item filed through `/v1/reviews`, with its
first quote only and long question texts cut to 300 characters.
Absent on a plain suggestion (kind `change`).
Where the evidence comes from, when a sample names a document.

OntologyConflict.description:
A current-data conflict found while previewing a subtractive ontology change.
Reported back so the caller can decide whether to re-run with
`allow_data_conflicts` (which keeps the affected records — Little Big Brain never
rewrites or drops them — and applies the change in warn mode).

affected.description: How many current records the change would orphan/flag.

samples.description: Bounded deterministic examples. `affected` remains the exact count.

OntologyDefineRequest.description:
Define the scoped graph's ontology. Imports `source` (any
[`crate`]-supported format), optionally merges the built-in default so the
standard entity types/relations stay available, and creates the graph head
with the result.

The call is re-runnable on a graph that already exists. An unchanged
ontology is a no-op; an additive difference is applied, including a widened
relation domain or range and a new property field; a narrowing or removing
difference is refused with a typed error naming the route that applies it.

dry_run.description:
Preview the exact definition without creating a graph, writing an
ontology object, or changing the graph head. Equivalent to the
`?dry_run=true` query parameter; either signal enables preview mode.

format.description: Import format hint. `auto` (the default) sniffs the content.

merge_default.description:
Merge the built-in `default_ai_context_ontology()` underneath the
imported types so the standard AI-context vocabulary stays available.

source.description:
Ontology document text: Little Big Brain JSON, JSON-LD, Turtle/N3, RDF/XML, or
CSV/TSV. Detected from `format` (default `auto`).

changed.description:
True when this call wrote a new ontology version, or when a dry run
predicts that it would. False when the proposed ontology already matched
the active one, which is what makes re-running the same bootstrap request
a no-op.

A widened relation domain or range and a new property field both set it,
even though neither appears in the class-and-relation schema diff.

changes.description:
The additive changes this call applied, or would apply during a dry run,
to an existing graph's ontology. Empty on create and no-op.

dry_run.description: True when this response is a preview and no durable state changed.

graph_created.description:
True when this call created the graph head, or when a dry run predicts
that the real definition would create it.

OntologyDraft.description: Durable, portable ontology review artifact owned by the graph database.

OntologyDraftCreateRequest.description: Create a reviewable induction artifact without inserting samples into the graph.

OntologyEntityTypeView.description: The full definition of one entity type (class) in the active ontology.

iri.description: Canonical query IRI minted by Little Big Brain for this class identity.

resolvable.description: True when instances of this type can be resolved from free-text mentions.

stable_id.description:
Frozen class identity used by commits and the RDF projection. This is
unique even when imported vocabularies reuse the same local name.

super_types.description:
Direct parent classes (`rdfs:subClassOf`), named by their frozen
`stable_id`s. Clients can build the full class lattice without a SPARQL
scan or a second ontology lookup.

evidence_ref.description: Stable connector/source reference; sample content is never used as identity.

record.description:
Representative connector record. Objects enable deterministic property
inference; other JSON values remain evidence examples.

OntologyEvolveOp.description:
One additive ontology change for [`OntologyEvolveRequest`]. Additive by
construction — it widens a relation's domain/range or declares a new entity
type, but never narrows or removes — so every record written under an earlier
version stays valid (its positional type/relation ids are preserved). This is
the supported "ontology evolution" path; identity-breaking changes (removals,
narrowing) still require an explicit expand→migrate→contract plan.

Every variant rejects unknown fields: a misspelled field fails the request
with `400 invalid_request` instead of reading as an empty change.

OntologyEvolveRequest.description:
Apply a list of additive ontology changes in order, writing a new ontology
version when anything actually changes. Ops are applied against the
in-progress ontology, so an `add_entity_type` earlier in the list is visible
to a later `widen_relation`.

allow_data_conflicts.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. Conflicting subtractive changes are
always rejected with structured conflicts until affected data is
migrated or retracted; setting this field no longer bypasses that gate.

applied.description:
The changes actually applied (empty on a no-op, or when a conflicting
subtractive request was rejected without `allow_data_conflicts`).

conflicts.description:
Current-data conflicts from subtractive ops. When non-empty and the
request did not set `allow_data_conflicts`, nothing was written and
`ontology_version` is unchanged.

dry_run.description:
True when this response came from `?dry_run=true` and no ontology object
or graph-head update was written.

no_op.description:
Every requested operation was already satisfied, so publishing would not
create a new ontology version.

ontology_version.description:
Active version after a publish, or the predicted resulting version for a
dry run. Equal to `base_ontology_version` for a no-op or blocked preview.

publishable.description:
Whether the exact request can be published. False for every
data-conflicting subtractive preview.

OntologyPropertyView.description: A typed property on an entity type, as declared in the active ontology.

allowed_values.description:
The field's enforced allowed-value set (`sh:in`), if any — a commit whose
value is outside it is rejected at write time. Empty/absent means the
field accepts any value of its type.

unit.description:
The unit an `i64` or `f64` field holds its numbers in (`mm`, `cm`,
`kg`, `m2`, …), absent when none is declared. Writers that read text,
such as `values.extract`, convert a number to this unit.

value_type.description:
Lowercase value type: bool | i64 | f64 | datetime | keyword | text |
bytes | vector_f32 | keyword_set | i64_set. The `*_set` types hold a
sorted, deduplicated member set filterable by membership
(`overlaps`/`contains_all`/`not_overlaps`).

OntologyRelationView.description:
The full definition of one relation type (predicate) in the active ontology,
with domain/range resolved to entity-type names so the schema renders without
a second lookup.

dst_types.description: Range — entity-type names this relation can point to (empty = any).

edge_count.description:
Number of current (reduced) edges of this relation in the served snapshot,
when the caller asked for population counts (`GET /v1/ontology?counts=true`).
`0` flags a declared-but-unused relation; `None` (field omitted) means the
count was not requested — the default cheap response skips the snapshot
load. Lets an agent see at a glance which of many declared relations
actually carry edges.

src_types.description: Domain — entity-type names this relation can originate from (empty = any).

exact_types.description:
When false (default), an `entity_types` constraint is satisfied by the
named type *or any subtype* (`rdfs:subClassOf` closure). When true, only
the exact declared type matches — the exact-match escape hatch.

OntologyStarterAdds.description: What applying a starter would change now.

widened_relations.description:
Relations the graph has that lack some of the starter's domain or
range classes.

OntologyStarterApplyRequest.description: Apply a starter to the scoped graph.

dry_run.description: Answer what applying would do without writing anything.

expected_ontology_version.description: Refuse with `409 conflict` when the graph's ontology version differs.

OntologyStarterApplyResponse.description: The result of applying a starter.

applied_ops.description: The evolve operations this call ran, or would run in a dry run.

no_op.description:
True when the graph already held the whole starter: nothing was (or,
in a dry run, would be) written.

ontology_version.description: The ontology version after the call, or the predicted one in a dry run.

status.description: The starter's status after the call, or the predicted one in a dry run.

OntologyStarterClass.description:
A class of a starter. LBB does not scope properties to classes:
`properties` is a hint for the fit and the docs.

equivalents.description: Equivalent or closest terms in public vocabularies, as CURIEs.

keys.description:
Properties whose value identifies one real thing across sources. No
ontology operation holds them yet.

name.description: PascalCase.

properties.description:
The properties records of this class carry, beyond its parents' and
the shared ones.

superTypes.description: Direct parents, declared earlier in the starter.

OntologyStarterConflict.description:
A term the graph holds differently from the starter. Applying would keep
the graph's version silently, so `apply` refuses while one exists.

name.description: The term's name in the starter.

starter.description:
What the starter declares, for example `keyword` or
`many_to_one, inverse EMPLOYS`.

OntologyStarterConflictKind.description: The kind of term a conflict is about.

OntologyStarterDetail.description:
`GET /v1/ontology/starters/detail`: one starter's document, its status and
the operations applying it would run now.

missing_ops.description:
The evolve operations applying the starter would run now: what the
graph lacks, with a relation the graph has widened instead of added.

ontology_version.description: Null when the graph does not exist yet.

OntologyStarterDocument.description:
A starter as the JSON document the data plane embeds
(`database/crates/lbb-ontology/starters/<id>.json`).

id.description: Stable id, for example `crm`.

ops.description: The evolve operations that create the starter on an empty graph.

shared.description: Properties every record of every class may carry (provenance).

sources.description: The connector kinds that map to this starter, for example `hubspot`.

version.description: Semantic version. A major change renames or removes terms.

OntologyStarterList.description: `GET /v1/ontology/starters`: every starter with its status on the graph.

ontology_version.description:
The graph's ontology version; null when the graph does not exist yet
(every starter is then `absent`).

OntologyStarterPresent.description: How many of a starter's terms the graph holds.

OntologyStarterProperty.description: A property of a starter. Properties are global: one name, one value type.

equivalent.description: The schema.org (or other) term it corresponds to, as a CURIE.

name.description: snake_case.

OntologyStarterQuestion.description:
A question the starter's ontology must answer, with the terms an answer
needs.

id.description: For example `crm-01`.

sparql.description: The SPARQL that answers it, when one exists.

domain.description: Class names the relation goes from.

inverse.description: The name of the reverse direction.

name.description: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.

range.description: Class names the relation goes to.

OntologyStarterState.description: How much of a starter a graph holds.

OntologyStarterStatus.description: A starter compared with a graph's ontology.

OntologyStarterUpdateRequest.description:
File the operations a graph lacks of a starter as one ontology change
suggestion.

OntologyStarterUpdateResponse.description: The suggestion a starter update filed.

created.description:
True when this call filed the suggestion; false when it existed
already (it may have been revised) or nothing was needed.

suggestion_id.description: The suggestion's id; null when the graph already holds the starter.

OntologySuggestionBatchRequest.description:
`POST /v1/ontology/suggestions/accept-batch` and `/dismiss-batch`: one
decision for many suggestions, each decided as the single route decides
it.

pattern.description:
The pattern the person decided (`SuggestionPattern::key`), recorded
