The promoted `fusion` model run whose trained weights served as this
search's channel-weight defaults (WS9 trainer loop). `None` when the
graph has no promoted fusion run or the request pinned an explicit
profile — so a client can label a ranking "trained (run N)" vs
"profile defaults" honestly.

vector_model_id.description:
The embedding model the vector leg actually searched: `Some(model_id)` for
a real-embedding space (a graph's managed `Stored` model or client-supplied
`ExternalVectors`), `None` for the char-trigram hash space (or when the
vector leg was disabled). Lets a client label the vector row honestly —
"real embeddings · {model}" vs "auto-derived from text (hash)".

SetPropertyConstraintOp.description:
Set (or clear) the enforced allowed-value set on an **existing** property
field — the tightening path for a field already in use (e.g. constrain
`status` to its ADR vocabulary). A non-empty list installs the `sh:in`
constraint that future commits are checked against; an empty list clears
it. Enforcement is write-time only: values already stored are not
retroactively validated. Errors on an unknown field or a non-enumerable
type. Bumps the ontology version.

allowed_values.description: Canonical allowed values; empty clears the constraint.

property.description: Name of the existing property field to constrain.

SetPropertyUnitOp.description:
Set (or clear, with no `unit`) the unit of an **existing** `i64` or
`f64` property field. Metadata only: stored values are not converted,
so change a unit only to state what the values already are. Errors
on an unknown field, a field that is not a number, or a unit LBB does
not know. Bumps the ontology version.

property.description: Name of the existing property field.

unit.description: The unit's symbol (see `add_property`); absent clears it.

SetRelationCardinalityOp.description:
Change a relation's cardinality (`one_to_one` | `one_to_many` |
`many_to_one` | `many_to_many`). A narrowing transition is checked
against the exact current reduced edge projection before publication.
Once accepted, the declared cardinality is enforced on future commits.

SetRelationInverseOp.description:
Set (or replace) a relation's inverse-relation display name, enabling
one-hop reverse lookup (e.g. `PHASE_OF` for `HAS_PHASE`). Metadata
only — never touches stored edges.

hit_rate_at_k.description: Fraction of labeled queries whose expected entity appeared in top-k.

mrr_at_k.description: Mean reciprocal rank of the first expected target in top-k.

recall_at_k.description: Mean fraction of each query's expected targets recovered in top-k.

ShadowEvalRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/shadow-eval` — champion vs challenger retrieval over the
same pinned snapshot: the challenger is a search configuration (a
challenger embedding run's space, different weights, a profile), replayed
against the same queries the champion serves. Promotion stays a decision
on this evidence — the endpoint never promotes.

oneOf.description: Champion arm search options; `None` = the graph's serving defaults.

gate.description:
Fail-closed promotion verdict over the same labeled queries and pinned
snapshot. Requires quality non-regression plus p50/p95/p99 latency
ratios within the configured ceiling; this endpoint still never
performs the promotion itself.

labeled.description: Labeled queries (those with `expected`) the hit rates are over.

ShadowQuery.description:
One shadow-eval probe: a query and (optionally) the entity names that
count as a hit. Pairs come from captured signals, hand-written evals, or
the execution-verified synthetic generator.

overlap_at_k.description: |champion ∩ challenger| / k over the returned top-k names.

SignalEnvelope.description:
The stored form, one JSON object per NDJSON line. **[PIN]** the field set
(`v`, `kind`, `ts`, `request_id`, `snapshot_token`, `payload`) — Wave-5
consumers decode it.

ts.description: RFC 3339 capture timestamp, stamped by the server.

accepted.description: Number of signals written (0 when the feature flag is off).

object_key.description: The object the batch was flushed to, absent when nothing was written.

SignalInput.description:
One signal as a client sends it. The server stamps `v`, `ts`, and (when the
client omits it) `snapshot_token` to produce the stored [`SignalEnvelope`].

SignalKind.description:
The closed set of signal kinds (v1). Extending this is a deliberate format
change, not an open string.

v1.1 (2026-07-07, planner-feedback capture): adds the legacy
`ask_trace`/`ask_feedback` supervision records. They remain decodable for
durable training data, but no public Ask endpoint emits them.

`branch_merge_accepted`/`branch_merge_rejected` stay decodable for stored
signal records only: graphs have no branches, and nothing emits them.

SignalReadResponse.description:
`GET /v1/signals?from=&to=&limit=` — the consumer side of the signal bus:
signals whose flush seq lies in `[from, to]`, oldest first. Trainers split
on a pinned seq T (train ≤ T, eval > T) and record the window in the WS9
manifest's `data_lineage`.

objects_read.description: Objects fetched to serve this read (cost transparency).

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the result short.

SignatureSparsity.description:
How constrained the graph's relation type-signatures are. Sparse signatures
(many type pairs admitting exactly one relation) mean type-context alone
forces the predicate — the strongest, cheapest grounding.

forced_pct.description:
Fraction of observed (src_type, dst_type) pairs that admit exactly one
relation.

le3_pct.description: Fraction of observed type pairs that admit at most three relations.

type_pairs.description: Distinct type pairs observed in the current edge projection.

oneOf.description:
When a read was pinned with `as_of_commit_seq`, the pin that was applied.
This makes a pinned response self-describing — `commit_seq` still reports
the loaded head, so a caller can see both "you asked for N" and "head is
at M" instead of silently getting head.

compacted_seq.description:
Highest durable graph-truth commit folded by background compaction.
This is maintenance provenance, not the query-serving watermark.
Published reads expose their one common `served_at_seq` through the
response and `/v1/graph/read-snapshot`; handlers never fold the WAL tail
or assemble derived indexes to satisfy a request.

oneOf.description:
The coherent watermark named by the one immutable published generation
pinned for this response. All enabled families (RDF, Base, BM25, ANN,
summary, and conformance) are interpreted against this same
watermark; request pressure cannot select an older family or change it
mid-request. Omitted only for responses that do not use published state.

stale.description:
F2 (roadmap 18.3): true when this snapshot was served from the in-memory
cache while storage was degraded and the latest head could not be
verified — so `commit_seq` may not be the current head. Absent (false) on
every normal read; writes never serve stale. Omitted from the wire form
when false so healthy responses are byte-identical to before.

stale_reason.description:
The reason a read is `stale`. `"storage_degraded"` (F2),
`"eventual_consistency"` (served from the immutable published
generation); omitted when not stale.

SourceCaptureScope.description:
Source capture has no destination graph. Customer graph deletion therefore
cannot retire a shared reader or erase another customer's replay history.

SourceCheckpoint.description:
The connector owns the meaning and comparison of offsets. Equality here is
an exact checkpoint-chain check, never a lexical LSN/GTID comparison.

restore_state.description:
Exact opaque connector restore state, including schema history. Large
schema snapshots must use separately verified, scoped objects later.

sealed_credentials.description:
Sealed by the SaaS control plane. Username, password and optional CA
open only in its isolated reader supervisor, never in a workflow step.

SourceSetupScope.description: A connection in the owning storage tenant. No customer graph exists yet.

SourceValue.description:
A source value never uses a JSON number for exact decimal/integer data.
Missing columns are absent map entries; unchanged and NULL are distinct.

SparqlAggregate.description:
One aggregate projection: `func(operand) AS as_var`. `operand` is absent for
`COUNT(*)` (count rows); for SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX it must resolve to a numeric
value (typically a `property` term). `distinct` applies to COUNT.

SparqlAggregateFunc.description: An aggregate function for a grouped SELECT.

SparqlCompareOp.description: A comparison operator for a SPARQL FILTER.

SparqlEntailment.description:
Entailment regime applied to a conformant SPARQL query. The regime is
evaluated at query time as a closure-driven pattern rewrite over the
dataset's asserted schema triples; the published dataset itself stays
asserted-only.

SparqlFilter.description:
A FILTER over a solution: a comparison, or a boolean composition of filters.
A comparison whose operands are unbound, incomparable, or a type mismatch is
not satisfied (treated as false).

SparqlGroup.description:
One result group of a grouped/aggregated SELECT: the GROUP BY key entities
(`keys`, identity keys) and typed scalar keys (`value_keys`, property /
date-bucket keys), plus each aggregate's value bound to its `as` variable.

keys.description: Entity-identity GROUP BY keys, under their variable name.

value_keys.description:
Typed scalar GROUP BY keys (from `group_keys` property/date-bucket
entries), each under its `as` name. Empty for a purely entity-keyed group.

SparqlGroupKey.description:
A GROUP BY key. `var` groups by the identity of the entity bound to a
variable (the legacy `group_by` behavior); `property` groups by a typed
scalar `field` read off that entity, projected into each group's
`value_keys` under `as`. Externally tagged
(`{"var": {…}}`, `{"property": {…}}`).

oneOf.description:
Group by the entity bound to `var` (identity). The group's `keys` map
carries the key entity under `var`, exactly like a `group_by` entry.

var.description:
Group by the entity bound to `var` (identity). The group's `keys` map
carries the key entity under `var`, exactly like a `group_by` entry.

oneOf.description:
Group by the typed scalar property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.
The value lands in each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Rows whose entity
lacks the property form a single `null`-valued group.

property.description:
Group by the typed scalar property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.
The value lands in each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Rows whose entity
lacks the property form a single `null`-valued group.

oneOf.description:
Group by a calendar truncation of a **datetime** property `field` of the
entity bound to `var` — the unit for a time series (commits per month,
events per day). The bucket label (e.g. `2026-06`, `2026-06-25`) lands in
each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Errors if `field` is not a datetime
property. Rows whose entity lacks the property form a `null`-valued group.

date_bucket.description:
Group by a calendar truncation of a **datetime** property `field` of the
entity bound to `var` — the unit for a time series (commits per month,
events per day). The bucket label (e.g. `2026-06`, `2026-06-25`) lands in
each group's `value_keys` under `as`. Errors if `field` is not a datetime
property. Rows whose entity lacks the property form a `null`-valued group.

SparqlKeyValue.description:
One typed GROUP BY key value projected into a group's `value_keys`: a typed
scalar (a property value, or a date-bucket label). Distinct from
[`SparqlScalar`] (numeric-only aggregate results) because a key can be a
string/keyword, datetime, or boolean. `null` is an unbound key (the entity
lacked the property).

oneOf.description: RFC3339 instant (a datetime property) or a bucket label (`2026-06`, etc.).

date_time.description: RFC3339 instant (a datetime property) or a bucket label (`2026-06`, etc.).

SparqlOrderBy.description:
One ORDER BY key. `var` names an aggregate `as` var or a GROUP BY key in
aggregated mode, or a bound variable otherwise; rows/groups are ordered by
that value (numeric for aggregates, entity name for entity keys).

SparqlProfileJoinOrder.description:
The order the planner chose for one basic graph pattern (`bgp`) or one
join group (`join_group`).

bound_before.description: Variables already bound when the order was chosen (a seeded join).

evaluations.description:
How many times the planner made this same decision in the request,
for example once per seed row.

steps_total.description: Steps in the decision; `steps` keeps at most 64.

SparqlProfileJoinStep.description: One step of a join order, in the order the planner chose.

estimate.description:
For `bgp`, the cardinality estimate the planner compared when it chose
this pattern, given the variables bound before it. For `join_group`,
the child's standalone estimate. Absent when not priced.

pattern.description:
The triple pattern (`bgp`) or a short label of the child group
(`join_group`). Literals are cut at 64 characters and the whole step
at 512, IRIs included; a cut ends with `…`.

rows_after.description: `join_group` only: the rows accumulated after this child folded in.

SparqlProfileJoins.description: Binary-join counters of a profiled request, by strategy.

SparqlProfileOperator.description:
One operator kind that ran in a profiled request. Counters an operator
does not keep are zero; its other counters are in `detail`.

SparqlProfilePlans.description: Which specialized plans ran, as counts of sub-plans.

histogram_runs.description: Grouped counts answered from the key histograms.

obj_window.description: Range FILTERs served from an object-value window.

pair_join_stats.description: Two-pattern join counts answered from the pair-count sidecar.

row_reuse.description: Join steps that reused their row buffers.

small_build.description: Hash joins that built on the smaller pattern side.

star_prefix.description: BGPs evaluated as a merged star plus the rest.

stats_answered.description: Sub-plans answered from index statistics, reading no data blocks.

str_byte.description: String tests evaluated on raw dictionary bytes.

summary_fast_path.description:
The published summary answered the query: `hit`, `entailed_hit`, or
`declined`. Absent on the structured route, which has no fast path.

typed_adjacency.description: Typed-adjacency grouped counts answered by the batched plan.

SparqlProfileReads.description: Object reads of a profiled request.

blocks.description: Block and dictionary reads the plan charged.

budget_trips.description: Times the request read budget stopped the query.

bytes_fetched.description:
Stored bytes of the block reads that missed the request block cache.
Such a read goes to the node's cache tiers (RAM, NVMe) or to object
storage, so a miss is not always an object-storage GET. Zero when the
request block cache is off.

cache_hits.description: Block reads the request block cache served; zero when it is off.

cache_misses.description: Block reads that missed the request block cache; zero when it is off.

peak_bytes_held.description: The request block cache's largest residency, in bytes.

SparqlProfileStage.description: One timed stage of a profiled request.

SparqlProfileWcoj.description: Worst-case-optimal join counters of a profiled request.

SparqlQueryProfile.description:
What the server measured while it answered one profiled SPARQL request.
It describes that request only. Times are milliseconds of wall time.

filter_type_errors.description:
FILTER conditions dropped by a type error (for example a comparison
between datatypes with no defined order).

join_orders.description:
The order the planner chose for each basic graph pattern and join
group, with its estimates. At most 64 records of 64 steps each.

join_orders_dropped.description: Distinct join orders past the 64-record bound.

operators.description: Operators that ran, with the rows they took and produced.

result_cache.description:
The result-cache outcome. Always `bypassed`: a profiled request never
reads or fills the cache.

stages.description:
Stage timings in order. The text route reports `resolve_snapshot`,
`parse_rewrite`, `execute` and `serialize`; the structured route
reports `resolve_snapshot`, `lower`, `execute` and `decode`.

total_ms.description: The whole request inside the graph store, snapshot resolution included.

trigram.description:
The label-trigram decision for a string FILTER: `used`, a decline
reason (`unsupported`, `no_sidecar`, `predicate_not_covered`,
`short_needle`, `or_chain`, `candidate_cap`, `not_selective`,
`live_delta`, `read_failed`), or absent when the query had no string
test the index could serve.

SparqlScalar.description:
A scalar aggregate result value. `null` is an empty AVG/MIN/MAX (no numeric
rows).

SparqlSearchEstimate.description:
The costs the planner compared when the entities that satisfy the rest
of the query fit under its limit, counted from cluster metadata. The
search-first plan runs when `search_first_entries` is below
`filter_first_scored`.

filter_first_entries.description:
Entries of the clusters that hold an allowed entity: what the
filter-first plan reads.

filter_first_scored.description: Allowed entities with a vector: what the filter-first plan scores.

search_first_allowed.description:
Allowed entities inside those nearest clusters: what the search-first
plan scores.

search_first_entries.description:
Entries of the nearest clusters the planner compared: the smallest
probe that holds enough allowed entities for the exact rerank, or the
first probe with at least `filter_first_scored` entries. What the
search-first plan reads.

SparqlSearchPlan.description: How the planner answered the search of one query.

SparqlSearchReport.description:
What the search inside a SPARQL query did. Its hits are bound into the
query as a `VALUES` block, so the rest of the query sees them as rows.

allowed.description:
Entities that satisfy the rest of the query, when the planner read
them; capped at 20,001.

complete.description:
False when fewer than `top` entities satisfy the query within the
candidates the search may score.

oneOf.description:
The oldest commit every searched embedding covers. Text changed after
it is searched with its earlier vector.

The costs behind the choice of plan, when `allowed` fit under the
planner's limit.

hits.description: The entities it found and bound.

lag_commits.description: Commits between the snapshot the query read and `embedded_through_seq`.

oneOf.description:
The rerank (`search:rerank true`), when the query asked for one and
the search had hits. The model read the best `2·top` hits (20 to 40)
and the best `top` by its relevance were bound; any other status
bound the `top` most similar, without a relevance.

rounds.description: Search rounds (a search-first plan widens until it has `top`).

top.description:
The entities the search was asked for: `search:top`, else the query's
`LIMIT` plus `OFFSET`, else 10.

usage.description: The model call for the query text, if one ran.

SparqlSearchTimings.description: The phases of one search inside a SPARQL query, in milliseconds.

check_ms.description: The graph checks of the candidates.

embed_ms.description: The query vector (0 when cached, given, or read from an entity).

filter_ms.description: The read of the entities that satisfy the rest of the query.

rerank_ms.description: The exact rescoring of the candidates.

resolve_ms.description: Embedding documents, manifests and class lists.

SparqlSelectRequest.description:
A SPARQL-subset SELECT/ASK query: a conjunctive basic graph pattern (the
WHERE) evaluated over the conformant published RDF dataset, with variable
projection, DISTINCT, and LIMIT/OFFSET. Structured-request-first — the SPARQL
text syntax is a later addition behind a dialect field, and FILTER plus
aggregation arrive in later milestones.

aggregates.description:
Aggregate projections (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX … AS …). Presence switches
the query into grouped/aggregated mode.

oneOf.description:
Exact transaction-time watermark from the retained graph-owned RDF
lineage. Uses the same bounded base and commit deltas as SPARQL text;
a missing checkpoint or a pin beyond head fails instead of serving a
different snapshot. Valid-time selectors are unsupported.

ask.description:
`ASK` form: return only `boolean` (whether the pattern has any solution).
Projection, DISTINCT, and limit/offset are ignored.

oneOf.description:
Read consistency. `eventual` (the default) pins the native RDF runset in
the current `PublishedReadSnapshot`; it never folds a gap or discovers
another family. The served watermark is surfaced as
`snapshot.served_at_seq`. A graph without a published generation returns
a retryable readiness error. `strong` requires that same immutable
generation to cover head and otherwise returns
`strong_read_pending`.

filters.description:
FILTER: boolean conditions on each solution, implicitly AND-ed. A solution
is kept only when every filter holds.

group_by.description:
GROUP BY: variables whose bound entities define the groups. When set (or
when `aggregates` is non-empty) the response returns `groups` instead of
`solutions`. Empty `group_by` with `aggregates` set yields one group over
the whole result.

group_keys.description:
GROUP BY keys richer than a bare entity variable: group by a typed scalar
`property` value (e.g. a commit's `area`), or a `date_bucket` truncation
of a datetime property (e.g. commits per month). Additive to `group_by`;
the effective grouping is the `group_by` variables (as entity-identity
keys) followed by these. Entity-identity keys land in each group's `keys`;
scalar keys land in `value_keys` under their `as` name. Presence (like a
non-empty `group_by` or `aggregates`) switches the query into grouped mode.

having.description:
HAVING: conditions on the aggregated groups, implicitly AND-ed. Only
meaningful in aggregated mode; a `var` term resolves to an aggregate value
or a GROUP BY key entity.

limit.description: Return at most this many rows (applied after `offset`).

max_solutions.description:
Fail-closed ceiling on the intermediate join solution set
(see `AnalyticQueryRequest::max_solutions`).

oneOf.description:
A5 read-your-writes floor: require the read to be served from state whose
watermark ≥ this `commit_seq` (the `new_commit_seq` a commit/import
returned). Under the default `eventual`, a floor not yet covered by the
published generation returns a retryable `read_your_writes_pending` 429 (poll
until it lands); under `strong` the floor is satisfied by construction and a
floor above head is a client error. `None` == no floor. See
`docs/architecture/segment-native-indexing.md` §6.

order_by.description:
ORDER BY: sort keys applied to the result rows (or groups), in priority
order, before LIMIT/OFFSET.

patterns.description: WHERE: the conjunctive basic graph pattern (shares the analytic engine).

profile.description:
Return what the server measured while it answered this request in
`profile`. A profiled request never reads or fills the result cache,
so the profile always describes an execution.

reason.description:
Not available on the published SPARQL surface: a graph's stored
inference rules already run at publish time, folding derived facts into
the asserted dataset every query reads. Requesting `reason: true`
returns a typed, non-retryable error.

select.description:
SELECT projection: the variables to return, in order. Absent = `SELECT *`
(every variable the pattern binds, sorted). Ignored in aggregated mode.

SparqlSelectResponse.description:
Result of a `SparqlSelectRequest`. For SELECT, `vars` is the projected head
and `solutions` the rows; for ASK, `boolean` is set and `solutions` empty.

boolean.description: Set for the ASK form: whether the WHERE pattern has any solution.

groups.description: Aggregated/grouped result rows. Empty unless the query aggregates.

oneOf.description:
What the server measured for this request. Present only when the
request asked for `profile`.

solutions.description: Non-aggregated SELECT rows. Empty in aggregated mode and for ASK.

truncated.description:
The intermediate-solution ceiling cut the join
(see `AnalyticQueryResponse::truncated`).

vars.description:
The projected variable names (the result head). For aggregated queries
this is the GROUP BY keys followed by each aggregate's `as` variable.
Empty for ASK.

SparqlTerm.description: An operand in a FILTER comparison.

oneOf.description: The entity bound to a query variable.

var.description: The entity bound to a query variable.

oneOf.description: A literal property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.

property.description: A literal property `field` of the entity bound to `var`.

oneOf.description: A literal constant.

SparqlTextRequest.description:
Run a SPARQL 1.1 query supplied as **text** (SELECT or ASK) through the
conformant engine over the live graph, returning SPARQL 1.1 Query Results
JSON. Distinct from [`SparqlSelectRequest`] (the structured-request form);
this is the raw-text dialect. CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected (they yield an
RDF graph, not a results table).

oneOf.description:
Exact transaction-time watermark to read from a retained immutable
published generation. The server never reconstructs WAL state in the
request path and never substitutes a newer or older generation.

cursor.description:
Opt into snapshot-bound keyset pagination: empty string starts a page,
otherwise echo `next_cursor` with the identical query. Requires one
supported indexed ordered LIMIT (1..10000), OFFSET 0, and no transport
`limit`/`offset`. An unavailable snapshot expires the cursor explicitly.

entailment.description:
Entailment regime. `None` (default) matches asserted triples only.
`Rdfs` applies the practical RDFS core at query time, `Subclass` the
class-only subset, and `Owl` the OWL profile on top of `Rdfs`. All
derive the closure from the pinned generation's asserted schema
triples.

limit.description:
Return at most this many result rows. Applied to SELECT bindings after the
conformant engine has produced the complete result document.

offset.description: Skip this many result rows before `limit`.

profile.description:
Return what the server measured while it answered this request in
`profile`. A profiled request never reads or fills the result cache,
so the profile always describes an execution.

query.description: The SPARQL query text (SELECT or ASK).

reason.description:
Not available on the published SPARQL surface: a graph's stored
inference rules already run at publish time, folding derived facts into
the asserted dataset every query reads. Requesting `reason: true`
returns a typed, non-retryable error.

request.description:
The user's words behind this query, when the caller has them. When
present the server records an eval trace and returns its `trace_id`,
so the caller can label the result valid or not (managed evals).

oneOf.description:
With `request`: how the caller routed the question, such as the
`route` of a `POST /v1/query/ask` answer in `mode: "route"`. The eval
trace keeps it, so a label on the answer can confirm the route and a
run can score the router. It does not change the query.

SparqlTextResponse.description:
Result of a [`SparqlTextRequest`]: the SPARQL 1.1 Query Results JSON document,
carried verbatim as a string (the engine already serializes it to the
standard `{ "head": …, "results": … }` / `{ "head": …, "boolean": … }`
shape). Clients parse `results` as JSON.

next_cursor.description:
Continuation for the query's inner ordered window. OPTIONAL enrichment
can return more rows than that window. Absent when exhausted or when
cursor pagination was not requested; a full final page may yield a
continuation whose following page is empty.

oneOf.description:
What the server measured for this request. Present only when the
request asked for `profile`.

How the search by meaning in the query ran (`?x search:similarTo …`).
Present only when the query holds a search.

A3 (bounded-staleness serving): present when the request selected a
consistency mode, so a text-dialect client can read the served watermark
and staleness the same way structured callers read `snapshot`. Omitted
(absent) for a bare strong-consistency request, so existing responses stay
byte-identical.

trace_id.description:
The eval trace recorded for this query, present only when the request
carried `request`. Label it with `POST /v1/evals/label?trace=<id>`.

SparqlValue.description:
A literal constant operand in a FILTER. Scalars compare by typed value;
`entity` compares by identity against a bound variable.

StarterWorkflow.description: One starter workflow: an entry of `GET /v1/workflows/starters`.

available.description: Whether this server can run it now.

code.description:
The template a developer can copy to run this work in their own
worker: a folder of `sdk/templates/`, the catalog id with dashes
(`documents-link`, `values-extract`, `ontology-fit`, `rows`). Null
when there is none (`search.embed` and `documents.parse` run in LBB
only, and `workflow` is the developer's own code).

group.description:
The Workflows page group, a stable slug: `documents`, `values`,
`search`, `ontology`, `developer`.

id.description: `search.embed`, `ontology.fit`, `workflow`, `rows`, …

media_types.description:
The media types of the content trigger that feeds its workflow, for
a template your worker runs on files (`rows`, `sections`; `watch` is
`none`): `type/subtype`, `type/*` or `*/*`. Its workflow is created
with `PUT /v1/workflows/named` and this content trigger, as the
template's `trigger()` makes it. Empty for a starter workflow that
watches a class.

owns.description:
The outputs it owns when they are fixed. A developer workflow
declares its own when it is created.

params.description:
The parameters it takes in `params`. For a template your worker runs
on files, the settings of the template's code (`defaults` in its
`workflow.ts`): no route takes them.

samples.description:
The names of the sample files that Try on samples loads
(`POST /v1/workflows/starters/try`), as the template's `samples/`
folder names them. For a template your worker runs on files, the
files its own `npm run try` loads. Empty for `workflow`.

shortcut.description: The older route family that reads and writes the same documents.

try_on_samples.description:
Whether this server can run Try on samples for it now: SaaS mode, a
sample set, a version LBB runs, and the models (and for the document
starter workflows, the parser) the run needs. Always false for a
template your worker runs on files.

StarterWorkflowCatalog.description: `GET /v1/workflows/starters`: the starter workflows of this server.

StarterWorkflowParam.description: One parameter a starter workflow takes in `params`.

StarterWorkflowParamKind.description: The value kind of a starter workflow parameter.

StarterWorkflowTryRequest.description:
Try a starter workflow on its samples (`POST
/v1/workflows/starters/try`): a new graph in the caller's stack with the
samples loaded and the workflow created there with its sample defaults.

params.description:
Parameters over the sample defaults, an object: each key replaces the
default of that key. The starter workflow's own `params` keys apply.

starter.description:
The catalog id, with or without the version (`values.extract`,
`values.extract@v1`). The former id `infer.llm` reads as
`values.extract`.

StarterWorkflowTryResponse.description:
The answer of `POST /v1/workflows/starters/try`. The workflows run as
usual from here; read them with `GET
/v1/workflows/triggered?graph=<graph>`.

graph.description: The new graph's id, in the caller's stack.

note.description:
What happens next and how to delete the graph, in one or two
sentences.

samples.description: The sample files loaded, by name.

workflows.description:
The workflows created there, in the order they were created
(`documents.link` also creates `documents.parse`, which reads its
files).

complete.description:
True only when every configured recipe and its named versions were inspected.
This is diagnostic coverage, not a claim that all embeddings are ready.

configured_count.description: Unknown when the roster could not be read, including a missing roster.

metadata_budget_bytes.description: Total control-object bytes admitted for this class inspection.

oneOf.description: Existing class status semantics; recall is not inspected on this bounded read.

StatusIssue.description: A diagnostic failure, without backend keys, credentials or raw storage errors.

publication_caught_up.description: Validated RDF coverage only; says nothing about class embedding readiness.

StatusResponseSelector.description:
Accepted selectors during the finite source/release transition. The
response version stays CurrentStatusVersion and never claims legacy shape.

StreamErrorEvent.description:
A streamed response ended with an error: the status, code and message of
the JSON error that the same request without a stream gets. The text of a
`5xx` is redacted the same way.

status.description: The HTTP status of the same error without a stream.

SuggestContext.description:
Endpoint types for [`SearchSuggestRequest::context`]. Both optional; supplying
only one narrows on that side alone (a known source type, unknown target).

SuggestDatasetResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/suggest-dataset` — the suggest-ranker trainer's probe
feed: `suggestion_adopted` signals (each carries the typed prefix and the
adopted suggestion text) at or below the split pin, topped up with
execution-verified synthetic pairs from the graph's own vocabulary so a
cold graph can still train.

probes.description:
`query` = the typed prefix, `expected` = the adopted (or synthetic
gold) suggestion text.

split_seq.description:
Signals with flush seq ≤ this were consumed (record it as the run's
`trained_at_commit_seq` so the split audit can verify).

SuggestRankerWeights.description:
Per-kind multipliers for the suggest ranking (`score = kind_weight ×
df_factor`): the trainable artifact of the `suggest_ranker` model kind.
`None` leaves that kind on the shipped default weight, so a trained vector
only moves the kinds it learned about.

SuggestServingDefaults.description:
Suggest-ranker serving default derived from a promoted `suggest_ranker`
run: the per-kind weights the suggest path applies when a request does not
override `ranker`.

run.description: The promoted registry run these weights came from.

SuggestedFacts.description:
Graph facts a review item proposes. Accepting commits them through the
ordinary triplet commit, after any evolve operations; dismissing writes
nothing. At most 200 triplets plus entity property rows, and 64 KiB of
JSON. On an RDF-native graph the accept writes them as RDF, the
statements a records graph shows for them. A person can leave facts out
of the accept (`OntologyChangeSuggestionAcceptRequest::facts`), except
the rows `required` names.

oneOf.description:
The outputs the producer owns on the facts' subjects; the accept
replaces them (see `ReplaceOwnedInput`).

required.description:
The `entity_properties` rows an accept must keep when it leaves other
facts out: the other facts need them (the type of a new instance). An
accept that leaves one out is refused; dismiss the suggestion instead.

summary.description: One line about the facts for a reviewer. At most 500 characters.

SuggestedIdentity.description:
Records from different sources that describe one real-world thing.
Accepting links each later member to the first with a `SAME_AS` edge
(`https://littlebigbrain.com/r/same_as` in SPARQL). Search and SPARQL's
OWL entailment do not merge linked records yet.

confidence.description: From 0 to 1; 1 for an exact key match.

members.description: 2 to 10 records; the first is the canonical one.

reason.description:
Why they match, for example `email ada@acme.test`. At most 200
characters.

SuggestedQuery.description:
One zero-result-rescue alternative: a query the caller might have meant,
with the source that produced it.

SuggestionAnchor.description:
The ontology element a suggestion is attached to. `name` is the class,
property or relation name; it is absent for `ontology`.

SuggestionBatchDecision.description:
How a batch decided a suggestion: the batch, its size, the pattern a
person decided, and whether the person saw this suggestion as a sample.

id.description:
The batch's id (`batch_` and 24 hex characters), the same on every
suggestion one call decided.

pattern.description: The pattern key the request named (`SuggestionPattern::key`).

shown.description:
Whether the request's `shown` named this suggestion: the person saw
it as a sample before deciding. Absent when the request named no
samples.

size.description: How many suggestions the call named.

SuggestionBatchOutcome.description: What a batch did with one suggestion.

reason.description:
Why it was skipped, or that it was decided before (`accepted
already`).

oneOf.description: Its status after the batch; absent for an unknown id.

superseded_by.description:
For a superseded suggestion: the suggestion its producer named in
its place, when it named one.

author.description: Declared by the caller; the data plane does not authenticate people.

SuggestionCommentKind.description:
A discussion entry. `event` entries are written by the server when the
suggestion changes state (accepted, dismissed, revised, reopened).

SuggestionConfidenceRange.description: The lowest and the highest confidence of a pattern's suggestions.

SuggestionEvidence.description:
What the producer saw. Every field is optional; the server bounds the
sizes (at most 20 samples of at most 4 KiB each, at most 200 source fields).

fill_rate.description: Share of those records that carry a value, from 0 to 1.

records.description: How many records the change concerns (for example 311 deals).

source_fields.description: Source fields the change is about, for example `deals.amount`.

SuggestionFactsCommit.description: The commit an accept made for a suggestion's facts.

no_op.description: The facts were in the graph already: nothing new was written.

oneOf.description: What `replace_owned` removed.

request_id.description:
The commit's idempotency key: `ontology-suggestion:<id>:facts:r<revision>`,
with `:k<hash>` of the kept facts when a person left some out.

SuggestionFactsWritten.description:
What the producer wrote after the accept, for facts it writes itself:
the item of the `review` workflow commits the proposals' status on
accept, and the workflow then writes the facts. Absent until the
producer has written them.

at.description: RFC 3339 time of the last change.

dismissed.description: Facts the person left out, or that a dismissed item took with it.

waiting.description:
Facts that wait for another review item: a link to an instance that
the other item makes.

written.description: Facts written, or held by the graph already.

SuggestionKind.description:
What a suggestion asks a person to decide: facts to review (the review
items of `review`, the values of `values.extract`, any facts without a
change), links (the link reviews of `documents.link`), an ontology
change, or something else (records to link as one identity).

SuggestionLinkDecision.description:
What a link review of `documents.link` asks: link a mention to an entry
(a link below the gate), or the model chose no entry and the facts link
each mention to its best candidate.

SuggestionLinkSummary.description:
A link review in brief, from its first fact and evidence sample: the
mention it goes from, the entry it goes to, and the model's answer.

best_probability.description: For no entry: the probability the model gave its best candidate.

confidence.description: The link's confidence; for no entry, the confidence of that answer.

document.description:
The mention's document, page (from 1) and line. The document is the
`Document`'s IRI that the link's evidence names (without its
`#page=` fragment), or the file name in evidence written before
typed content.

document_name.description:
The file's name: for a `document` IRI, its `Document`'s `name` at
the published generation (absent before the generation holds the
file, or after its delete); for evidence written before typed
content, the name the evidence holds.

mentions.description: The mentions the review holds (its facts).

relation.description:
`REFERS_TO` (the span names the entry) or `SAME_ITEM_AS` (the same
item).

target.description:
The entry's identifier, and its key (`entry:<sha256>:<identifier>`,
the sha-256 of its defining document).

SuggestionOrigin.description:
The producer of a suggestion. `id` names it within its kind: the
integration's connection id, the agent's name, or the person. `label` is
display text.

SuggestionPattern.description:
The pattern of a suggestion: the suggestions that ask one decision a
person can make from a few samples (the same producer, document, kind of
fact and shape of text). Derived when the suggestion is read, from its
stored fields.

key.description: Stable: `pt_` and 20 hex characters of the pattern's parts.

label.description:
The pattern in words, for example `Link "#.#.#" in manual.pdf to
Section #.#.# (REFERS_TO)`. At most 200 characters.

oneOf.description: Over the suggestions whose evidence carries a confidence.

members.description:
Every suggestion of the pattern with its title and confidence, in
the order of `suggestion_ids`: a person can leave some out before a
batch decision.

origin.description: The producer (every suggestion of a pattern has the same).

samples.description:
Up to 3 suggestions to check: the least confident, the middle one and
the most confident.

suggestion_ids.description: Every suggestion of the pattern, the least confident first.

SuggestionPatternMember.description: One suggestion of a pattern, for the list a person picks from.

oneOf.description: For a link review: where it goes from and to.

SuggestionSourceSummary.description:
Where a suggestion's evidence comes from, for a list row: the first
evidence sample that names a document.

SuggestionStatusCounts.description: Suggestions per status, over the whole graph (not only the listed page).

SyntheticEvalResponse.description:
`GET /v1/models/synthetic-eval` — execution-verified QA pairs generated
FROM the graph: each question is templated from a current edge and its
expected answer IS the executed projection, so labels are verified by
construction, never hallucinated. Deterministic per snapshot.

properties.description: Source column to owned RDF predicate. SQL NULL contributes no fact.

TrainGateReport.description:
The deterministic promotion gate's verdict, reported in full so a held
run is as auditable as a promoted one (null results are data).

effect.description:
Challenger − champion primary quality metric on the held-out eval
slice (nDCG for fusion and retrieval-profile comparisons).

labeled.description: Labeled eval probes the decision is over.

latency_p50_ratio.description: Challenger / champion latency ratios at each reported percentile.

latency_ratio.description:
Legacy decision latency ratio. For configuration shadow evaluation this
is the worst of p50/p95/p99; older trainer kinds may use their primary
latency statistic.

max_latency_ratio.description:
Ceiling on `latency_ratio` — unoptimized metrics are guarded, never
traded away.

min_effect.description: Minimum effect size for promotion (refuses noise).

min_labeled.description: Minimum labeled probes for any promotion.

ndcg_ci95_lower.description:
Deterministic paired-bootstrap 95% interval for challenger − champion
nDCG@10. Promotion requires the lower bound to be at least zero.

reason.description: Human-readable one-liner for the console status surface.

recall_delta.description:
Paired held-out retrieval deltas. When present, all must be
non-negative.

TrainModelJobProgress.description: Bounded in-flight work counters for a durable trainer job.

estimated_duration_ms.description:
Linear estimate from work completed so far. Absent before the first
measured probe or for trainers without fine-grained progress.

heartbeat_micros.description: Worker heartbeat attached to this progress snapshot.

replay_evaluations_completed.description: Expensive search executions or cached-score evaluations completed.

source_probes_completed.description: Distinct input probes prepared at the pinned source snapshot.

TrainModelJobStatusResponse.description:
Durable background trainer status. The terminal `result` carries the full
snapshot lineage, held-out gate evidence, and recorded run number.

TrainModelRequest.description:
`POST /v1/models/train` — run the deterministic trainer once for one
kind: build an execution-verified probe set, search a bounded candidate
space on the train slice, gate challenger vs champion on the held-out
eval slice, record the run in the WS9 registry either way, and promote
only when the gate passes. This is the same tick the auto-train cadence
fires; calling it by hand is always safe (bounded, snapshot-pinned).

force.description: Train even when the cadence says retraining is not yet due.

max_probes.description: Probe-set ceiling (train + eval slices together). Clamped server-side.

probes.description:
Bring-your-own labeled probes (captured signals, hand-written evals).
`None` ⇒ execution-verified synthetic pairs from the graph itself.

source_job_id.description:
Server-assigned durable execution identity. Clients normally omit it;
it is persisted into the model manifest to make worker redelivery safe.

TrainModelResponse.description: Outcome + evidence of one trainer tick.

oneOf.description:
Winning Platt scaler for `kind: calibration` ticks. For calibration,
arm `hit_rate_at_k` carries `1 − Brier` (higher is better) and the
manifest metrics carry the explicit Brier scores.

candidates.description: Candidate configurations evaluated on the train slice.

oneOf.description: Best candidate on the held-out eval slice.
Champion (serving defaults) on the held-out eval slice.

run.description: The recorded registry run (promoted or held); absent when nothing ran.

oneOf.description: Winning candidate weights for `kind: suggest_ranker` ticks.

Winning candidate weights (recorded in the run's artifact), for
`kind: fusion` ticks.

TriggeredDocumentPage.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/named/documents`: one page of the documents of a
`documents.link` or `documents.map` workflow, in the list envelope. Each
row has the fields of a row of the workflow's `details.documents`. A
request with `Lbb-Version` before 2026-10-21 gets the earlier shape:
`documents` and `next_after` in place of `object`, `data`, `has_more`
and `next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

total.description: The documents that match `q`, on every page.

details.description:
The workflow's own status: `EmbeddingStatus` for `search.embed`,
`FitSourceStatus` for `ontology.fit`, `DeveloperWorkflowDetails` for
`workflow`.

oneOf.description:
Where the gate came from when a person applied it from the inbox
decisions (`POST /v1/workflows/triggered/calibration/apply`).

starter.description: The starter workflow's catalog id, without the version.

TriggeredWorkflowList.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/triggered`: every triggered workflow of the graph,
ordered by starter, then name.

details.description:
The workflow's own preview: `EmbeddingPreviewResponse`,
`FitSourcePreviewResponse`, or the trigger messages a developer
workflow would receive.

iris.description: Show these instances instead of a sample.

propose.description:
Run the models on the sample, where the starter workflow has models
(a dry run of `ontology.fit`). Its spend counts against the budget.

sample.description: Sample instances to show (the starter workflow's own default and cap apply).

TriggeredWorkflowPreviewRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/triggered/preview`: what creating or changing a
triggered workflow would do. Writes nothing.

TriggeredWorkflowRef.description:
A triggered workflow by its two names: the starter workflow's catalog id
and the workflow's name (`?starter=&name=` of the triggered routes).

queued.description: The workflow's job was asked to run.

TriggeredWorkflowRequest.description:
Create a workflow from a starter workflow, or change one (`PUT
/v1/workflows/triggered`). The same request again is a no-op.

name.description:
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}`. Default: the class's local name, or the
starter workflow's default name.

oneOf.description: `workflow` only: the outputs the developer's code owns.

params.description:
The starter workflow's parameters, an object. `search.embed`:
`model`, `dim`, `title`. `ontology.fit`: `context`.

starter.description:
The catalog id, with or without the version (`search.embed`,
`search.embed@v1`). The former id `infer.llm` reads as
`values.extract`.

oneOf.description: `workflow` only: the workflow type that receives the instances.

TriggeredWorkflowRunning.description:
The step a workflow runs now in the starters job: a phase in plain
words and how far it got. The job writes it every few seconds while the
step runs (and at least every 15 s), so it reads the same on every node.

heartbeat_at.description: When the job last wrote this progress (RFC 3339).

phase.description:
What the step does now, in plain words: `reading documents`,
`reading pages`, `linking mentions`, `asking the decision model`,
`writing facts`, `filing review items`, `sending messages`, ….

started_at.description:
When the step started (RFC 3339). A step that goes on in the job's
next round keeps its start.

total.description: Absent when the step does not know it.

TriggeredWorkflowState.description: The state of a triggered workflow.

TriggeredWorkflowStatus.description: The one status shape every triggered workflow reports.

lag_commits.description: Published commits the workflow has not read yet (when ready).

oneOf.description: Review items the workflow filed, per status.

pending.description: Instances waiting to be read or sent.

pending_since_ms.description:
When the queue last went from empty to not empty, in milliseconds
since the Unix epoch: the age of the oldest wait. Absent while
nothing waits, and for `search.embed` and `ontology.fit`.

oneOf.description: The step the workflow runs now; absent while it does not run.

Edge-level duplicate handling. `append` preserves historical behavior:
every emitted triplet appends a new edge event. `skip_unchanged` makes a
triplet a no-op when an identical current edge already exists, which is
useful for re-runnable backfills. Evidence-only repeats are also skipped:
use `append` when a repeated current edge carries new provenance that
must be recorded. Omitted = `append`.

entity_embeddings.description:
Client-supplied vectors to attach to entities in this commit. Entities
are matched by (type, name); ones not mentioned in `triplets` are
upserted standalone so vectors can be attached without new edges.

entity_properties.description:
Client-supplied literal property values to attach to entities in this
commit. Entities are matched by (type, name) against the triplet endpoints
(and embedding targets) in the same commit; each property's `field` is
resolved against the ontology. This is the ingest side of the typed-value
channel that FILTER/aggregation read.

observed_at.description:
Backfill timestamp (RFC3339). When set, this commit is recorded **as of**
that instant rather than now: every edge's transaction time
(`commit_time_micros`) is stamped with it, and any triplet that does not
carry its own `valid_time` defaults its `valid_time.start` to it. Replaying
history in source-chronological order with `observed_at` set per commit is
what makes `as_of` reads (by date) and the temporal-coverage probe
faithful — without it, a backfill stamps everything "now" and every past
`as_of` returns empty. Omit it for normal live writes (stamped now).

oneOf.description:
Optional compare-and-swap guard evaluated atomically against the head
used to build this commit.

How `entity_properties` (and embedding-only) writes combine with an
entity's already-stored fields. `merge` (the default) keeps prior fields
the commit does not re-send and overlays the ones it does — so an
incremental "just add `h_index`" enrichment never drops the title or
status you set earlier. `replace` makes the commit's field list the
entity's complete attribute set, clearing every field it omits (send it
to authoritatively re-state, prune, or with an empty `properties` list to
clear an entity). Omitted = `merge`.

The outputs this writer owns on `subjects`. The same commit removes
the owned facts it does not write again, so a rerun replaces them. See
[`ReplaceOwnedInput`]. On an RDF-native graph the commit writes the
statements a records graph shows for its facts and removes the owned
statements this writer wrote before and does not write again.

triplets.description:
The edges to commit. Defaults to empty so a properties-only or
embeddings-only commit needs no placeholder `"triplets": []`; the commit
still requires at least one triplet, embedding, or entity-property overall.

oneOf.description:
The workflow turn that makes the commit (`WorkflowFence`): a repeat
of the commit's `Idempotency-Key` is answered as a replay, and a new
commit is refused with `409 workflow_fence_lost` unless the token
still holds the turn. The TypeScript SDK's `writeOwned` sends it.

TruncatedCollection.description: One capped collection: how many rows came back out of how many the read saw.

total_observed.description:
Rows the bounded read observed. This is a **lower bound**: establishing
the true total means walking the entity's whole degree, which is the
cost the cap exists to avoid. Render it as "returned of at least total".

TruthSource.description: Who set a call's ground truth.

oneOf.description: Explicitly null when the ask produced no original plan.

VersionResponse.description: Unauthenticated build, wire-capability, and persisted-format identity.

built_at.description: UTC build timestamp baked into the running binary.

capabilities.description: Fine-grained additive features safe for SDK capability gates.

git_commit.description: Source revision baked into the running binary.

persisted_format.description: Deterministic fingerprint of all persisted format versions.

VocabExportResponse.description:
`GET /v1/search/vocab` — the graph's grounding vocabulary as sorted,
deduped string sections: the canonical input for a decoder-side automaton
(an FST/trie builder consumes byte-sorted streams directly), and the
vocabulary half of an "intelligence to go" export bundle. Derived per
snapshot from the same sources the suggest surface reads — no doc/postings
block reads.

attribute_values.description:
Attribute directory entries as `field=value`, byte-sorted. Present only
when a persisted index run carries the attribute directory.

entities.description: Live entity display names, byte-sorted and deduped.

schema.description:
Ontology schema names (entity types, relations, property fields),
byte-sorted and deduped.

truncated.description: True when any section hit its cap (silent truncation is never OK).

max_segments.description:
When appending the new segment would leave the manifest with more
than this many segments, merge them all into one.

min_tail_commits.description: Compact only when the WAL tail holds at least this many commits.

compacted_commits.description: WAL tail commits folded into the new segment.

compacted_seq.description: Highest commit folded; equals `snapshot.compacted_seq` after success.

merged.description: True when this compaction merged the existing segments into one.

segments.description: Segments referenced by the manifest after this compaction.

skipped.description:
True when the tail was below `min_tail_commits` (or another writer
already compacted past this head) and nothing was written.

WidenRelationOp.description:
Add already-declared entity types (by name) to a relation's declared
domain (`add_domain`) and/or range (`add_range`). The relation and every
named type must already exist. Ids already present are skipped, so the op
is idempotent and a re-run is a no-op.

add_domain.description: Entity-type names to add to the relation's domain (source types).

add_range.description: Entity-type names to add to the relation's range (target types).

scope.description: Immutable authorization and identity binding for a capture epoch.

oneOf.description:
Capture workers may only acquire leases for these exact approved
settings. Rotating source credentials invalidates older reader grants.

scope.description:
Source capture has no destination graph. Customer graph deletion therefore
cannot retire a shared reader or erase another customer's replay history.

oneOf.description:
Capture workers may only acquire leases for these exact approved
settings. Rotating source credentials invalidates older reader grants.

WorkflowBlob.description:
A blob of a workflow (`POST /v1/workflows/blobs?workflow_id=`): bytes a
step stores beside the engine for a large output or a large shared read
(a catalogue), keyed by their SHA-256. A step names `key` in its output,
its state or a message; `GET /v1/workflows/blobs?key=` reads the bytes.
A blob stays while a live identity of the graph names it (its state, an
unfinished turn's message, steps or operation), and at least a day after
its last write; it goes with its workflow and with the graph.

created.description: This write stored the bytes; false when they were stored already.

key.description:
`<workflow>/<sha256>`: the workflow is the named workflow of the
writing identity (`starter.<name>[.<k>]` writes under `<name>`), or
`instance:<id>` for an identity of no named workflow.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes, lowercase hex.

wait_ms.description: Long-poll timeout, capped at ten seconds.

oneOf.description: Optional direct handoff: claim another ready task in this workflow in the same durable transaction.

WorkflowContentTrigger.description:
A content trigger: the uploads (`POST /v1/files`) whose media type is
one of `media_types`, read from the graph's content log as they arrive,
without a wait for a publication. Each message holds one content: its
`Document` in `instances`, and an origin of kind `content` with the
content's SHA-256, media type, upload time and request id. Messages are
routed to shards by the content's SHA-256.

media_types.description:
1 to 32 media types, `type/subtype` (`application/pdf`) or
`type/*` (`image/*`), compared without case and without parameters.

data.description: Any JSON, at most 64 KiB serialized.

id.description:
1 to 128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : -`: the event's idempotency key. An id
the stream received in its dedupe window is dropped.

key.description: The events of one key go to one shard, in order. Absent: the id.

type.description: The event's type, at most 128 characters.

WorkflowEventRecord.description:
An event as the stream keeps it and as a batch holds it: the event, when
the stream received it and the id of the request that sent it.

WorkflowEventsBatch.description: The blob of a batch: its events, in the order of the stream.

WorkflowEventsMessage.description:
The message of a batch of events (`type: "events"`). The events are in
the blob `blob` (`GET /v1/workflows/blobs?key=`); the SDKs read it before
the handler runs.

shard.description: The shard the events' keys route to.

WorkflowEventsReceipt.description: What a send of events answers: the stream took them.

received.description:
Events the request held. Repeats of an id are dropped later, when
the trigger reads them.

received_at.description: When the stream took them, RFC 3339.

WorkflowExecutionCredential.description:
Short-lived data-plane authority for one validated workflow turn attempt.
The bearer is distinct from the original workflow control credential and
contains no raw turn lease secret. Do not persist it in workflow state or
checkpoints. Every execution still freshly validates the live lease.

expires_at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds; at most the current lease deadline and 60 seconds
after issue. Refresh uses the original control client and lease request.

graph_epoch.description: Exact main-branch incarnation; send as expected_graph_epoch with reads.

issued_at_ms.description:
Server issue time. Together with expiry this provides a clock-independent
lifetime; optional when decoding responses from older servers.

operations.description: Exactly one explicitly requested operation; no general read/write grant.

WorkflowExecutionCredentialRequest.description:
Issue or refresh one operation credential using the original control bearer.
Omitted operation preserves the SELECT/ASK contract. This is deliberately
distinct from heartbeat/checkpoint lease requests.

WorkflowExecutionOperation.description:
One explicit operation of a workflow execution credential. `file_read`
and `owned_write` are the grants of LBB's hosted workers: only LBB's work
token is issued them.

WorkflowFence.description:
A commit made from a workflow turn (`POST /v1/graph/commit`,
`workflow_fence`): the server answers a repeat of the commit's request id
as a replay, and refuses a new commit unless `token` still holds turn
`turn` of instance `workflow_id` (`409 workflow_fence_lost`). The check
runs before the commit, so a lease that ends while the commit runs is the
only window left.

WorkflowGate.description:
Outputs whose confidence is below `below` go to the review inbox instead
of the graph.

target_precision.description:
The precision a lower gate measured from the inbox decisions must
reach, 0.5 to 0.999 (`GET /v1/workflows/triggered/calibration`).
Absent: 0.95. A change of it alone reads no instance again.

WorkflowGateApplyRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/triggered/calibration/apply`: set a gated workflow's
gate from its measurement. The labels are read again; the request is
refused without a proposal (409 `calibration_no_proposal`).

gate.description:
The gate to set: from the proposal's gate up to below the current
gate. Absent: the proposal's gate.

WorkflowGateBand.description:
One confidence band of a gate's report: the labels whose gate value lies
in `[low, high)` (the last band of the scale includes 1). A band that
reaches above the gate is cut at the gate.

below_gate.description:
The band lies below the gate. A band at or above the gate holds
answers written without a person: inbox decisions do not measure it
(calibration sessions with a judge do).

correct.description: Labels that say the answer was right.

wilson_low.description: The 95% Wilson interval of the precision; absent without labels.

WorkflowGateCalibration.description:
Where a gate came from when a person applied it from a measurement: the
inbox decisions (`POST /v1/workflows/triggered/calibration/apply`) or a
calibration session (`POST /v1/models/calibration/apply`). A change of
the gate by `PUT /v1/workflows/triggered` removes it.

applied_at.description:
When (RFC 3339) and who: `account:<id>` for a console session,
`token` in single mode.

gate.description: The gate the apply set, and the gate before it.

oneOf.description: For the inbox: the measurement the gate was applied from.

source.description:
What the gate was applied from. Absent in a record from before the
field: `inbox`.

WorkflowGateCalibrationReport.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/triggered/calibration`: the gated workflows of the
graph, ordered by starter, then name.

include_batch.description: The unseen batch labels fill the bands (`include_batch=true`).

items_read.description:
Review items read. The read is bounded as the inbox list is: at most
1,000 items.

truncated.description: The graph holds more review items than were read.

WorkflowGateCandidate.description:
One candidate gate below the current gate (0.50, 0.55, …), with the
labels from it up to the current gate and those of its tail.

n.description:
The labels from the candidate up to the current gate, and their
precision with the low end of its 95% Wilson interval.

pass.description: The gate can go down to this candidate.

tail_high.description:
The tail: the labels from the candidate up to 0.1 above it (or the
current gate, when that is lower), and their precision.

why.description: Why it does not pass, in one sentence.

WorkflowGateCandidateOutcome.description: What the rule says about one candidate gate.

WorkflowGateLabels.description: What the labels of a gate are made of.

batch.description:
Labels from the other batch decisions. They fill the bands only with
`include_batch=true`.

batch_seen.description:
Labels from a batch decision on an item the person saw: they fill
the bands.

decided_items.description: Items of the workflow that a person accepted or dismissed.

excluded.description:
Labels left out: the value the gate compared is at or above the
gate now, or the item does not keep it.

open_items.description: Items of the workflow that wait for a person.

single.description: Labels from a decision on one item: they fill the bands.

WorkflowGateMeasurement.description:
The labels of a gate at one time: the bands, the counts and the
proposal. A gate's calibration keeps the one it was applied from.

WorkflowGateProposal.description: A lower gate the labels support.

gate.description:
The proposed gate: the lowest candidate that passes, walking down
from the current gate.

precision.description:
The precision of the labels from the proposed gate to the current
one, with the low end of its 95% Wilson interval and their count.

oneOf.description: The calibration the gate was last applied from, when it was.

bands.description: The display bands, from 0 up: 0 to 0.5, then 0.1 wide up to 1.

candidates.description:
The candidate gates below the current gate (0.50, 0.55, …), from
the highest down: where the gate could go, and why not.

gate.description: The gate now: answers below it go to a person.

no_proposal.description: Why there is no proposal, in one sentence.

oneOf.description:
A lower gate the labels support. A proposal never raises a gate:
the inbox labels no answer at or above it.

starter.description:
The starter workflow's catalog id: `documents.link`, `review` or
`values.extract`.

target_precision.description:
The precision a proposal must reach (`gate.target_precision`, else
0.95).

WorkflowGateSource.description: What a person applied a gate from.

WorkflowInboxMessage.description:
One unfinished turn of an instance's inbox: a message that runs or
waits.

error.description: The error of the last failed attempt.

message_bytes.description: The size of the message, serialized.

oneOf.description: The progress of a running turn that follows the progress convention.

ready_at_ms.description: When a worker may claim it (a queued or waiting turn).

received_at_ms.description: When the inbox admitted the message.

turn.description: The turn number; turns run in this order.

oneOf.description:
A wait that counts no attempt (a failure with `retry_at_ms`, or a
capacity deferral): the turn is ready again at `wait.until_ms`.

WorkflowInboxResponse.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/instances/inbox?id=&after=&limit=&payloads=`: the
unfinished turns of one instance, oldest first, from one read of the
instance object.

newest_received_at_ms.description: When the newest unfinished message was admitted.

next_after.description: The turn number to pass as `after` for the next page.

oldest_received_at_ms.description: When the oldest unfinished message was admitted.

pending_messages.description: Every unfinished turn, on this page or not.

history_pruned_through.description:
Turns `1..=history_pruned_through` were removed by history retention:
reading one answers 404, and a message id whose turn was removed is
admitted again as a new message. Zero when nothing was removed.

history_through.description: Completed history safely copied to immutable object storage and evicted locally.

on_exhausted.description: What a turn that failed for good does: absent while `block`.

oneOf.description:
The progress of the current turn while it runs, when its operation
details follow the progress convention (see `WorkflowProgress`).

turn.description: Required for retry/skip; prevents a repeated command affecting the next turn.

WorkflowInstanceCreateRequest.description: A stable workflow identity. Each message executes one bounded, version-pinned turn.

on_exhausted.description:
What a turn that failed for good does to the inbox: `block` (the
default) keeps it at the inbox head until a person retries or skips
it; `skip` keeps the failed turn in the history and goes on with the
next message. Absent on the wire while `block`.

WorkflowInstanceDeleteRequest.description: Delete a message workflow instance, its turns and its history.

deleted.description:
True when this call deleted a live instance. An id with no instance,
a repeated call, or a call that finishes a delete that another call
began answers false.

WorkflowMessageOrigin.description:
Where a message came from. One origin per message: a message of several
instances holds the union of their fields. Every field but `kind` is
optional, and the whole origin is at most 1 KiB.

The engine stores it with the turn, beside the message. It is no part
of the message's identity: a repeated message id with the same message
answers the first turn and keeps the first origin.

actor.description: Who asked, when a person or a named client did.

attempt.description: How many times the item was sent before (a requeue).

due_at_ms.description:
A `schedule` origin: the slot's time, in milliseconds since the Unix
epoch.

event.description: The event of the data plane that sent it.

fields.description: The fields (predicate IRIs or names) whose change caused it.

from_seq.description: The first commit of the range that caused it.

media_type.description:
A `content` origin: the media type the upload named
(`application/pdf`).

message_id.description: A continuation: the message id of the turn that continued.

note.description: A short note, at most 280 characters.

ontology_version.description:
A `schema_changed` origin: the ontology version whose change of the
watched class started the pass.

requests.description: The request ids of the commits that caused it.

revision.description:
The settings revision of the named workflow whose watch sent the
message (`wrev_…`): its settings when the watch wrote it. A
continuation keeps its turn's.

sha256.description: A `content` origin: the SHA-256 of the content, lowercase hex.

target_seq.description: The commit a pass over a class reads up to.

to_seq.description: The last commit of the range that caused it.

turn.description: A continuation: the turn that continued.

uploaded_at_ms.description:
A `content` origin: when the upload was logged, in milliseconds since
the Unix epoch (the writing node's clock).

id.description:
Caller-assigned idempotency key. A repeated id answers the turn it
admitted while that turn is in the retained history (by default the
newest 256 turns, and every turn that finished in the last 24 hours).

oneOf.description:
Where the message came from, at most 1 KiB
(`WorkflowMessageOrigin`). Stored with the turn, and shown by the
inbox and turn views. No part of the message's identity.

WorkflowOnExhausted.description:
What a turn does after its last attempt failed
(`WorkflowInstanceCreateRequest::on_exhausted`).

WorkflowOwns.description:
The outputs a workflow owns: the classes whose instances it creates, and
the relations and properties it writes on the instances it watches. A
rerun replaces them, and they never wake the workflow itself.

WorkflowProgress.description:
What a running step of a message workflow does now, read from its
operation progress details. The same shape as the Running line of a
triggered workflow (`TriggeredWorkflowRunning`), with a free `unit`.

heartbeat_at.description: When the worker last reported progress (RFC 3339).

phase.description: What the step does now, in plain words: `reading pages`.

total.description: Absent when the step does not know it.

unit.description:
What `done` and `total` count: one of the `ActivityUnit` words
(`documents`, `pages`, `mentions`, `links`, `proposals`,
`instances`, `questions`, `messages`, `items`) or another short word.

WorkflowQueueInFlight.description: A message a watch wrote down and sends next.

WorkflowQueueItem.description: One item a watch has not sent yet.

origin.description:
Where it came from. An item queued before origins were kept shows
the origin its reason gives.

removed.description: The instance left the class: it goes in a message's `removed`.

WorkflowQueuePass.description: A pass over the class that has not reached its end.

cursor.description: The last instance queued, in IRI order.

target_seq.description: The published commit the pass reads at.

WorkflowQueueShard.description:
One shard in the queue view: what the watch holds for it and the head
of its inbox.

messages.description:
The first unfinished turns, oldest first, with their origins (at
most 10; `GET /v1/workflows/instances/inbox` pages the rest).

oneOf.description: The progress of its running turn.

WorkflowRequeueItem.description: One item a turn could not do (`POST /v1/workflows/named/requeue`).

error.description:
Why it failed, at most 1,000 characters. The first error is the
requeue origin's note.

instance.description: The instance IRI, as the message named it.

WorkflowRequeueRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/named/requeue?name=`: the instances a turn of a
shard could not do go back into the watch's queue, to be sent again
later with origin `requeue` (dogfooding design §3.3 G7). Record the
failure in the turn's result and counters, ask for the requeue, and
complete the turn: the shard goes on with its next message.

turn.description:
The turn that asks. Its message's origin gives the attempt: one more
than a requeue message's `attempt`, else 1.

workflow_id.description: The shard whose turn asks: `starter.<name>` or `starter.<name>.<k>`.

attempt.description: The attempt the items are sent with: 1 to 3.

exhausted.description:
The items that failed after 3 requeues: not sent again, counted in
the workflow's `exhausted` counter and named in its `last_error`.

not_before.description:
When they are sent at the earliest (RFC 3339): one minute after the
first failure, four after the second, sixteen after the third.

requeued.description: The items queued again, back on the asking shard.

WorkflowReviewTrigger.description:
A review trigger: the answers to the review items a workflow asked
(`POST /v1/reviews` with `workflow.name`, or origin `starter:<name>`)
arrive as messages of type `review.answered` ([`ReviewAnsweredMessage`]),
one per answer. It goes beside the workflow's watch or content trigger.

workflow.description: The workflow whose items' answers arrive. Absent: this workflow.

WorkflowRevision.description:
One revision of a workflow's settings, with the facts of one
activation (`GET /v1/workflows/named/revisions`: the activation of the
item; `…/revisions/get`: the newest kept activation of the revision,
none when the history keeps none).

activated_by.description:
The key (`key:<id>`) or the account (`account:<id>`) that asked;
absent for an `existing` activation.

activation.description: The activation's number in the workflow's history.

available.description:
The settings are kept and read: `false` for a history row whose
revision was deleted (it raced a collection), which has no
`target`, `settings` or `request`.

bound.description: The workflow's binding names this revision now.

created.description: When the revision was first written (RFC 3339).

id.description: `wrev_` and 32 hex characters: the hash of `settings`.

oneOf.description:
What the workflow's tests read with these settings (added
2026-10-27). Three states. An object: the newest test that read
inputs with this revision. `null`: no test is recorded for these
settings; a test that ran on an older node or before this field
existed is not recorded, so `null` does not prove that none ran.
Absent: the starter has no tests (only `values.extract` has them),
the server has no such record, or the record did not read; read it as
unknown.

settings.description:
The settings a person set, as the hash covers them: the template,
the trigger, `params`, `gate`, the owned outputs, the budget and,
for a workflow of your worker, its batch and routing. `null` when
not `available`.

source.description: `calibration` for a gate applied from its measurement.

starter.description:
The starter workflow it was made from (`workflow`, `values.extract`,
…).

oneOf.description: The workflow type and version that receive the work.

WorkflowRevisionAction.description: How an activation moved the binding.

WorkflowRevisionActivateRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/named/revisions/activate`: make a kept revision the
workflow's settings.

expected_revision.description:
The revision the caller read as bound: another one answers `409
workflow_revision_conflict`.

experiment.description:
An experiment whose B this activation applies (`exp_…`, added
2026-10-26): its revision change on this workflow. The activation
checks that the workflow still runs the experiment's A (409
`experiment_outdated`); when B's revision is bound already, it
changes nothing.

id.description: The revision to activate.

name.description: The workflow's name.

WorkflowRevisionList.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/named/revisions?name=&cursor=&limit=`: the history,
newest activation first, in the list envelope.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page (an activation number); absent on
the last page.

WorkflowRevisionRequest.description:
The request a revision resolves from: the body of the `PUT` route that
makes it (`route` `named` for `PUT /v1/workflows/named`, `triggered`
for `PUT /v1/workflows/triggered`). An activation sends it again.

WorkflowRevisionTested.description:
The newest test that read inputs with a revision's settings: the fact,
with no verdict. The test (`GET /v1/workflows/named/tests/get?id=`) is the
record; the counts are those of the moment it ended.

oneOf.description:
The experiment the test is an arm of (added 2026-10-27): its id and
the arm, `a` or `b`. Absent for a test a person started.

WorkflowRevisionTestedCounts.description:
What a workflow test read, by the checks of the live workflow: the names
of `WorkflowTestCounts` without `answered`, which goes stale when a
person answers later.

failed.description: Values a check dropped, and inputs the model did not answer.

no_value.description: Properties of a read input with no value.

passed.description: Values at or above the gate, which the workflow writes.

WorkflowRunDetail.description: One run with its model calls, in time order.

calls.description: At most 1,000. `GET /v1/models/calls/get` reads one call whole.

calls_truncated.description:
The run made more calls than `calls` holds, or the call log was read
only in part.

WorkflowRunHour.description:
One hour of a workflow's runs, each counted in the hour it started.
`queue_max` is the largest queue a run of the hour saw, `queue_last` the
queue after the hour's last run.

hour_start_ms.description: The hour's start, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

units.description: What the runs finished, in the workflow's unit.

WorkflowRunInput.description:
One input as a run records it: its IRI and label, what the run did with
it, and its values in the shape of a test's (`WorkflowTestValue`).

cost_micro_usd.description:
The model cost of this input, in millionths of a US dollar, when the
calls named it.
