error.description:
Why the input failed or has no values (the instance is gone), at
most 500 characters.

iri.description:
The input. Absent for a worker's write that names its subject by
type and name only.

label.description: The input's label, or the subject's name.

oneOf.description: The input's page box, when it was read from a file.

values.description:
What the run read or wrote, at most 32: a value with its quote,
support, conversion (`stated`) and outcome; a value filed for review
names its `review_item`.

WorkflowRunList.description:
A page of a workflow's runs, newest first, in the list envelope. A
request with `Lbb-Version` before 2026-10-21 gets the earlier shape:
`runs` and `next_before` in place of `object`, `data`, `has_more` and
`next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

repaired.description:
Summaries this read wrote again from the engine's history (the
first page only).

WorkflowRunPhase.description:
One phase of a run: each new `phase` value of the run's progress starts
one (`reading pages`, `asking the decision model`, …).

WorkflowRunResult.description:
One result as the list answers it: an input of a run with the run's id
and when the run recorded it.

created.description: When the run recorded it (the run's end), RFC 3339.

id.description: `wrr_` and 24 hex. Opaque.

run.description: The run id, as `…/runs` and `…/runs/get` name it.

WorkflowRunResultCounts.description: The inputs of a run by outcome.

WorkflowRunResultList.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/named/runs/results`: the results of a workflow's
runs, newest run first, each run's inputs in order.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

oneOf.description: With `run`: that run's counts; absent when the run has no results.

WorkflowRunResultOutcome.description:
What a run did with one input. When several hold, the first of
`failed`, `review`, `written`, `duplicate`, `no_value` is the input's.

WorkflowRunResultRunCounts.description:
The counts of the run a list names (`run`): every input by outcome, and
how many the run had.

listed.description: The inputs the run kept a result for (at most 200).

WorkflowRunResults.description:
The results of one run as they are stored: one object per run, beside
its summary, written once.

counts.description: Every input of the run by outcome.

inputs.description: The inputs of the run; `data` holds the first 200.

recorded_at_ms.description: When the run recorded them, Unix milliseconds: the run's end.

run.description: The run id, as the run's summary names it.

workflow.description: The workflow folder of the run.

WorkflowRunResultsReport.description:
What a worker reports with the completion or the failure of a turn:
the inputs of the run, and the counts of every input it handled (also
those past the bound). The SDK fills it from `writeOwned`, `review` and
`requeue`.

oneOf.description: Every input by outcome; absent, the inputs are counted.

inputs.description: At most 200 inputs, in the order the run first named them.

WorkflowRunStats.description:
The last hours of a workflow's runs, oldest first, up to the current
hour. An hour without a run is all zeros.

WorkflowRunSummary.description:
The run summary: the record of one run that a workflow keeps for 30
days.

attempts.description: The attempt the run was (1 for the first).

error.description: Why it failed, at most 500 characters; `null` otherwise.

fingerprint.description:
A hash of what an LBB-run workflow ran with (added 2026-10-20): its
starter and version, settings, gate and watch, the units of its
properties, its models and its system prompt. A workflow test
carries the same hash (`WorkflowTest::fingerprint`), so a run and a
test with one fingerprint ran the same workflow. Absent for engine
runs.

id.description:
`<started_at_ms:013>-<identity>-<turn>` for an engine run: sortable
by time. Selected source lifetimes append `~<64-hex-incarnation>`;
use the exact ID returned by the claimed task. A step of the Rust path keeps its own id,
`<started_at_ms:013>-<node>-<seq:06>`.

identity.description: The engine identity (`starter.<name>` for a step of the Rust path).

oneOf.description:
Where the turn's message came from; `null` when its sender named
none.

phases.description: The phases of its progress, oldest first, at most 32.

queue_after.description: What waited after it, counted the same way.

queue_before.description:
What waited when the run began. An engine run counts the identity's
unfinished turns at the claim, its own included; a step of the Rust
path the instances waiting after its own follow step.

revision.description:
The settings revision the run ran on (`wrev_…`, added 2026-10-21):
for a step of the Rust path the settings it read first, for an
engine run the revision its message was sent with (its origin's
`revision`). Absent for an identity of no named workflow and for a
message without one. A summary keeps it after the revision is
collected.

sample.description:
At most 20 names of what the run processed: the turn result's
`sample` (a list of text); for the document workflows of the Rust
path the documents' names, else instance IRIs.

steps.description: The steps the run checkpointed, in order.

turn.description: The turn's number; absent for a step of the Rust path.

units.description: What the run finished, in `unit`: the `done` of its last progress.

usage.description:
The sum of the run's model calls: what the SDK added up from the
activity responses and sent with the completion. The call log stays
the record that bills.

workflow.description:
The folder the run is kept in: the named workflow of the identity,
else `instance:<identity>`.

WorkflowRunUsage.description: What a run's model calls used, added up.

cost_micro_usd.description: In millionths of a US dollar.

errors.description: Calls that failed or gave no usable answer.

WorkflowScheduleMessage.description:
The message of one schedule slot (`type: "schedule"`): the slot's time,
the slots skipped since the last run, and the commit range since the
last run.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
The graph's published commit when the slot was sent: read at this
commit or later.

changed.description:
Whether a commit was published since the previous run
(`since_commit_seq < as_of_commit_seq`).

due_at.description:
The slot's time (RFC 3339, UTC); for a run now, the time it was
asked.

manual.description: A run now (`POST /v1/workflows/named/run`), outside the slots.

missed.description: Slots skipped since the previous run.

oneOf.description: Where the message came from; the engine keeps it with the turn.

previous_due_at.description: The time of the previous run's slot; absent for the first run.

since_commit_seq.description:
The previous run's `as_of_commit_seq` (the first run: the published
commit when the trigger was made). The changes since the previous
run are the commits after it, up to `as_of_commit_seq`.

WorkflowScheduleResolved.description:
A schedule trigger as the server resolved it: the stored form (a cron
expression names its `timezone`) and where its slots stand.

last_due_at.description: The time of the last slot sent or skipped.

missed.description:
Slots skipped since the last run (a run that had not finished, the
budget, a downtime); the next run's `missed`.

next_due_at.description:
The next slot's time, RFC 3339 (absent while the workflow is
paused).

WorkflowScheduleTrigger.description:
A schedule trigger: a `cron` expression in a `timezone`, or a period
(`every`, with an `offset`) in UTC, and an optional `jitter`. Exactly one
of `cron` and `every`. Slots come at least 5 minutes apart.

cron.description:
Five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week): `*`,
lists, ranges, steps, month and day names, Sunday as 0 or 7. As in
Vixie cron and cronie, when either day field starts with `*` a day
matches both; otherwise it matches either.
`@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly`, `@monthly` and `@yearly` too.

every.description:
A period of whole minutes (`5m`, `6h`, `7d`), 5 minutes to 366 days:
slots at `offset + k * every` since the Unix epoch, in UTC.

jitter.description:
Each slot is sent a fixed delay after its time, below this: at most 1
hour and half the shortest gap between slots. The message keeps the
slot's time.

offset.description: With `every`: whole minutes from 0 to less than `every`. Default 0.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name for `cron` (`Europe/Berlin`). Default `UTC`.

WorkflowScopeResponse.description:
Current graph incarnation and the durable write model it owns. The epoch
is a decimal string so clients preserve the entire u64 identity.

id.description: Stable caller-chosen idempotency key. Reusing it with different input is a conflict.

active_runs.description: Running activity-graph runs plus message workflows that are not idle.

archived_sequence.description: Equal to `local_sequence`: no change waits outside object storage.

durability.description:
`object_storage` when enabled: an acknowledged request is an object
write. `disabled` when the server has workflows turned off.

local_sequence.description: The generation of the scheduling index of this graph.

name.description: Activity name, or signal name for a signal step.

WorkflowStreamResolved.description:
A stream trigger as the server resolved it: its wait and where its
events stand.

backlog.description: Events received and not yet sent.

dedupe_since.description:
How far back the dedupe window reaches (RFC 3339): an id received
since then is dropped when it comes again.

duplicates.description: Events dropped as repeats of an id.

received.description: Events the stream took (repeats not counted).

WorkflowStreamTrigger.description:
A stream trigger: the events a client sends to the workflow
(`POST /v1/workflows/named/events`), in batches of the workflow's `batch`
events, or fewer once the first event waited `max_wait`.

max_wait.description:
How long the first event of a partial batch waits: `1s` to `15m`.
Default `10s`.

effect_id.description: Stable across retries. Pass this to downstream services that support idempotency.

WorkflowTest.description:
A test of a workflow on chosen inputs. `get` returns it whole; a list
leaves out the inputs' texts and the results.

cost_micro_usd.description: What its model calls cost so far.

dataset.description:
The id of the Evals dataset saved from the test's answers
(`POST /v1/evals/datasets` with `source: {kind: "test", id}`); `null`
until the first save. A test has one dataset: a later save brings it
up to date with the answers.

error.description: Why it failed, at most 500 characters.

estimate_micro_usd.description:
What the start estimated the test to cost, in millionths of a US
dollar.

oneOf.description:
The experiment this test is an arm of (added 2026-10-26): its id and
the arm, `a` or `b`. Absent for a test a person started. An arm's
inputs are the experiment's dataset items, each named
`urn:lbb:item:<dataset>:<hash of the item's name>`.

fingerprint.description:
A hash of the settings, the units of the properties, the models and
the system prompt. A test and a run (`WorkflowRunSummary`) with the
same fingerprint ran the same workflow.

id.description: `wtest_` and an opaque suffix.

installed.description:
The workflow exists on the graph; `false` for a test of a create
request.

models.description:
The model of each use with its provider and effort (added
2026-10-22): the one the create named (`models`), else the one the
workflow's model choices give it (`GET /v1/models/choices`). Fixed
at the start: every call of the test runs it.

results.description: One result per read input, in input order.

revision.description:
The settings revision the test ran on (`wrev_…`, added 2026-10-21):
the one it named (`revision` of the create), else the workflow's.
Absent for a test of a create request. A run summary with the same
revision ran on the same settings.

uses.description:
The model of each use: `extract` (the reasoning model reads values)
and `decide` (the decision model scores their support).

WorkflowTestAnswerRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/named/tests/answer`: a person's answer to one
property of one read input; `answer: null` removes it.

WorkflowTestCounts.description: The values of a test by what the live workflow would do with them.

failed.description: Values a check dropped, and inputs the model did not answer.

no_value.description: Properties of a read input with no value.

passed.description:
Values at or above the gate, which the workflow writes: checks
passed.

WorkflowTestCreateRequest.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/named/tests`: run a workflow on chosen inputs. Name
a workflow of the graph (`name`), or a workflow to create (`install`,
the body that creates it from its template); and the inputs (`iris`, at
most 20), or a sample of the watched class's first instances (`sample`,
1 to 20, default 6).

oneOf.description:
The models to run the test on, per use, in place of the ones the
workflow's model choices give it: a model of the use's `options`
(`GET /v1/models/choices`), with an effort it takes. The test writes
nothing, so a model is tried on the workflow's inputs before it is
chosen. `400 model_choice_unsupported`, `409 model_choice_unavailable`
as for a choice.

name.description: The name of a workflow of the graph (`GET /v1/workflows/named`).

revision.description:
With `name`: a kept revision of the workflow's settings
(`GET /v1/workflows/named/revisions`) to run on instead of the one
in use, so two revisions compare on the same inputs without either
being activated. `404 workflow_revision_not_found` for one the
workflow does not keep.

oneOf.description:
Deprecated: the workflow by its template and name, as the Python SDK
0.29.0 sends it; read as `name`. Send `name`.

WorkflowTestExperiment.description: The experiment a test is an arm of.

WorkflowTestInput.description: One input of a test: an instance of the watched class.

label.description: The instance's label; empty until the input is read.

text.description:
The text the workflow read, at most 40,000 characters; empty until
the input is read. A list of tests leaves it out.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page.

WorkflowTestModels.description: The models a test names for its run (`models` of the create), per use.

oneOf.description: The decision model that scores their support.
The reasoning model that reads values.

WorkflowTestProperty.description:
One property a `values.extract` test reads: its name, value type and,
for a number, the unit the property holds.

WorkflowTestRegion.description: The page box of an instance read from a file: where its values are.

WorkflowTestResult.description: What a test read from one input.

answers.description:
A person's answer per property (`value` items of Review): to the
value the workflow read, or, for a property without one, the value
the text states (`correct`) or that it states none (`accept`).

cost_micro_usd.description: The model cost of this input, in millionths of a US dollar.

error.description:
Why the input has no values: the instance is gone, or its text is
empty.

failed.description: The model gave no usable answer.

oneOf.description: The page box of the instance, when it was read from a file.

WorkflowTestSettings.description: The settings a test runs with, frozen when it starts.

fields.description: The watched fields whose text the workflow reads.

gate.description: The gate: a value with this support or more is written.

repair.description:
The workflow's `repair` setting, frozen with the rest: how many
times the reading of an input may be retried with the failed checks
(0 or 1). Absent for a test of a workflow that does not repair, and
for a test from before the setting.

WorkflowTestStatus.description:
Where a test stands. `queued` → `running` → `done`, `failed` or
`cancelled`; the last three are final.

WorkflowTestValue.description:
One value the workflow read from an input, after every check, as the live
workflow would decide it. A live run records its values in this shape too
(`WorkflowRunInput`), with two more outcomes: `answered` (a person's
answer in force was written) and `rejected` (a person rejected the value,
or the graph refused it, so it was not written again).

attempt.description:
The attempt that read the value: `2` for a value of the repair
attempt (`repair` setting), absent for the first. A value of the
first attempt that failed a check stays in the list beside the
repair's.

outcome.description:
What the live workflow would do: `written` (at or above the gate),
`review` (a review item), `weak_support` (dropped below 0.5),
`quote_not_found`, `invalid_value`, `unknown_property` or
`duplicate`.

quote.description: The words of the text the model quoted.

oneOf.description: The quote's page box, when it differs from the input's.

review_item.description:
The review item a live run filed for the value (`rev_…`); a test
files none.

source.description:
Where the quote is: the evidence's `Document` IRI with its place
(`#page=3`, `#row=5`), or a name.

stated.description:
The number and unit as the text states them (`600 mm`), when they
were converted to the property's unit.

support.description: How well the quote supports the value, 0 to 1.

unconfirmed.description: Why the unit is not confirmed: such a value goes to review at most.

value.description:
The value as the workflow writes it (a number in the property's
unit).

WorkflowTestWorkflow.description:
The workflow a test runs: a starter workflow's catalog id and the
workflow's name.

name.description:
The triggered workflow's name; for a workflow not created yet, the
name its create would give.

WorkflowTrigger.description:
One trigger of a workflow: a watch, a content trigger, a schedule or a
stream, exactly one of them, and at most one review trigger beside it.

oneOf.description:
The uploads of some media types. A content trigger's id defaults to
`content`.

id.description:
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}`. Default `watch`. Each message's origin
names it.

oneOf.description: The answers to review items, in a trigger of its own (id `review`).

One run per slot of a timer: a cron expression in a time zone, or a
period in UTC. A schedule trigger's id defaults to `schedule`.

The events a client sends (`POST /v1/workflows/named/events`), run in
batches. A stream trigger's id defaults to `stream`.

The class (with its subclasses) and the fields whose change marks an
instance; no fields watch every field. `exclude` does not apply.

WorkflowTriggerInFlight.description:
A trigger message a developer workflow wrote down before it sent it: the
next run sends it again unchanged until the send succeeds.

WorkflowTriggerMessage.description:
The trigger message a developer workflow receives (`workflow@v1`). Its
id is `starter-<name>-<n>`; the same id always carries the same message.

as_of_commit_seq.description:
The published commit the workflow had read through when it built the
message. Read the instances at this commit or later.

instances.description: Instance IRIs to read and work on.

oneOf.description:
Where the message came from: the trigger, and a backfill, a commit
range with the watched fields that changed and the request ids of
its commits, a run now or a schema change. The engine keeps the same
origin with the turn. Absent on a message written before origins.

removed.description:
Instance IRIs that left the watched class: drop what was written for
them.

workflow.description:
The triggered workflow's name. Read as `starter` too: a message
stored before the field was renamed still reads.

WorkflowTriggerReason.description: Why a developer workflow receives instances.

WorkflowTriggerResolved.description:
A trigger as the server resolved it: a watch, a content trigger, a
schedule, a stream or a review trigger.

oneOf.description: The media types of a content trigger, lowercase.
The workflow whose answers a review trigger takes.
A schedule as stored, and its next and last slot.
A stream: its wait and where its events stand.
The class and fields of a watch.

Where the message came from: the origin its sender gave, or
`continuation` with the turn that continued.

The operation's progress as the progress convention reads it. Views
fill it; a stored turn never holds it.

The run of the turn's current attempt: its run summary's id, start,
phases and end. The engine sets it at the claim and keeps it with
the turn; a turn that never ran has none.

A wait that counts no attempt: the last failure asked for it with
`retry_at_ms`, or the server deferred the turn for capacity
(`WorkflowTurnWait::reason`). The next claim clears it.

delay_ms.description: Required for a sleep checkpoint, absent for an ordinary step.

include_execution_credential.description:
Request a short-lived SELECT/ASK execution credential for the claimed
turn. Disabled servers refuse this opt-in before changing a claim.
Ordinary workflow control and SDK defaults remain unchanged.

oneOf.description: Atomically enqueue a new turn at the inbox tail with the new saved state.

What the run did with each input (`WorkflowRunResultsReport`): the
SDK fills it from `writeOwned`, `review` and `requeue` when the claim
named `results_max`. Read leniently: an input that does not decode
is left out, and the completion never fails for its results. No part
of the completion's identity.

What the turn's model calls used, added up from the activity
responses (the TypeScript SDK sends it). It goes into the turn's run
summary and is no part of the completion's identity: a repeat with
other usage is the same completion.

What the attempt did with each input before it failed, as on a
completion.

retry_at_ms.description:
Wait until this time (Unix milliseconds, at most 366 days ahead) and
count no attempt: for a cause outside the turn, such as a spent budget
(`retry_at` of `429 workflow_budget_exceeded`) or a dependency that is
not there yet. A time less than a second ahead waits one second
(`WORKFLOW_MIN_WAIT_MS`). A resume or a wake of the instance moves the
time to now. Not with `non_retryable`.

oneOf.description: What the attempt's model calls used, as on a completion.

WorkflowTurnOperation.description: Worker lease renewal never extends these operation/progress deadlines.

sequence.description: Increasing per operation attempt; exact retries do not extend a deadline.

WorkflowTurnRun.description:
What the engine keeps on a turn for its run summary while the turn
runs. Stored with the turn; the claim of a new attempt starts it again.

ended_at_ms.description: When the attempt ended: completed, failed, cancelled or expired.

id.description:
The run summary's id: `<started_at_ms:013>-<identity>-<turn>`, with
`~<64-hex-incarnation>` for a selected source lifetime. Activity calls
use this exact value in `workflow.run_id`.

phases.description: The phases of the attempt's progress, oldest first, at most 32.

queue_after.description: The identity's unfinished turns after it ended.

queue_before.description: The identity's unfinished turns at the claim, this one included.

oneOf.description: The usage the completion (or the failure) reported.

WorkflowTurnSignal.description: Signals target one turn, so a delayed approval cannot affect its successor.

effect_prefix.description: Stable across attempt retries and recovery; SDK appends the named step key.

oneOf.description:
Present only for an explicit supported execution opt-in. The engine
itself leaves this absent; the authenticated server issues it.

results_max.description:
The inputs a completion or a failure may report results for
(`results`, at most this many kept whole). Set by a server that takes
results; a worker sends `results` only when it is present.

WorkflowTurnWait.description:
A wait of a turn that counts no attempt (`WorkflowTurn::wait`). Two
causes make one: a worker's failure with `retry_at_ms` (a spent budget, a
missing dependency), and the server's deferral of a turn for capacity.
The turn is ready again at `until_ms`. A resume or a wake of the
instance moves the time to now, and the next claim clears the wait. A
step's own sleep or signal wait is not one.

reason.description:
Why the turn waits: `retry` (the default, absent on the wire) or
`capacity`.

until_ms.description: When the turn is ready again.

WorkflowTurnWaitReason.description: Why a turn waits without counting an attempt (`WorkflowTurnWait`).

WorkflowTypeInboxEntry.description: One instance in the inbox of a workflow type.

oneOf.description: Its inbox head: the turn that runs, or runs next. No payload.

oldest_received_at_ms.description: When its oldest unfinished message was admitted.

WorkflowTypeInboxResponse.description:
`GET /v1/workflows/inbox?workflow_type=&version=&after=&limit=`: the
instances of a type with unfinished turns, by id. The namespace index
names them; each listed instance is one read.

identities.description:
Instances of the type (and version) in the namespace index, idle
ones included. The index lags a write of another node by at most
its poll interval.

next_after.description: The instance id to pass as `after` for the next page.

with_messages.description: Of them, the instances the index lists with an unfinished turn.

WorkflowTypeRef.description: The workflow type a developer workflow sends its trigger messages to.

WorkflowWatch.description:
The class a workflow watches, and the fields whose change marks an
instance dirty. `fields` takes the `from` path syntax of embeddings.

class.description: The class IRI (or a local name or prefixed name the ontology knows).

exclude.description: Names or IRIs to drop from an automatic choice of fields.

fields.description:
The fields, in the path syntax of embeddings. Absent or empty: the
workflow's own default (an embedding or a fit source picks the text
facts of a sample of the class).

WorkflowWatchResolved.description: A watch as the server resolved it.

WorkflowWatchRule.description: Whether a request that creates a workflow names the watch.

bearer.description: Stack API key (lbb_sk_test_… / lbb_sk_live_…) or single-mode token

info.description: Object-storage-native temporal graph and hybrid search engine. Public data-plane integrations use `/v1/*`, scoped by `?graph=` (default `main`) and authenticated with an environment API key (`lbb_sk_test_…` or `lbb_sk_live_…`) or single-mode token as a bearer. Send `Lbb-Version: 2026-10-21` to pin this contract. Lists use one envelope, `{object: "list", data, has_more, next_cursor}`, with `limit` and `cursor`; a request that sends an earlier `Lbb-Version` gets the shapes it was written for on the workflow lists.

error.message: Usage reporting admission is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.
The request ran, but its usage reporting handoff is unconfirmed. Check the operation state before retrying; repeating it may execute and charge again.

503.description: Service unavailable. On metered routes, application_usage_unavailable refuses admission before execution and is retryable. On writes, application_usage_handoff_unconfirmed means execution ran but its measurement was not durably confirmed: retryable is false and clients must inspect operation state before retrying. A saved measurement preserves success even if settlement needs recovery. Completed public reads preserve their response and hand reporting to a bounded background task; an unconfirmed handoff remains an explicit reporting gap. An original rejected request keeps its original status if its NoCharge acknowledgement fails.

error.message: Usage reporting admission is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.
The request ran, but its usage reporting handoff is unconfirmed. Check the operation state before retrying; repeating it may execute and charge again.

503.description: Service unavailable. On metered routes, application_usage_unavailable refuses admission before execution and is retryable. On writes, application_usage_handoff_unconfirmed means execution ran but its measurement was not durably confirmed: retryable is false and clients must inspect operation state before retrying. A saved measurement preserves success even if settlement needs recovery. Completed public reads preserve their response and hand reporting to a bounded background task; an unconfirmed handoff remains an explicit reporting gap. An original rejected request keeps its original status if its NoCharge acknowledgement fails.

Legacy `replace_owned` replaces a writer's owned edges and fields on its subjects in the same commit. post.summary: Start a calibration session of a choice job. `route` and `fit` measure their own threshold; `resolve`, `infer` and `map` measure the gate of the workflow named in `workflow` (a `documents.link`, a `values.extract`, or the `review` that gates the proposals of `documents.map`), from the gate decisions the workflow noted on its logged calls, above the gate as well as below it. The job's units of the last `since_days` days are sampled by confidence band ([0, 0.5), [0.5, 0.8), [0.8, 0.9), [0.9, 1]) with the disputed units added (at most 120), the sampled calls the checker has not checked are judged against the session's own budget, and one yes or no question is written per judged unit: is the judge right? Answers the queued session. 400 `invalid_calibration_request` for another job, a missing or extra `workflow`, or an option out of range; 404 for an unknown workflow; 409 `calibration_running` while another session of the graph and job (and workflow) is queued or running

503.description: Service unavailable. On metered routes, application_usage_unavailable refuses admission before execution and is retryable. On writes, application_usage_handoff_unconfirmed means execution ran but its measurement was not durably confirmed: retryable is false and clients must inspect operation state before retrying. A saved measurement preserves success even if settlement needs recovery. Completed public reads preserve their response and hand reporting to a bounded background task; an unconfirmed handoff remains an explicit reporting gap. error.message: Usage reporting admission is temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.
The request ran, but its usage reporting handoff is unconfirmed. Check the operation state before retrying; repeating it may execute and charge again.

503.description: Service unavailable. On metered routes, application_usage_unavailable refuses admission before execution and is retryable. On writes, application_usage_handoff_unconfirmed means execution ran but its measurement was not durably confirmed: retryable is false and clients must inspect operation state before retrying. A saved measurement preserves success even if settlement needs recovery. Completed public reads preserve their response and hand reporting to a bounded background task; an unconfirmed handoff remains an explicit reporting gap. An original rejected request keeps its original status if its NoCharge acknowledgement fails.

schema.description: Server-sent events, sent when the request has `Accept: text/event-stream`. post.summary: Answer a question about the graph. The router model picks the kind of question (lookup, aggregate, search, history, schema, unanswerable); the rewriter model runs a bounded loop of tool calls (queries, name lookups, the description, the commit of a date, a comparison of two points), reads the rows, and answers in plain words with citations and the query whose rows hold the answer. `mode: "route"` returns the route alone, with no rewriter call. With `Accept: text/event-stream` the answer is a stream of progress events (`QueryRewriteEvent`) that ends with `done` (the same response) or `error`. Replaces `POST /v1/query/rewrite`, removed on 2026-10-05

post.summary: Record a derivation once: the key, the run that made it (`run_id`, optional) and what it made (`outputs`, at most 16 KiB of JSON). A second record of the same key answers the stored one with `recorded: false`. With `content_uploaded_at` (the upload the check answered), the record writes only while that upload is the file's live one. When the file was deleted since, or deleted and uploaded again, nothing is written: 409 `derivation_upload_changed`, and the run of the current upload does the work. Only LBB's own worker records LBB's `lbb.*` types (403 `reserved_workflow_type`); a work token records nothing else (403 `worker_credential_scope`). 400 `derivation_invalid`

put.summary: Create or change a workflow of your worker with one trigger. A watch sends the class's new, changed and removed instances as messages to `shards` engine identities (1 to 16, default 1), routed by `route_by` (a field; default the instance IRI) so the changes of one key stay in order, at most `window` messages queued per shard (1 to 128, default 4). A content trigger (`content.media_types`) sends each upload of those media types as it is logged, without a wait for a publication: one content per message, routed by its SHA-256, with origin `content`. A schedule (`schedule`: a cron expression in a time zone, or `every` with an `offset` in UTC, at least 5 minutes apart) sends one message per slot to one identity, with the published commit and whether the graph changed since the last slot. A stream (`stream`) takes the events a client sends to `POST /v1/workflows/named/events` and sends them in batches of up to `batch` events (default 100) or after `max_wait` (default 10s), routed by each event's `key`; its `shards` stay as made. Each message names its origin. The same request again is a no-op; a workflow keeps its trigger's kind. 400 `workflow_trigger_unsupported` for more than one trigger; 400 `workflow_param_invalid` for an `lbb.*` target; 409 `workflow_shards_busy` for a change of `shards` or `route_by` while a shard's inbox holds messages; 409 `workflow_cycle`, `workflow_owns_conflict`; 503 `workflows_disabled`. The PUT replaces the whole workflow, so a repeat with the same body changes nothing: it needs no `Idempotency-Key`

Record the failure in the turn's result, ask for the requeue, and complete the turn. A repeat from the same turn queues nothing again (the items wait with this attempt already); past 3 attempts a repeat counts the same items in `exhausted` again. It takes no `Idempotency-Key`
